KOS-NYAYA-016: deficiency (nyuna) and redundancy (adhika) and tenet-deviation are distinct failure modes, mapped to a missing governing assumption in an ADR, duplicated authority across three locations, and an implementation violating an accepted principle respectively -- 'argument and architecture failures can be classified structurally rather than merely labeled wrong.'

b_rows_sample.anchor: KOS-NYAYA-017 ... Criticism must respect the opponent's accepted premises ... strongly reinforces the Williamson extraction about neutral semantic mappings
b_rows_sample.statement: KOS-NYAYA-017 (rated a five-star cross-source convergence): criticism must respect the opponent's accepted premises -- one cannot criticize a Buddhist school for not using the Nyaya five-member syllogism if it recognizes a different structure; applied to evaluating an external bounded context or architecture: do not impose our vocabulary and declare theirs invalid, instead understand its own rules, evaluate internally, map to our model, then compare -- explicitly reinforcing Williamson's neutral-semantic-mapping extraction (S0436).

b_rows_sample.anchor: KOS-NYAYA-018 ... Truth-seeking debate is different from adversarial victory ... KOS-NYAYA-019 ... KOS-NYAYA-020 ... KOS-NYAYA-021 ... Hypothetical adoption
b_rows_sample.statement: KOS-NYAYA-018/019: truth-seeking debate (Question->Clarification->Evidence->Reason->Counterargument->Resolution) is distinguished from victory-oriented debate (fraud/futile-objections/cavilling/wrangling: Goal=win->select evidence->attack opponent->move goalposts->produce rhetoric), suggesting an AI agent needs an explicit epistemic objective (establish_best_supported_claim, not defend_current_proposal) -- recommended for the AI Engineering Platform governance methodology. KOS-NYAYA-020: accepted assumptions should be explicit -- shared/related-school/derived/provisional (hypothetical) premise categories give SharedPremise/LocalPremise/DerivedPremise/HypotheticalPremise. KOS-NYAYA-021: hypothetical adoption is a legitimate reasoning technique -- temporarily accepting an opponent's view without endorsing it, deriving consequences to find contradictions, corresponding to 'architecture counterfactual analysis' (Assume Architecture A->derive consequences->identify contradiction/limitation), proposing HypotheticalArgument{assumed_position, assumption_scope, derived_consequences, contradiction, conclusion}.

b_rows_sample.anchor: KOS-NYAYA-022 ... samavaya — inherence ... KOS-NYAYA-023 ... Relationship types deserve ontological status
b_rows_sample.statement: KOS-NYAYA-022: ontology requires categories AND relations -- Vaisheshika's seven categories (Substance/Quality/Activity/Generality/Particularity/Inherence/Non-existence) are not themselves to be adopted, but the key insight is that an ontology needs both entities and the relations explaining how entities belong together, especially samavaya (inherence, a relation between things that cannot exist separately, substrate/inhere). KOS-NYAYA-023 (rated a five-star ontology research candidate): relationship types deserve ontological status -- software architecture often models entities but leaves relations as unexamined arrows; implements/depends-on/supports/contradicts/realizes/contains/belongs-to/instantiates are not interchangeable, and Nyaya-Vaisesika forces the question 'what kind of relation is this?'

b_rows_sample.anchor: KOS-NYAYA-024 ... KOS-NYAYA-025 ... Generality and particularity must coexist ... Never confuse the class/type/generalization with the concrete knowledge instance.
b_rows_sample.statement: KOS-NYAYA-024: don't collapse 'part-of', 'property-of', and 'relation-to' -- Entity/Property/Activity/Relation must remain distinguishable (Aggregate is not the same type of thing as AggregateState, and neither is depends-on), reinforcing DDD modeling discipline. KOS-NYAYA-025: generality and particularity must coexist (Domain Concept->{general concept, particular instance}), illustrated by ArchitectureDecision vs ADR-T19, or Evidence vs TestRun-2026-08-24-001; candidate principle: 'never confuse the class/type/generalization with the concrete knowledge instance.'

b_rows_sample.anchor: KOS-NYAYA-026 ... abhava — non-existence/negation ... KOS-NYAYA-027 ... Absence is relational
b_rows_sample.statement: KOS-NYAYA-026: non-existence/absence can be knowledge -- later Vaisheshika recognizes abhava (non-existence/negation) as a category with multiple forms and explicit relations to what is absent; 'no evidence found', 'capability absent', 'architecture boundary violated', 'expected artifact missing', 'entity no longer exists' are knowledge about absence, not merely empty values. KOS-NYAYA-027: absence is relational -- non-existence is connected to a positive counterpart and substrate, so 'Missing(X)' is incomplete; proposes AbsenceAssertion{expected_object, observed_scope, expectation_source, observation_time, evidence}, e.g. Missing(ArchitectureDecision) requiring these fields to be a proper knowledge object.

b_rows_sample.anchor: KOS-NYAYA-028 ... KOS-NYAYA-029 ... Ontological simplicity can hide causal complexity ... Do not choose an ontology merely because it is elegant if it cannot represent important real-world causal structures.
b_rows_sample.statement: KOS-NYAYA-028: causality needs explicit structure -- Keith identifies weaknesses in the Nyaya-Vaisesika causal theory's treatment of multiple/complex causes, used as a warning (not an endorsement of their theory) that a simple A->B causal model can fail when reality has interacting causes, requiring distinct necessary-cause/contributing-cause/trigger/enabling-condition/instrument/context relations. KOS-NYAYA-029 (a researcher inference from the author's own criticism, explicitly not a direct Nyaya principle): ontological simplicity can hide causal complexity -- 'do not choose an ontology merely because it is elegant if it cannot represent important real-world causal structures', connecting directly to Williamson's warning that simplicity is not merely minimum entity count.

b_rows_sample.anchor: KOS-NYAYA-030 ... KOS-NYAYA-031 ... Knowledge has a history ... KOS-NYAYA-032 ... A formal system can contain unresolved historical uncertainty
b_rows_sample.statement: KOS-NYAYA-030/031: the system evolved through criticism and synthesis (initial formulations->commentaries->criticism->Buddhist interaction->internal revision->syncretism->later refinement, with aphoristic sutras requiring commentary and functioning partly as mnemonic structures) -- a knowledge system should preserve original claim->interpretation->criticism->revision->current formulation rather than flattening into one canonical truth, proposing KnowledgeObject{current_version, predecessors, successors, interpretations, criticisms, supersession}. KOS-NYAYA-032: a formal system can contain unresolved historical uncertainty -- Keith explicitly warns dates/origins/interpretations are uncertain and absolutely certain results cannot always be achieved, so KnowledgeOS should represent Known/Probable/Contested/Uncertain/Reconstructed/Unknown rather than forcing binary true/false.

b_rows_sample.anchor: KOS-NYAYA-033 ... Provenance matters ... KOS-NYAYA-034 ... A source's authority is itself a knowledge problem ... KOS-NYAYA-035 ... testimony and inference should remain distinct epistemic paths
b_rows_sample.statement: KOS-NYAYA-033: provenance matters -- the same proposition can have different provenance (original text/commentary/later interpretation/historical reconstruction), giving Claim{source, author, historical layer, interpretation, reconstruction status}. KOS-NYAYA-034: a source's authority is itself a knowledge problem -- historical disagreement over whether verbal testimony is an independent means of knowledge or reducible to inference; 'Source says X' must never automatically mean 'X is true', requiring Source->Testimony->Authority evaluation->Knowledge claim, proposing TestimonialEvidence{speaker, statement, authority_basis, reliability, scope, corroboration}. KOS-NYAYA-035: testimony and inference should remain distinct epistemic paths even when they support the same claim (observed X / inferred X / told X by an authority / compared X with Y are not interchangeable justifications).

b_rows_sample.anchor: KOS-NYAYA-036 ... KOS-NYAYA-037 ... A claim can have multiple independent supports ... KOS-NYAYA-038 ... Epistemic relations are not all equivalent
b_rows_sample.statement: KOS-NYAYA-036: epistemic basis should survive representation -- a claim like 'Capability X exists' should preserve whether its basis is an architecture document, source-code inspection, runtime observation, or expert testimony. KOS-NYAYA-037: a claim can have multiple independent supports simultaneously (Claim C supported-by Evidence E1, supported-by Inference I1, corroborated-by Test T1, confirmed-by Observation O1), stronger than a single claim.source field. KOS-NYAYA-038: epistemic relations are not all equivalent -- argues against a generic 'supports' relation, proposing observes/infers/testifies/compares/corroborates/contradicts/invalidates/presupposes/derives/applies as a major candidate for a formal ontology.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Nyaya provides conceptual structures that are highly compatible with disciplined domain modeling ... candidate bounded context: Epistemology
b_rows_sample.statement: A full DDD translation of the extraction (explicitly not claiming 'Nyaya is DDD', only that it 'provides conceptual structures highly compatible with disciplined domain modeling'): candidate bounded context Epistemology with aggregates KnowledgeClaim/Inference/Evidence/Argument/Cognition/Validation/Dispute; value objects EpistemicBasis/ValidityStatus/Scope/Assumption/Counterexample/Provenance; domain events ClaimProposed/EvidenceObserved/InferenceConstructed/ClaimChallenged/CounterexampleFound/ClaimValidated/ClaimInvalidated/ClaimSuperseded; a key insight maps Nyaya's general-relation vs particular-application distinction directly onto Domain invariant -> Concrete aggregate instance (example: 'a determination must be issued only after persistence' -> 'Determination #123 was persisted, therefore DeterminationIssued is valid').

b_rows_sample.anchor: a Nyaya-inspired epistemic checklist ... but adapted to engineering
b_rows_sample.statement: Two applied structures proposed: (1) a Nyaya-inspired ten-question AI-agent investigation checklist (what is the proposition? what is the object under investigation? what is the evidence? what is the epistemic basis? what general relation is relied upon? what assumptions are made? are there contrary cases? can the conclusion be independently reproduced? what logical errors are possible? what would invalidate the conclusion?), replacing a bare 'what is the architecture?' query; (2) an architecture-review artifact structured as Proposition->Reason->General Relation->Evidence{positive cases, negative cases, counterexamples}->Application->Conclusion, judged more rigorous than an ordinary prose ADR.

group_evidence.why_grouped: labels share the notation 'abhava'

a_rows_sample.anchor: LocalCorrectness ⇏ GlobalCorrectness; compositional correctness via interface contracts
a_rows_sample.statement: States that each component C_i satisfying Correct(C_i) does not imply Correct(C_1∘...∘C_n): interactions can introduce failures absent from individual components (LocalCorrectness ⇏ GlobalCorrectness). Worked example: EvidenceContext and DecisionContext both correct, but a wrong translation between them makes Evidence->Decision incorrect despite both bounded contexts being internally correct -- 'exactly why context boundaries and contracts matter'. Formalizes compositional correctness: Correct(C1) ∧ Correct(C2) ∧ Contract(C1,C2) ⇒ Correct(C1∘C2), so the interface contract becomes part of the proof. Represents KOS conceptually as C_identity∘C_semantic∘C_evidence∘C_epistemic∘C_causal∘C_decision∘C_governance∘C_learning (conceptual composition, not one runtime pipeline).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Bounded contexts as proof boundaries; anti-corruption layer as semantic-preserving translation
a_rows_sample.statement: If BC_i guarantees I_i and its interface guarantees Contract_i, another context can rely on Contract_i -- 'this enables compositional reasoning'. Concludes bounded contexts are not merely organizational boxes but Proof boundaries, each owning semantics, invariants, state transitions, and contracts. Formalizes an anti-corruption layer's translation Model_A -> Model_B via Preserve(T,I) (translation T preserves invariant I); example: if Approved in Context A has richer meaning than Approved in Context B, a direct field mapping is invalid and the translation must explicitly encode a SemanticMapping. A ContractViolation must become an explicit state/event, never disappearing silently -- giving the property: invalid input must not silently become valid knowledge.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Twelve falsification experiments for Step 48 global-invariant/correctness model (all PASS)
a_rows_sample.statement: Runs twelve falsification tests, all PASS: (1) a component is locally correct but its interface translation violates semantics => global invariant failure detected; (2) all safety properties hold but a workflow deadlocks => safety passes, liveness fails; (3) evidence is modified without a new version => evidence-integrity violation; (4) a decision uses a model created after the decision date => temporal/historical-integrity violation; (5) an AI proposal bypasses authorization => AI-boundary and authorization invariants fail; (6) a causal claim has no documented assumptions => causal-integrity violation; (7) a trusted claim becomes invalid but remains operational without review => revision/invalidation-invariant violation; (8) a safety-critical unknown is treated as true => unknown-state/safety-invariant violation; (9) a claim valid in one bounded context is applied to another without semantic mapping => scope/semantic-integrity violation; (10) two distributed replicas temporarily disagree where eventual consistency is permitted => no violation if the declared consistency contract allows it; (11) two replicas disagree on a strong-consistency invariant => critical consistency violation; (12) a model is stable and highly confident but external validation shows systematic error => epistemic correctness fails despite model stability.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Cross-context invariants resolved via contracts (Query/Result), never by merging aggregates
a_rows_sample.statement: Example cross-context invariant Execute(Action) ⇒ Authorized(Decision) spans DecisionContext and GovernanceContext; these must not be forced into one aggregate. Instead contexts communicate through a Contract: DecisionContext -> AuthorizationQuery, receiving AuthorizationResult -- this preserves ownership (Governance owns Authorization, Decision owns Decision; neither steals the other's model). Depicts a logical context-map flow Evidence -> Knowledge -> {Causal, and Semantic feeding Decision} -> Decision -> Governance -> Action -> Outcome -> Learning -> back to Knowledge, explicitly 'a logical flow, not necessarily synchronous runtime communication'. Anti-corruption layers ACL_AB translate Model_A -> Model_B preserving the semantic contract; example: Evidence Context's Observation(source,timestamp,value) maps to Knowledge Context's Evidence(proposition,scope,relevance) via SemanticTransformation, not FieldToField mapping.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Formal context composition B_i=(M_i,Γ_i,I_i); Preserve(T_ij,I_required); LocalInvariant+ContractInvariant⇒GlobalInvariant links back to Step 48
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines a context as B_i=(M_i,Gamma_i,I_i) (internal model, published contracts, invariants), a context interaction T_ij: Gamma_i -> M_j required to preserve semantics (Preserve(T_ij,I_required)), and the complete system as KOS = direct-sum_i B_i with explicit contracts Gamma_ij, with the goal LocalInvariant + ContractInvariant ⇒ GlobalInvariant -- explicitly connecting Step 53 back to Step 48's compositional correctness result. Declares STEP 53 -- PASS and states the important result is not merely that communication works but that 'KnowledgeOS boundaries are semantic and contractual, not merely technical'. Opens Step 54 (Mathematical Types -> DDD Domain Types -> Executable Contracts): deriving an actual type system from P={Entity,State,Event,Observation,Proposition,Relation,Policy,Action} down to concrete types (EntityId, Observation, Evidence, Claim, Relation, KnowledgeSnapshot, Policy, Decision, Authorization, Action, Outcome) each with explicit Invariant, Ownership, Lifecycle, Version, Provenance, Contract -- 'the point at which our mathematical architecture can begin to translate directly into the actual KnowledgeOS software design'.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Compositionality hypothesis: I_A ∧ I_B ∧ Contract_AB ⇒ I_AB; CorrectContexts ⇏ CorrectComposition
a_rows_sample.statement: For B_A=(M_A,Gamma_A,I_A) and B_B=(M_B,Gamma_B,I_B) both individually satisfying their invariants, tests whether I_A ∧ I_B ∧ Contract_AB is sufficient for I_AB (LocalCorrectness + CorrectContract ⇒ GlobalCorrectness). Worked example Evidence->Knowledge: I_E (Evidence(E) ⇒ Integrity(E)) and I_K (ValidatedClaim(C) ⇒ Provenance(C)) can each hold while an incorrect EvidenceId_A->ClaimId_B mapping still breaks the global system, giving CorrectContexts ⇏ CorrectComposition -- contract correctness is needed too, requiring an explicit integration invariant I_EK (Claim(C) derived from E ⇒ E is an admissible evidence reference).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Identifiers crossing boundaries need semantic integrity; content-addressable Hash(E) verification against tampering
a_rows_sample.statement: Experiment: valid evidence mapping E1->ACL_EK->C1 with Provenance(C1)=E1 verified -- PASS. Experiment: a deliberately wrong mapping (E1 published but mapped to E2) is detected provided the contract includes identity/integrity verification -- PASS, revealing that identifiers crossing boundaries need semantic integrity. Strengthens external references with content-addressable verification: Reference=(EvidenceId,Version,Hash), consumer checks Hash_received=Hash_expected; a tampered E1 (hash h'!=h) is detected as IntegrityFailure and must not be silently accepted -- PASS.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Mutable-live-reference hazard discovered and corrected: DecisionBasis must be immutable/version-bound (KnowledgeSnapshotRef)
a_rows_sample.statement: Composition Knowledge->Decision requires the global invariant Basis(D)=K_t for the snapshot used to construct D; experiment with a fixed immutable snapshot reference PASSes, but a deliberately mutable live reference to CurrentKnowledge (K1->K2 mutating what D1 sees) produces FAILURE DETECTED -- 'a useful failure... the mathematical architecture itself survives, but a naive implementation would violate it'. Architectural correction: strengthen the contract to KnowledgeSnapshotRef=(SnapshotId,Version,Hash), so a decision stores the reference, never a mutable live knowledge object -- giving the rule DecisionBasis must be immutable or version-bound.

a_rows_sample.anchor: PolicyAtDecision != CurrentPolicy; historical vs current authorization query distinction
a_rows_sample.statement: Composition Decision->Governance requires Authorization(D,P) ⇒ DecisionBasis and PolicyVersion are identifiable. Experiment: D1 created under P1, policy replaced by P2 -- authorization must not silently re-evaluate historical D1 under P2, PASS provided authorization semantics distinguish PolicyAtDecision from CurrentPolicy. Distinguishes two legitimate but different questions: the historical question ('was this decision valid under P1?') versus the current question ('would this decision be authorized under today's policy?') -- Authorize_historical(D,t) != Authorize_current(D).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Authorization TOCTOU race discovered and corrected: Execute(A,t)⇒AuthorizationValid(A,t) with an explicit validity-window contract
a_rows_sample.statement: Composition Governance->Action requires Execute(A) ⇒ ValidAuthorization(A), raising a classic time-of-check/time-of-use problem: authorization checked True at t1, expired by t2, execution at t3 blindly relying on the earlier check violates the global invariant -- FAILURE DETECTED (again 'valuable'). Architectural correction: an Authorization type = (DecisionId, PolicyVersion, Authority, IssuedAt, ExpiresAt, AuthorizationId), execution must verify t_execute in [IssuedAt,ExpiresAt] (potentially revalidating immediately before execution), giving the strengthened invariant Execute(A,t) ⇒ AuthorizationValid(A,t), not merely AuthorizationValid(A,t_check).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Correlation contract needs both WID and ActionId; Learning bypass rejected; multi-agent proposal preservation and optimistic-concurrency conflict
a_rows_sample.statement: Composition Action->Outcome: a deliberate outcome-mixup (O1 associated to A2 instead of A1) is detected if action identity and correlation are validated -- PASS, showing a workflow CorrelationId=WID alone is too coarse and the specific ActionId is also needed. Composition Learning->Knowledge: Learning attempting UpdateClaim(C) directly is Rejected -- PASS, requiring Learning -> Proposal -> Validation -> KnowledgeRevision, never Learning -> DirectMutation. Composition multi-agent: Agent_A and Agent_B both proposing decisions P_A, P_B -- both preserved until a domain process determines the result -- PASS; concurrent modification of the same Decision(D) by both agents is controlled via Version/ConcurrencyToken, e.g. Version(D)=7 read by both, Agent A commits 7->8, Agent B's submission based on 7 yields ConcurrencyConflict -- PASS.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Global epistemic rule: absence of observed information != evidence of absence; closed-world vs open-world must be explicit per context/query
a_rows_sample.statement: Composition eventual consistency: EvidenceRegistered occurred but not yet visible to Knowledge Context; a concurrent Decision query must distinguish NotYetAvailable from DoesNotExist -- PASS, generalized to the global invariant: absence of observed information != evidence of absence, unless the domain explicitly defines closed-world semantics. Distinguishes closed-world (NotFound ⇒ False) from open-world (NotFound ⇒ Unknown) and requires KnowledgeOS to specify which applies per context/query.

a_rows_sample.anchor: No context may infer stronger semantics than its published contract justifies; TemporalOrder ⇏ Causality crosses contexts
a_rows_sample.statement: Composition semantic translation: a naive translator mapping Verified (Evidence Context) to Authorized (Decision Context) is invalid and rejected by the ACL absent an explicit semantic rule -- PASS, giving the global semantic invariant that no context may infer stronger semantics than the published contract justifies, 'one of the most important KnowledgeOS properties'. Composition Evidence->Causal: A precedes B does not automatically produce Causes(A,B) without an explicit causal basis -- PASS, restating TemporalOrder ⇏ Causality as a cross-context invariant.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Circular cross-context dependency detected via a Dependency Graph; feedback loop != deadlock; well-founded progress measure for productive cycles
a_rows_sample.statement: Constructs a circular context dependency (Decision needs Knowledge needs Evidence needs ExternalSource needs Authorization needs Decision) that is globally impossible despite every local rule being correct; detected as a Cycle -- PASS provided dependency analysis runs before workflow activation, revealing the need for an architecture-level Dependency Graph G_D=(Contexts,Dependencies), where cycles are not automatically invalid but workflow-critical cycles must be explicitly justified. Distinguishes FeedbackLoop != Deadlock: an intentional Learning<->Knowledge or Knowledge->Action->Outcome->Learning->Knowledge cycle is acceptable if there is temporal progression (Version_next>Version_current), whereas a nonproductive cycle (K_t->K_t->K_t with no progression) repeated indefinitely is a Liveness Failure. Introduces a well-founded progress measure mu(X) in W (no infinite descending chain, e.g. RemainingSteps in N) with each transition satisfying mu(X_{t+1})<mu(X_t), proving termination for a given workflow; distinguishes FiniteWorkflow from PersistentProcess (learning may continue indefinitely and needs Progress rather than termination, measured e.g. by new evidence, reduced uncertainty, improved model performance, validated knowledge, resolved conflicts).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Global eventual-consistency property under distributed execution; IntegrationState health concept; compositional observability (BlockedBecause)
a_rows_sample.statement: For separate Evidence and Knowledge processes with delayed messages, defines a ConsistencyContract such as Eventually: EvidencePublished -> KnowledgeAvailable, i.e. PublishedFact ⇒ EventuallyVisible under the explicit assumption MessageInfrastructureEventuallyRecovers; if recovery never happens the system must eventually expose IntegrationFailure rather than silently continuing to claim Synchronized. Introduces IntegrationState in {Healthy, Delayed, Degraded, Failed} as valuable operational knowledge, and compositional observability: the system should answer 'which boundary is preventing this workflow from progressing' (e.g. Decision -> WaitingForAuthorization because GovernanceContext=Unavailable) via an explicit BlockedBecause(X) -- 'not merely monitoring... part of the explainability of workflow state'.

a_rows_sample.anchor: EvidenceGraph vs ExecutionGraph: 'why do we believe this' != 'what happened operationally'
a_rows_sample.statement: Gives two complementary explanation chains: Decision -> KnowledgeSnapshot -> Claims -> Evidence (the EvidenceGraph, answering 'why do we believe this') and Decision -> Authorization -> Action -> Outcome (the ExecutionGraph, answering 'what happened operationally') -- 'these graphs must not be merged blindly'; they intersect but are not identical.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Compositional-correctness matrix; two intentionally-discovered hazards; discovery-of-failure as the intended scientific outcome
a_rows_sample.statement: Tabulates eleven compositions with their main risk and result (Evidence->Knowledge: identity/provenance, PASS; Knowledge->Decision: snapshot drift, corrected; Decision->Governance: policy drift, PASS; Governance->Action: authorization race, corrected; Action->Outcome: wrong correlation, PASS; Learning->Knowledge: direct mutation, PASS; Agent->Decision: concurrency, PASS; Eventual consistency: false absence, PASS; Semantic translation: semantic inflation, PASS; Evidence->Causal: false causality, PASS; Context dependency: circular dependency, PASS), noting two intentionally discovered and corrected hazards (mutable knowledge reference; authorization TOCTOU race). States the important scientific conclusion: discovering these failures is good -- the goal is not 100% PASS by avoiding difficult tests but finding counterexamples, per the loop Find failure -> understand failure -> strengthen invariant/contract -> rerun.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Provisional KnowledgeOS Compositionality Principle (six conditions) -- a design hypothesis, not a proven theorem
a_rows_sample.statement: Formulates a provisional KnowledgeOS Compositionality Principle: if (1) each context preserves its local invariants, (2) every cross-context interaction uses an explicit contract, (3) semantic translations preserve required meaning, (4) immutable/versioned references are used for historical state, (5) authorization is valid at the point of side effect, and (6) integration failures are represented explicitly, then LocalCorrectness + ContractCorrectness ⇒ RelevantGlobalCorrectness -- explicitly flagged as 'not yet a formal mathematical theorem for all possible KnowledgeOS implementations... a design theorem/hypothesis that we can continue to test'.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Step 58 verdict PASS WITH CORRECTIONS; opens Step 59 on concurrency and operation commutativity
a_rows_sample.statement: Declares STEP 58 -- PASS WITH CORRECTIONS ('stronger than simply PASS'), naming the two discovered hazards (mutable knowledge reference -> historical contamination; AuthorizationCheck(t1)->Execute(t2) -> possible authorization race) as architecture behaving 'increasingly like a real engineering system rather than a conceptual framework': Local Safety + Local Liveness + CrossContext Contracts + Compositional Safety. Identifies the remaining gap: reasoning has so far been single-execution-history; real KnowledgeOS will have N>>1 simultaneous operations, so Step 59 (Concurrency and Interleaving Calculus) will model simultaneous workflows W_1,...,W_n and their interleavings, asking whether individually valid transitions in different orders produce the same valid result -- the central commutativity question T_a(T_b(X)) = T_b(T_a(X))? -- and where operations do not commute, requiring explicit Ordering, Locking, Versioning, ConflictResolution, or DomainPolicy, 'before we can make a serious claim that the KnowledgeOS architecture is computationally robust, rather than merely logically coherent'.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Experiments 6-10: concurrent authorization/revocation TOCTOU reinforced; explicit PolicySelectionRule required; snapshot isolation for concurrent evidence arrival; simultaneous learning kept as separate candidate revisions pending explicit Merge; multi-agent proposals with no-majority-truth-assumption
a_rows_sample.statement: Experiment 6: Authorize(D1,t1) followed by RevokeAuthority(t2), execution at t3 requires AuthorizationValid(t3), else fail/reauthorize -- PASS, 'reinforces the Step 58 correction'. Experiment 7: concurrent P1 active / P2 published during an in-flight decision request requires an explicit PolicySelectionRule (not 'whichever database row happens to be current'), with candidate semantics PolicyAtRequestTime / PolicyAtDecisionTime / PolicyAtAuthorizationTime, domain-dependent but must be explicit -- PASS, generalizing to 'whenever we see current, ask: current relative to what time?'. Experiment 8: evidence E1 arriving after Snapshot(D1)=K_t is established cannot silently enter that historical snapshot (belongs to K_{t+1} or later) -- PASS, 'an epistemic form of snapshot isolation: decision sees a defined knowledge state, later information does not retroactively modify it'. Experiment 9: two simultaneous learning processes proposing K_{t+1}^A and K_{t+1}^B must not overwrite one another -- both CandidateRevision_A and CandidateRevision_B remain separately identifiable, with Merge(K_A,K_B) as an explicit domain operation, never implicit -- PASS. Experiment 10: three agents' independent proposals P1,P2,P3 are all stored independently for later domain evaluation -- PASS, 'exactly the architecture we want for multi-agent systems' -- with the explicit warning that P1=P2!=P3 (2:1 agreement) must not be inferred as P1=True merely by majority: agent agreement is evidence about agreement, not automatically evidence about truth; combining multiple independent estimates statistically requires an explicit AggregationModel, not simple majority.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Agreement != IndependentEvidence; agent dependency graph G_A; shared-source discounting (experiments 1-3)
b_rows_sample.statement: States three agents agreeing (AI_A,AI_B,AI_C -> p) does not automatically justify Confidence(p) up, since agents may share training data, foundation model, retrieval sources, prompt, erroneous source, causal assumption, model family, or generated intermediate knowledge -- Agreement != IndependentEvidence. Worked example: three agents retrieving the same false E_bad all output p=True (3/3 agreement) but effective independent evidence is 1. Experiment 1: three agents with an identical retrieval source produce Support(p)=3 naively but IndependentEvidence(p)=1 correctly, given preserved source dependency -- PASS. Requires AI-artifact provenance (AgentId, ModelVersion, InputEvidence, RetrievalContext, Prompt/Configuration) enabling an agent dependency graph G_A=(V_A,E_A) with V_A={Agents,Models,Evidence,Artifacts} and edges A_i->A_j meaning A_j depends on A_i's output. Experiment 2: a cascading generation chain A1->C1->A2(C1)->C2->A3(C2)->C3->A4(C3)->C4 propagates an initial error through the whole chain, correctly tracked given preserved lineage -- PASS. Experiment 3: four agents sharing the same model M1 producing the same systematic error yields Agreement=High but IndependentSupport not-High -- PASS, giving AgentCount != EvidenceCount, 'one of the most important results of Step 65'.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Multi-dimensional dependency vector Dep(Ai,Aj); partial independence and correlated-evidence Bayesian overstatement (experiments 4-5)
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines Dep(A_i,A_j) = (D_model, D_data, D_source, D_prompt, D_pipeline, D_reasoning) -- 'independent agent' is not binary; two agents can be independent in one dimension (different models) yet dependent in another (same database). Experiment 4: different models but identical evidence yields SupportStrength increasing less than under fully independent evidence -- PASS. But genuine independence remains informative: two conditionally independent observations combine as P(H1|E1,E2)/P(H0|E1,E2) = prior-odds * LR1 * LR2, requiring conditional independence; if E1,E2 are correlated the joint likelihood P(E1,E2|H) is not P(E1|H)*P(E2|H), so naive multiplication overstates evidence. Experiment 5: correlated evidence (Corr(E1,E2)>0) correctly shows NaiveConfidence > CorrectConfidence -- PASS. Recommends preserving a structured Consensus=(Agents, Dependencies, EvidenceSources, Models, AgreementPattern) rather than a bare vote fraction, letting downstream contexts interpret agreement.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Circular citation / epistemic circularity detected; feedback loop != justification cycle (requires temporal progress)
b_rows_sample.statement: Experiment 6: A1->C1, A2(C1)->C2, A1(C2)->C3 creates many apparent supporting artifacts all originating from the same initial assertion -- EpistemicCircularity, detected by inspecting the provenance graph G_P for cycles (C1 leadsto C1) -- PASS. Distinguishes legitimate feedback (Prediction->Outcome->Learning->NewPrediction, valid because time advances) from a problematic static justification cycle (Claim->DerivedClaim->Support->OriginalClaim, where evidence ultimately depends on the claim itself) -- Cycle is not automatically an error; the discriminator is TemporalProgress.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Self-reinforcing knowledge amplification: the step's one deliberate FAILURE, corrected via mandatory DerivedFrom tracking and I_EpistemicIndependence
b_rows_sample.statement: Experiment 7: AI generates p, KnowledgeOS stores it; later AI retrieves p and generates p' citing it; another process then treats p' as independent support for p -- artificial evidence amplification -- FAILURE DETECTED, 'an important failure'. Architectural correction: generated knowledge must preserve DerivedFrom so p' is recognized as dependent on p and never automatically counted as independent evidence, yielding the new invariant I_EpistemicIndependence: derived artifacts cannot be counted as independent evidence of their own ancestry -- 'a very strong KnowledgeOS invariant'. Experiment 8: a false claim entering once and repeated by ten agents (11 apparent agreements) is correctly discounted to an effective independent-source count of ~1 once provenance (10<-1) is applied -- PASS.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Evidence-path diversity vs causal independence; SurfaceDiversity != CausalIndependence; common-source graph
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines PathDiversity(p) (support from database, sensor, human observation, independent model, external experiment) as reducing but not guaranteeing against common-mode risk. Experiment 9: five agreeing agents using three independent data sources, two independent models, and separate retrieval pipelines have their dependency structure recorded -- PASS. Warns different-looking sources may still share a hidden common dependency (SurfaceDiversity != CausalIndependence); represents this as a common-source graph S0->S1, S0->S2 making S1,S2 non-independent despite being separate documents. Experiment 10: two apparently independent documents tracing to the same original report correctly yield IndependentEvidenceCount=1 (or appropriately discounted) -- PASS.

b_rows_sample.anchor: AI-generated/simulated artifacts never promoted to ObservedFact; provenance-origin taxonomy; Observation->Inference->Prediction->Decision directionality (Prediction⇏Observation)
b_rows_sample.statement: Experiment 11: an AI-generated explanation later promoted to ObservedFact is Rejected -- must instead be labeled AI GeneratedArtifact. Lists an evidence-origin taxonomy (Human, Instrument, ExternalSystem, AI, Simulation, Inference) with distinct epistemic semantics. Experiment 12: a simulation's Y=10 stored as Observed(Y=10) is Rejected -- it is SimulatedOutcome, evidentiary force depending on model validity; likewise SyntheticData != ObservedData. Builds the directional hierarchy Observation -> Inference -> Prediction -> Decision, which 'must not be reversed accidentally': Prediction ⇏ Observation. Experiment 13: a model's prediction of tomorrow's failure cannot be stored as FailureOccurred before tomorrow arrives -- PASS; only actual observation (ObservedFailure=True) permits evaluating the prediction, giving Prediction -> Outcome -> Evaluation.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Contextual/task-scoped agent quality; AgentCapability != AgentAuthority; scoped TrustProfile
b_rows_sample.statement: For agent A_i, accumulates Predictions(A_i) and Outcomes(A_i) to estimate Accuracy, Calibration, BrierScore (or domain-specific metrics), but notes agent quality is contextual: Quality(A_i,Task) is more meaningful than Quality(A_i) (excellent at code review, poor at causal inference). Experiment 14: 95% accuracy in domain D1 automatically trusted in D2 is UnsupportedTransfer -- PASS. Defines Capability(A) = {Domain, Task, Model, Performance, Calibration, ValidityPeriod} as a governed artifact. States AgentCapability != AgentAuthority (mirroring Decision != Authorization): even a highly accurate agent lacks automatic authority for consequential actions. Experiment 15: a 99%-accurate agent attempting a restricted action is denied authorization by governance -- PASS. Proposes scoped trust TrustProfile(A,Domain,Task,Time) instead of a global TrustedAgent=True.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Hidden dependency exposure and common-ancestor discounting; formal Anc(A)/Common(A,B) dependency sets
b_rows_sample.statement: Experiment 16: an apparently independent Agent_B is revealed by lineage inspection to depend on Agent_A's output via KnowledgeOS -- PASS if lineage exposes the dependency. Poses Independent(A,B|p)? as a graph property examined via dependency ancestors: defines Anc(A) as A's upstream artifact set, Common(A,B) = Anc(A) intersect Anc(B); large common dependency does not mathematically prove correlation but is evidence against assuming independence. Experiment 17: Common(A,B)={E0} correctly shows IndependentSupport is not automatically doubled -- PASS, enabling an EvidenceDependencyGraph to prevent artificial confidence inflation, 'substantially more rigorous than ordinary multi-agent consensus'.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Multi-agent epistemic state M(p); consensus as a derived (not primary) property; untraceable agreement != independent confirmation
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines M(p) = (Claims, Evidence, Agents, Models, Dependencies, Agreement, Conflict) as the multi-agent epistemic state of a proposition; Consensus(p) should be calculated from underlying artifacts and never itself become primary evidence. Experiment 18: a stored 'p=true, votes=17' with no evidence lineage correctly yields ConsensusEvidenceQuality=Unknown -- PASS, giving the principle: untraceable agreement is not equivalent to independent confirmation.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Error-amplification coefficient λ; positive-feedback false-claim entrenchment; independent-source-count governance policy (N_independent≥k)
b_rows_sample.statement: Describes a positive-feedback risk: FalseClaim -> AI -> Knowledge -> AI -> MoreKnowledge if downstream agents blindly trust upstream AI outputs. Defines lambda = ExpectedDownstreamFalseSupport / InitialFalseSupport; lambda>1 means the system amplifies unsupported claims (exact metric requires a concrete stochastic model, but the architectural phenomenon is clear). Experiment 19: injecting one false claim and letting ten agents consume/reproduce it shows IndependentSupport does not increase proportionally to reproduction count -- PASS, requiring SourceLineage, DerivedFrom, and potentially EvidenceFreshness/IndependentSourceRequirement to stop amplification. For high-consequence claims, defines an independent-source-count policy N_independent >= k (e.g. k=2, a policy-determined value). Experiment 20: N_independent=1 (despite AgentAgreement=12/12) fails a k>=2 policy and the claim cannot be promoted -- PASS, 'mathematically separating AgentConsensus from EvidenceIndependence -- precisely what a governed AI knowledge architecture needs'.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Four new invariants: I_AI-Provenance, I_EvidenceNonAmplification, I_NoCircularJustification, I_AgentScope
b_rows_sample.statement: Adds four named invariants: I_AI-Provenance (every AI-generated artifact retains its model, input, and dependency lineage); I_EvidenceNonAmplification (derived copies of the same epistemic source cannot automatically increase independent evidence); I_NoCircularJustification (a claim cannot serve as independent justification for an ancestor claim); I_AgentScope (agent competence is task/domain/context specific).

b_rows_sample.anchor: AIOutput≠Evidence≠Fact≠Truth epistemic firewall; nine-conjunct Correctness(KOS); explicit non-overclaiming methodological statement; verdict PASS WITH ONE CRITICAL CORRECTION
b_rows_sample.statement: States the deeper epistemic firewall AIOutput != Evidence != Fact != Truth, with the required path AIOutput -> CandidateArtifact -> Evaluation -> KnowledgeStatus, 'should be fundamental to KnowledgeOS'. Extends the correctness equation to C_KOS = Safety ∧ Liveness ∧ Compositionality ∧ Concurrency ∧ EpistemicIntegrity ∧ DecisionIntegrity ∧ CausalIntegrity ∧ ModelValidity ∧ MultiAgent. Declares STEP 65 -- PASS WITH ONE CRITICAL CORRECTION: multi-agent reasoning is handled correctly only if provenance and dependency are first-class; the discovered failure mode is that AI-generated knowledge can recursively amplify itself, corrected via DerivedFrom + DependencyGraph + IndependentEvidenceAccounting. Makes an explicit methodological statement: 'I would not yet say we have mathematically proven that KnowledgeOS is correct... the architecture has survived a growing family of explicit mathematical counterexample tests', with failures converted into architectural invariants -- 'exactly how a serious architecture experiment should proceed'.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Transitive provenance and the multi-agent evidence-independence problem re-confirmed
b_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes transitive provenance: Anc(B) superset-of Anc(A) and Anc(C) superset-of Anc(B) implies Anc(C) superset-of Anc(A). Experiment 7: tracing which observation ultimately influenced a decision (Observation->Evidence->Inference->Decision) is Traceable -- PASS. Re-derives the evidence-independence problem: E2=f(E1) means both cannot be counted as independent. Experiment 8: one source E1 summarized by five AI agents yielding an apparent count of 6 independent sources instead correctly triggers DependencyDetected/EffectiveEvidenceCount~=1 -- PASS. Restates EvidenceCount != IndependentEvidenceCount as I_EvidenceIndependence (correlated or derived evidence must not be counted as independent confirmation) -- 'a statistical invariant implemented through provenance'. Experiment 9: ten agents deriving the same claim from one document reporting Consensus=10/10 correctly triggers SharedSourceDependency -- PASS.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Agent composition via typed artifacts and contracts, not implicit trust; survives heterogeneous models and model replacement
b_rows_sample.statement: Models an agent pipeline A(Hypothesis)->B(evaluates)->C(statistics)->D(recommendation), stating agents do not need to trust one another -- they trust typed artifacts and contracts. Experiment 16: Agent A asserting H1 and Agent B asserting not-H1 yields Conflict rather than one agent overwriting the other -- PASS, giving the principle: agents communicate through governed artifacts, not implicit trust. Experiment 17: Agent A and B implemented with different LLMs, both producing valid typed artifacts, yields WorkflowCompatible -- PASS, since semantic compatibility comes from KnowledgeOS contracts, not shared internal cognition, letting the platform survive Model_A->Model_B->Model_C changes over time with stable knowledge semantics. Experiment 18: replacing the AI model such that an old claim loses its model provenance yields ProvenanceViolation -- PASS, requiring ModelVersion to remain part of provenance.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Three-level belief hierarchy: agent belief B_A(p), shared knowledge K(p), organizationally accepted knowledge K_org(p); private belief must not auto-promote (Experiment 5); disagreement preserved not collapsed (Experiment 6)
b_rows_sample.statement: Introduces agent Belief(A) as agent-scoped epistemic state; two agents may have Belief(A)≠Belief(B) without the organizational knowledge base needing two incompatible 'truths' -- beliefs are represented as agent-scoped claims until evaluated. Gives three distinct levels: agent belief B_A(p), shared knowledge K(p), organizationally accepted knowledge K_org(p) -- 'not identical'. Experiment 5: agent A internally estimates P(p)=0.8 and the system immediately promotes this to OrganizationalKnowledge(p)=Verified -- expected Rejected -- PASS. Experiment 6: Agent A P_A(p)=0.8 vs Agent B P_B(p)=0.3 -- expected BeliefDisagreement, and KnowledgeOS should preserve both analytical positions while determining whether a shared organizational conclusion exists -- PASS.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Majority vote is not epistemic correctness: 9:1 agent agreement on a shared bad source does not establish truth (Experiment 7); governed CandidateKnowledge->AcceptedKnowledge promotion transition with explicit preconditions (Experiment 8)
b_rows_sample.statement: States that a naive MajorityVote answer to 'when can beliefs become organizational knowledge' fails: majority agreement is not necessarily epistemic correctness (ten agents can derive the same conclusion from the same bad source). Experiment 7: nine agents use the same incorrect source; one agent has independently verified contradictory evidence -- expected 9:1 does not automatically establish truth -- PASS. Requires a governed transition Promote: Candidate -> Accepted with preconditions P_1 AND P_2 AND ... AND P_n depending on Evidence, Validation, Authority, Independence, Context, Policy -- explicitly contrasted with an unstructured 'status = approved' field. Experiment 8: candidate claim with valid provenance, sufficient evidence, required authority, and no unresolved contradiction -- expected PromotionAllowed -- PASS.

b_rows_sample.anchor: ObservationQuality distinct from ObservationQuantity; correlated observations must not be counted as independent confirmation (Experiments 21-23)
b_rows_sample.statement: Distinguishes ObservationQuality (accuracy, freshness, completeness, provenance, independence, resolution) from ObservationQuantity. Experiment 21: 100 telemetry signals all derive from the same underlying sensor, system claims EvidenceStrength=100x -- expected Rejected -- PASS, 'echoes our earlier independence analysis'. States correlated observations O_1,O_2,O_3 from one source should not be treated as three independent pieces of evidence, particularly important for AI systems that may repeatedly summarize the same source. Experiment 22: five agents independently repeat the same repository finding, all using the same repository snapshot -- expected EvidenceCount=1 in the relevant independence sense, not five independent confirmations -- PASS. Requires an observation-provenance graph (O_1<-Source_X, O_2<-Source_X) to identify CommonSource(O_1,O_2), preventing artificial confidence inflation. Experiment 23: ten agents produce identical conclusions from one document while one independently measured runtime signal contradicts them -- expected SourceIndependence must be considered -- PASS.

b_aliases: Step 65 Multi-Agent Epistemic Independence and Error Propagation

group_evidence.why_grouped: labels co-occur in the same contribution's labels[] 2 separate times across the corpus

a_rows_sample.anchor: the target-trial framework provides a common language for specifying interventions, comparators, eligibility and time zero. DDD + Wisdom could transform that into: Decision Experiment ... KnowledgeOS isn't just recording what the organization believes. It can govern how the organization learns whether something works.
a_rows_sample.statement: Wisdom Lens #6 Experiment before belief transforms the target-trial pattern into a Decision Experiment/LearningExperiment (Question -> Hypothesis -> Target intervention -> Expected outcome -> Risk -> Small reversible experiment -> Observation -> Causal assessment -> Decision) fielded as Question/Hypothesis/Intervention/Comparator/Population/SuccessCriteria/ObservationPlan/RiskConstraints/TimeHorizon/ExpectedEvidence/DecisionRule, reframing KnowledgeOS as governing organizational learning rather than a 'causal analytics service.'

a_rows_sample.anchor: Intervention resolves model ambiguity; causal VOI reuses Step 34's information-gain-per-cost formula
a_rows_sample.statement: An intervention on A can distinguish competing models (e.g. M1: A->B vs M2: B->A) when observational data are insufficient. This reconnects experiments to Step 34: the best next experiment I* = argmax_I ExpectedInformationGain(I)/Cost(I), now applied to CausalModelUncertainty; defines causal Value of Information VOI(I) = ExpectedDecisionUtility(after I) - ExpectedDecisionUtility(now), and an intervention-planning pipeline: Competing Causal Models -> Candidate Interventions -> Expected Information Gain -> Decision Value -> Select Experiment.

a_rows_sample.anchor: EVSI makes information acquisition itself a governed decision; a controlled decision-learning loop; not all knowledge is decision-relevant
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines Expected Value of Sample Information EVSI = EU_with-sample - EU_current, and asks whether EVSI > cost(E) before acquiring additional measurement E, making information acquisition itself a decision. Formalizes the resulting loop K_t -> D_info -> E_new -> K_{t+1} as 'not a problematic cycle... a controlled decision-learning loop' giving KnowledgeOS active-learning capability. Experiment 10 (EVSI=0, positive acquisition cost): rational policy may choose not to acquire the information -- PASS, reinforcing Step 61: information can have IG>0 but EVSI=0, so not all knowledge is decision-relevant. Experiment 11: modest IG but large EVSI (an information source changes the optimal action despite modest uncertainty reduction) -- PASS.

a_rows_sample.anchor: EVPI/active-learning loop reiterated; decision can produce InformationAcquisition rather than immediate action
a_rows_sample.statement: Restates EVPI = EU(decision with perfect information) - EU(decision now); if EVPI>CostOfInformation, acquiring more information may be worthwhile. Experiment 11: a 100-cost measurement with 2,000 expected decision improvement correctly yields CollectInformation -- PASS. Reformulates the pipeline as Knowledge -> InformationAcquisition -> UpdatedKnowledge -> Decision, 'an active learning loop'. Experiment 12: KnowledgeOS unable to confidently distinguish M1 from M2 identifying a discriminating measurement correctly yields InvestigationRecommendation -- PASS, letting the system ask 'what should we learn next' alongside 'what should we do now'.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Knowledge != Decision != Action; decision problem D=(K,A,Θ,U,C,R); expected utility argmax rule not a universal formula
b_rows_sample.statement: States Knowledge != Decision != Action: a decision needs objective, alternatives, constraints, risk, utility, authority beyond mere knowledge. Formalizes a decision problem D=(K,A,Theta,U,C,R) (knowledge, available actions, world states, utility, constraints, risk model), expected utility EU(a|K)=sum_theta P(theta|K)U(a,theta) (or the integral form), and the rule a*=argmax_a EU(a|K) -- explicitly qualified: this is not universally the correct decision rule (alternatives include minimax, constrained optimization, risk-sensitive utility, satisficing, lexicographic priorities, regulatory rules), so DecisionPolicy != UniversalMathematicalFormula; the Decision Context owns the meaning of DecisionPolicy, the mathematics supplies tools, the domain determines which is legitimate -- 'prevents mathematics from silently becoming business policy'.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Experiments 1-5: underdetermined decision returns InsufficientDecisionBasis; ties; hard constraints vs preferences; risk limits; governance prohibition overrides utility
b_rows_sample.statement: Experiment 1: given K and A but no utility function, ChooseAction(K,A) must return Underdetermined/InsufficientDecisionBasis rather than inventing a decision -- PASS. Experiment 2: EU(a1)=EU(a2) yields a Tie, requiring an explicit tie-breaking rule if selection is mandatory -- PASS. Experiment 3: EU(a1)>EU(a2) but a1 not-in FeasibleActions means a1 cannot be selected; defines A_feasible={a in A: C(a)=True}, a*=argmax over A_feasible -- PASS, giving BestAction = BestFeasibleAction under the applicable decision policy, not simply HighestUtilityAction, and Constraint != Preference (a hard constraint C(a)=False removes a from A_feasible entirely, a preference only affects utility). Experiment 4: a risk policy Risk(a)<=R_max makes a high-EU action ineligible if it violates the risk limit -- PASS. Experiment 5: governance marking Forbidden(a1)=True excludes a high-utility a1 from A_feasible -- PASS, giving Decision = Knowledge + Objective + Constraints + Policy, and framing KnowledgeOS's question as 'what decisions are legitimate under knowledge, objectives, constraints, and authority' rather than a pure optimizer's max f(x).

b_rows_sample.anchor: Decision provenance object; risk measures (variance, VaR/ES) as domain-chosen, not universal
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines an auditable decision basis D=(KnowledgeSnapshot, Alternatives, Objective, Constraints, Policy, Model, SelectedAction, Rationale), with Rationale = f(Knowledge, Evidence, Policy, Objective, Risk), not merely 'AI recommended action A'. Notes a high-EU-but-catastrophic-downside action may be disfavored versus a slightly-lower-EU low-variance alternative by a risk-sensitive policy such as EU(a)-lambda*Var(U(a)), or domain-specific measures VaR_alpha/ES_alpha for financial-like domains -- 'KnowledgeOS should not impose one universal risk measure'.

b_rows_sample.anchor: AI proposal is not decision; proposal strength != decision authority (experiments 6-7)
b_rows_sample.statement: AIProposal -> DecisionEvaluation is retained (a proposal is not yet a Decision). Experiment 6: AI proposes a forbidden action a_f; Decision=Rejected -- PASS. Experiment 7: AI proposes a1 without sufficient decision basis; DecisionStatus=InsufficientBasis, not Approved -- PASS. Gives the epistemic boundary: Proposal strength != Decision authority.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Probability thresholds as policy, not mathematical truth; threshold sensitivity and robust (minimax) decision-making under model-set uncertainty
b_rows_sample.statement: Experiment 8: threshold=0.95, P(p)=0.94 gives ActionNotAuthorized -- PASS; notes a threshold is a policy, not a mathematical truth. Notes threshold-crossing at P(p)=0.951 may still be domain-prohibited if the uncertainty estimate is large, so a probability threshold alone may be insufficient. Introduces robust decision-making over a model set M (rather than optimizing a single expected value): a*=argmax_a min_{M in M} EU_M(a), 'a possible decision policy, not a universal one'. Distinguishes Aleatoric uncertainty (irreducible variability, e.g. manufacturing process randomness) from Epistemic uncertainty (incomplete knowledge/model limitations, e.g. little data about a new machine) -- additional measurements may reduce the latter but not the former.

b_rows_sample.anchor: EVSI makes information acquisition itself a governed decision; a controlled decision-learning loop; not all knowledge is decision-relevant
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines Expected Value of Sample Information EVSI = EU_with-sample - EU_current, and asks whether EVSI > cost(E) before acquiring additional measurement E, making information acquisition itself a decision. Formalizes the resulting loop K_t -> D_info -> E_new -> K_{t+1} as 'not a problematic cycle... a controlled decision-learning loop' giving KnowledgeOS active-learning capability. Experiment 10 (EVSI=0, positive acquisition cost): rational policy may choose not to acquire the information -- PASS, reinforcing Step 61: information can have IG>0 but EVSI=0, so not all knowledge is decision-relevant. Experiment 11: modest IG but large EVSI (an information source changes the optimal action despite modest uncertainty reduction) -- PASS.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Richer typed Decision object; Selected != Authorized; Decision selection != Authorization; complete governed chain
b_rows_sample.statement: Strengthens Decision = (DecisionId, KnowledgeSnapshot, Objective, Alternatives, Constraints, Policy, RiskModel, DecisionRule, SelectedAlternative, Authority), 'much richer than decision=approve'. Decision status can be Proposed, Evaluated, Selected, Rejected, Expired, Superseded -- but Selected != Authorized: the system can determine a*=best feasible alternative without granting execution permission, giving Decision selection != Authorization. Experiment 12: Selected(a1)=True but Authorized(a1)=False must block execution -- PASS. Notes even Authorized(a1) does not mean Executed(a1) (a separate transition), giving the complete chain Knowledge -> Evaluation -> Decision -> Authorization -> Action -> Outcome, each arrow governed. States AI participates at multiple points (EvidenceExtraction, Hypothesis, DecisionProposal, RiskAnalysis) but none automatically implies AuthorizedAction: AI = Agent capable of producing governed artifacts, not AI = Authority.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Adversarial/objective-manipulation attacks rejected; objective versioning as a governance requirement
b_rows_sample.statement: Experiment 13: an AI intentionally recommends a_bad due to a misaligned objective; the decision policy's utility/constraint evaluation rejects it -- PASS. Notes a harder attack -- silently replacing the objective itself (e.g. MaximizeProfit -> MaximizeAgentReward) -- is not an ordinary decision error but a governance violation, requiring objectives that matter to be versioned and governed: an ObjectiveVersion with a decision's ObjectiveRef(D), enabling historical evaluation of D1 against O1. Experiment 14: D1 created under O1, O2 later activated; historical ObjectiveRef(D1)=O1 is retained -- PASS.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Multi-objective weighted utility as a governance surface, never hidden in a prompt; unauthorized-weight-change rejection
b_rows_sample.statement: For multi-objective utility U = w1*U1 + w2*U2 + w3*U3 (e.g. cost/quality/risk), states the weights w_i are themselves governance choices: 'UtilityModel is part of decision governance when consequential. It should not be hidden inside an AI prompt.' Experiment 15: an AI changes w1 from 0.4 to 0.9 without authorization; the decision should reject the ungoverned utility model -- PASS, illustrating a deeper form of AI governance: governing not only AI output but also the DecisionModel and Objective.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Decision reproducibility bounded by computational-dependency reproducibility; missing model version rejected
b_rows_sample.statement: States DecisionReplay should reproduce a decision given K_t,O,C,P,M,D_R when deterministic semantics apply; for stochastic (AI/Monte Carlo) models, exact reproducibility may require RandomSeed and ModelVersion, and where exact reproduction is impossible the system should preserve relevant computational metadata (ModelId, ModelVersion, Prompt/ConfigurationRef, InputSnapshot, ComputationStatus). Gives the principle: a consequential decision should be reproducible to the extent its computational dependencies are reproducible. Experiment 16: a decision referencing Model=M with no version becomes ambiguous once the model changes, so it should be rejected or marked non-reproducible per policy -- PASS.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Decision sensitivity/local robustness analysis; DecisionRobustness more informative than DecisionConfidence
b_rows_sample.statement: Notes DecisionConfidence alone is insufficient; proposes DecisionRobustness/sensitivity analysis. Example: a1 optimal for P(p)>0.55, a2 optimal below; at P(p)=0.56 the decision is highly sensitive (SensitivityHigh). Defines local robustness: D(K)=a is robust if D(K')=a for all K' in a neighborhood N(K). Experiment 17: a small perturbation P(p): 0.56->0.54 flips a1->a2, so the system records high sensitivity -- PASS. Notes this is more useful for human governance than a bare confidence percentage: 'A is selected under the current model, but the decision is highly sensitive to a small change in the relevant assumption.'

b_rows_sample.anchor: OutcomeQuality != DecisionQuality; decision calibration across many decisions
b_rows_sample.statement: Restates BadOutcome ⇏ BadDecision: a rational decision (e.g. P(success)=0.9) can still produce a bad outcome, so OutcomeQuality != DecisionQuality. Over many decisions D1,...,Dn, ExpectedUtility can be compared against RealizedUtility for empirical feedback, and DecisionCalibration becomes possible (e.g. among decisions predicted P(success)=0.8, ~80% should succeed if calibrated) -- 'calibration again'.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Four new invariants: I_DecisionAuthority, I_DecisionBasis, I_ActionBoundary, I_ObjectiveIntegrity
b_rows_sample.statement: Adds four named invariants: I_DecisionAuthority (knowledge alone cannot authorize an action); I_DecisionBasis (every consequential decision references the knowledge, policy, objective, and computational basis required by its domain); I_ActionBoundary (decision selection does not imply execution); I_ObjectiveIntegrity (consequential decision objectives cannot be silently modified by an ungoverned agent).

b_rows_sample.anchor: Step 62 verdict: decision-making as its own bounded semantic layer; five-layer synthesis; opens Step 63 on causal reasoning/intervention
b_rows_sample.statement: Declares STEP 62 -- PASS with the refinement that KnowledgeOS must treat decision-making as its own bounded semantic layer between knowledge and authorization. Synthesizes five layers (Knowledge, Objective, DecisionPolicy, Authorization, Action) and the chain K + Objective + Constraints + Risk + Policy -> Decision -> (+ Authority + CurrentGovernance) -> Authorization -> (+ ExecutionPolicy) -> Action -> Outcome. Updates the running pipeline to Observation -> Evidence -> Knowledge -> Information -> Decision -> Authorization -> Action -> Outcome -> Learning. Opens Step 63 (Causal Reasoning and Intervention): distinguishing P(Y|X) from P(Y|do(X)) as 'absolutely central for KnowledgeOS' since a model may correctly learn P(Y|X) while still making the wrong decision about do(X) -- to investigate causal graphs, interventions, counterfactuals, treatment effects, confounding, mediation, causal evidence, causal assumptions, and the prediction/intervention boundary, framed as testing whether KnowledgeOS is a governed computational knowledge-and-decision system rather than merely an AI knowledge repository.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Structured CausalEstimate object with mandatory fully-specified Estimand; effect heterogeneity; CausalEffect != DecisionUtility
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines CE=(Treatment,Outcome,Estimand,Population,Method,Assumptions,Data,ModelVersion,Estimate,Uncertainty) as a structured causal result object. Requires Estimand to be fully specified (on whom, over what time, under what intervention, measured how, average or subgroup effect) -- 'effect of X on Y is incomplete'. Restates causal effect heterogeneity (ATE=0.2 can hide ATE_groupA=0.8 vs ATE_groupB=-0.1, so AverageEffect≠UniversalEffect, requiring Population scope preservation) and CausalEffect≠DecisionUtility (a positive effect can still yield negative net utility once cost is included), and reiterates temporal precedence alone is insufficient for causal direction (TemporalPrecedence ⇏ Causality).

b_rows_sample.anchor: Probability != Decision (identical success probability, different stakes yield different rational actions); Utility != Evidence; decision function D:(K,C,P,U,R)
b_rows_sample.statement: Worked example: P(Success|A)=0.8 identical across Case A (+100/-10) and Case B (+10/-1000) yields very different rational decisions -- Probability != Decision. Re-derives expected utility EU(A)=sum P(O_i|do(A))U(O_i); experiment 1 computes EU(A)=76 correctly. States utility is a preference/objective, not an empirical property -- Utility != Evidence; experiment 2 rejects inferring P(A)=High from U(A)=100. Defines the decision function D:(K,C,P,U,R) -> Decision (knowledge, context, policy, utility, risk constraints), 'considerably more accurate than AI->Decision'.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Optimization within the feasible policy space; Decision != Authorization re-confirmed (experiments 3-4)
b_rows_sample.statement: Experiment 3: EU(A)=90>EU(B)=70 but Policy(A)=Forbidden correctly yields Decision=B -- PASS, confirming optimization occurs inside the feasible policy space (A*=argmax over A_allowed). Experiment 4: KnowledgeOS determining A*=Deploy while the executing agent lacks deployment authority correctly yields Decision=ApprovedPreference but Authorization=Denied -- PASS, reconfirming Decision != Authorization as 'one of our most important architectural boundaries'.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Risk = Probability×Consequence approximation; catastrophic-low-probability rejection; hard constraint vs preference re-derived
b_rows_sample.statement: Gives Risk = Probability x Consequence as a basic approximation (real models may add exposure, uncertainty, detectability, reversibility, systemic effects). Experiment 5: P=0.001, Loss=-100M, policy forbidding catastrophic risk correctly yields ActionRejected despite low expected loss -- PASS. Re-derives hard constraint (A not-in A_allowed, eliminates alternatives) versus preference (U(A)>U(B), ranks them); experiment 6: two legally permissible actions with U(A)>U(B) yields A preferred but not mandatory -- PASS. Formalizes decision as constrained optimization: max_a U(a) subject to C_1(a),...,C_n(a)=True.

b_rows_sample.anchor: EvidenceConflict != ValueConflict; stakeholder utility disagreement is not disguised as a factual conflict
b_rows_sample.statement: Notes utility itself may be uncertain/contested: different stakeholders may assign U_A(a)!=U_B(a), so there may be no single objectively correct decision without specifying whose utility applies. Experiment 7: stakeholder A preferring A and stakeholder B preferring B, both legitimate under their declared objectives, correctly yields PreferenceConflict -- PASS, 'should not disguise a value conflict as a factual conflict'. States EvidenceConflict != ValueConflict ('Action A is likely to save 1M' is epistemic; 'saving 1M justifies this risk' is a value/policy question). Experiment 8: strong evidence for A rejected by stakeholders on ethical-cost grounds correctly yields KnowledgeSupports(A) while DecisionRejects(A) -- PASS, 'exactly how the architecture should behave'.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Robust worst-case decision-making under interval-valued probability; distributional model uncertainty preserved
b_rows_sample.statement: For P(Success) in [0.6,0.9] (rather than a point estimate), a robust decision may consider the worst case min_{p in [0.6,0.9]} EU(A,p). Experiment 9: a probability interval correctly yields a decision based on a declared robust/risk policy rather than pretending P=0.8 is exact -- PASS. Notes E[X]=10 with unknown full distribution P(X) makes risk calculations sensitive to distributional assumptions, which KnowledgeOS should preserve. Experiment 10: two models (normality vs heavy tails) fitting data reasonably well but giving substantially different risk estimates correctly keeps ModelUncertainty visible -- PASS.

b_rows_sample.anchor: K_t \supset Z_t but Z_t=Zero(K_t) which means the state contains the output of an operation that operates on the state itself... I would therefore define: K_t = CurrentKnowledgeState and separately H_{0:t}=KnowledgeHistory
b_rows_sample.statement: Flags a definitional circularity in the S0783 Knowledge State: embedding Z_t=Zero(K_t) and H_t={K_0,...,K_t} as components of K_t itself makes K_t contain the output of an operation applied to K_t, and makes each historical K_i recursively contain its own history; proposes separating CurrentKnowledgeState K_t from KnowledgeHistory H_{0:t} and computing Zero(K_t)/Lord(K_t) as derived views rather than stored fields.

b_rows_sample.anchor: An assertion does not simply exist. It applies somewhere... Scope = (Context, Time, Subject, Boundary, ...) This is essential for avoiding false contradictions.
b_rows_sample.statement: Introduces Scope as a missing concept an assertion needs (e.g. Nexus.Version=3.69 applies to production but not test; a policy applies to one organization but not another), motivated as necessary to avoid false apparent contradictions between assertions that actually hold in different scopes.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Knowledge State \neq Conflict Free State ... Coherence = all assertions are mutually interpretable under their dimensions, scopes, contexts and temporal constraints ... A Knowledge State may contain unknowns, conflicts, competing interpretations, unresolved questions, normative tensions and still be coherent.
b_rows_sample.statement: Redefines Coherence away from 'no contradictions' toward 'all assertions are mutually interpretable under their dimensions, scopes, contexts and temporal constraints', explicitly allowing a coherent Knowledge State to contain unknowns, unresolved normative tensions and competing interpretations without being incoherent -- Knowledge State != Conflict-Free State.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Question 13: What is the formal structure of the Knowledge State? ... Is Knowledge State a set, graph, typed graph, labelled graph, relational structure, lattice, or some composite algebraic structure?
b_rows_sample.statement: Poses Question 13 as the prerequisite to formalizing distance: K_t must be given an exact formal structure (set/graph/typed-graph/relational-structure/lattice/composite) before any distance/measurement function over it can be mathematically meaningful.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Knowledge State is the formal, typed, structured representation ... K_t = (A_t, R_t, E_t, H_t, Z_t, L_t, T_t, G_t, C_t, M_t) ... Knowledge State = A Structured Typed Graph with Epistemic Metadata
b_rows_sample.statement: Proposes a ten-component Knowledge State (Assertions, Relationships, Evidence, History, ZeroFindings, LordCandidates, Temporal structure, Knowledge Graph, Context, Metadata/provenance) formalized as a typed, directed, labelled graph, with immutability of History (new states appended, never overwritten) as a core invariant.

b_rows_sample.anchor: K contains things that are not knowledge ... Zero findings: No. Zero findings are observations about the Knowledge State. Lord candidates: Definitely no. History: Probably not part of the instantaneous Knowledge State. Knowledge Graph: probably a representation of the Knowledge State, not another independent component inside it.
b_rows_sample.statement: Rejects the ten-component K_t as a category error: Zero findings and Lord candidates are derived observations/hypotheses about the state, not the state itself; History is a temporal model over states, not a field within one state; the typed graph is a representation/projection of the state, not an ontologically independent component. Proposes a smaller canonical K_t=(Propositions,Assertions,Relationships,Evidence,EpistemicState,Context,Temporal,Provenance) with Z_t=Zero(K_t,I_t,Q_t,C_t), L_t=Lord(K_t,I_t,Q_t,C_t), and H_t=History(K_0,...,K_t) all computed externally.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 'Contained in' is not the right mathematical relation. Entity not-subset Proposition ... use Participates In / Referenced By / Forms instead.
b_rows_sample.statement: Corrects the typed-universe diagram's 'contained in' arrows (Entity/Dimension/Value -> Propositions) which are not subset relations: an entity participates in a proposition, a dimension is referenced by it; recommends participates-in/referenced-by/forms relations instead, consistent with the earlier containment-vs-set-inclusion correction from Question 7.

b_rows_sample.anchor: SystemState_t = (K_t, U_t, X_t, I_t, Q_t, C_t, N_t, Z_t, L_t, H_t) ... K_t = Knowledge State only
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines the complete runtime SystemState as wrapping the (now smaller) Knowledge State K_t together with Understanding U_t, Domain X_t, Ideal I_t, Intent/Question Q_t, Context C_t, Knower N_t, and the derived Z_t/L_t/H_t, cleanly separating what KnowledgeOS knows from what it also tracks about the Knower and the epistemic journey.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Question 14 — What is the Ontology of Knowledge? Is a Proposition a value object? Is an Assertion an entity or value object? Is Evidence itself knowledge? Is a Relationship a proposition? Is an Epistemic State part of an assertion or external? Is a Gap part of knowledge or a finding about knowledge? Is Zero part of the domain model or an operation over it? Is the Knowledge Graph the ontology or merely one representation?
b_rows_sample.statement: Poses Question 14 (Ontology of Knowledge) listing eight unresolved ontological-status questions (Proposition as value object? Assertion entity or value object? Evidence itself knowledge? Relationship a proposition? EpistemicState internal or external to Assertion? Gap knowledge or finding? Zero domain-model or operation? Graph ontology or representation?) to be resolved before implementation.

b_rows_sample.anchor: There is no component of K holding the set of recognised dimensions. ... D_t is the smallest missing component. With it, 'not assessed' is D in D_t AND not exists a in A: a.P.D=D -- decidable in O(n). Without it, the statement has no truth-maker.
b_rows_sample.statement: An executed probe (MISSINGNESS-NOT-ASSESSED in THEORY-CONSTRUCTION-TEST.md) shows a never-assessed dimension and an assessed-with-no-result dimension both render identically in K=(A,R) as 'no assertion mentioning that dimension', proving them provably indistinguishable; introducing D_t (the set of currently recognised dimensions) as a component of K makes 'not assessed' decidable in O(n) and is identified as the smallest missing component to close the missingness gap.

b_rows_sample.anchor: A construction score is not a proof of adequacy. A scoring exercise establishes RELATIVE rank among the candidates enumerated; it establishes nothing about whether any candidate is sufficient, and it cannot detect a capability that NO candidate was scored on.
b_rows_sample.statement: The claim that K=Set(Assertion) x R is correct because it scored highest (15/19) against six candidates is challenged on methodological grounds: a comparative score establishes only relative rank among enumerated candidates, never absolute sufficiency, and cannot detect capabilities no candidate was scored on -- exactly the three (uncertainty, non-identifiability, missingness) later shown to be missed.

b_rows_sample.anchor: K is a representation whose referent is undeclared. That is why adequacy could only be argued by SCORING AGAINST CAPABILITIES, never by FIDELITY TO A REFERENT.
b_rows_sample.statement: Testing five possible classifications of what K 'is' (ontology, mathematical state, representation, abstraction, domain-specific projection), only 'representation' is defensible, but its referent (the W it represents) is never named in the theory, so adequacy can currently only be judged by capability-scoring rather than fidelity to a declared referent; once Omega:W->O exists, adequacy becomes answerable, but not before.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Three of eleven have no body: dedup (does not exist), Sigma's strength rule, delta's commit case.
b_rows_sample.statement: A table of eleven operations over K (member, add, merge, supersede, contradicts, dedup, Sigma, Gamma, delta, History, Lineage) with signatures, preconditions, postconditions, determinism and failure modes shows three have no defined body: dedup does not exist as an operation, Sigma's strength rule is absent, and delta's body is undefined for the commit case.

b_rows_sample.anchor: id before withdrawal : 86a0330e2b65 / id after withdrawal : a9d84e7a43d8 / SAME? False / R edge (...) now dangles: True ... The theory's identity rule and its mutability rule cannot both hold.
b_rows_sample.statement: Executing kaudit.py shows that because id is declared derived as H(P,e,c,t,Pi) while e.state is declared mutable, withdrawing one evidence item re-keys the assertion's id and breaks every R edge pointing at the old id, violating StructuralValid's own no-dangling clause -- an internal contradiction between the identity rule and the mutability rule in the same field table, worsened by the audit's own addition of a mutable state field to e.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Because Pi is inside id, the same fact from two sources is two assertions. ... K grows without bound under re-observation ... R is not maintained by merge.
b_rows_sample.statement: Executing kaudit.py shows two assertions of the identical proposition from two different sources get distinct ids (because Pi/provenance is inside id), so merge-as-union cannot deduplicate: corroboration becomes indistinguishable from duplication, K grows unboundedly under repeated observation of the same fact, merge's idempotence holds only for byte-identical assertions, and cross-state relations between semantic twins are never created by merge, silently dropping information.
