b_rows_sample.anchor: Identifiable(g,Omega) quantifies over a world space W ... The canonical theory's eight-layer ontology ... has NO Omega. The property is therefore not FALSE in that theory; it is NOT STATABLE. ... therefore a layer is missing beneath Observation.
b_rows_sample.statement: Step 031 s31.17-31.21 gives a complete, correctly-quantified identifiability definition (Identifiable(g,Omega) iff for all W1,W2, Omega(W1)=Omega(W2) implies g(W1)=g(W2)) requiring the system to return Underdetermined when it fails; the audit could not see it because the canonical eight-layer ontology has no world-space W or observation function Omega, so the property is unstatable rather than false in that theory -- the correct conclusion is a missing ontological layer, not an inexpressible capability; Underdetermined (current-observation-relative) is distinguished from Non-identifiable (an information-theoretic limit that no further observation of the same kind can resolve).

a_rows_sample.statement: Evidence-map table for IV.1: the thin-executable-layer inventory from 3C CF-015 and Tier-2 reads [E]; fail-closed bootstrap behavior from session-bootstrap.php's own header [E]; the 'checks and reports, never installs, never repairs' doctor quote from KnowledgeOsDoctor.php's doc-comment [E]; invariants-as-spec from v0.2 §4 [FA]/[P]; the authority-layer-first pattern from 3C CF-007 and this book [M]/[IN]; and OQ-3/OQ-4 on the implementation path plus OQ-12's missing statement from FA-6 [U].

b_rows_sample.anchor: A governed AI session — Claude or DeepSeek — must be able to resolve its own registered lane / role / workflow state / authority deterministically at session start, from the SAME authoritative state, WITHOUT weakening a single governance rule.
b_rows_sample.statement: AST-017's one-line thesis: any governed AI session, regardless of model provider, must be able to deterministically resolve its own lane/role/state/authority from the single authoritative workflow record without weakening any governance rule; 'Resolution is not activation' — the report creates no authority, ownership, or state change.

b_rows_sample.anchor: AST-017 holds no fold loop, no transition state machine, no state derivation. Every workflow fact comes from AST-015 invoked as a subprocess
b_rows_sample.statement: AMENDMENT 2 delegation contract: AST-017 delegates every workflow fact (assignment, grant, mutation_owner) to AST-015 via askMechanism(fold/identity/authorized); if the mechanism is unavailable the bootstrap fails closed (UNRESOLVABLE) rather than reading records itself.

b_rows_sample.anchor: AST-017 performs exactly ONE raw read, in the named function v3HandoffRead() ... the single HANDOFF-to/from-lane fact
b_rows_sample.statement: The one bounded exception to AST-017's read-only delegation is a single named function reading exactly the HANDOFF-to/from-lane fact directly from the raw record, because no AST-015 read command yet exposes it (open finding V-3); regression S16 poisons the raw record to prove the bootstrap still reports fold-derived truth.

b_rows_sample.anchor: identity ≠ role ≠ eligibility ≠ authorization ≠ ownership ≠ continuation
b_rows_sample.statement: AST-017's output contract is a six-way separation, each a first-class report block: identity (evidence-only, never a grant input per INV-ATTR-1/2), assignment, activation_prerequisites (the G-3 prerequisites, never a status), grant, mutation_owner, gates, continuation, and meta.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Fail-closed mapping: any AMBIGUOUS/UNRESOLVED/UNRESOLVABLE ⇒ operable=false, authorized_to_act=false, current_session_can_continue=false, unresolved_message = missing fact · source · responsible next actor. Never invent; never transition.
b_rows_sample.statement: Every non-RESOLVED verdict collapses to a uniform fail-closed report shape naming the missing fact, its source, and the responsible next actor, and never invents identity/authorization or performs a transition.

b_rows_sample.anchor: $recordedHumanStartAct = $selected['state'] !== 'CREATED'; // AFTER — $recordedHumanStartAct = $selected['state'] === 'ACTIVE';
b_rows_sample.statement: V-1 defect: recorded_human_start_act was derived from 'state !== CREATED', falsely claiming a human START for a lane that reached CANCELLED without ever being STARTED; corrected to derive from 'state === ACTIVE', the fold state AST-015 sets only on START/CONTINUATION.

b_rows_sample.anchor: meta.disambiguation_required rendered describeLanes($candidates) — every discovered candidate, not the ones that actually matched the process selector
b_rows_sample.statement: V-3 defect: the disambiguation message listed every discovered candidate rather than only the ones actually matching the process selector (e.g. listing a non-matching lane V3LANE-C); corrected by tracking an explicit $ambiguousMatches set and rendering only it, verified live to still leave the real a8ce5a39 case AMBIGUOUS without silently selecting a lane.

b_rows_sample.anchor: harness consumers referenced bootstrapping_status; the report emits activation_prerequisites. Mechanism and consumers disagreed.
b_rows_sample.statement: V-5 defect: harness documentation referenced field name bootstrapping_status while the implementation already emitted activation_prerequisites; resolved by canonicalizing activation_prerequisites everywhere (no working code change needed) and pinning a regression asserting bootstrapping_status is never emitted.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Preservation conditions — all eight survive
b_rows_sample.statement: Eight named preservation properties (single-authority AST-015; AST-017 read-only; V-3 exception bounded to one fact; no second fold/engine; provider independence; ambiguity fail-closed; identity evidence-only; human START boundary intact) were each independently checked and all survive the correction; full suite 50/50 · 566 assertions green.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The regressions S-18/S-19/S-20 were read, then independently reconstructed with fresh hermetic fixtures built through AST-015 in temp dirs ... never touching the live store
b_rows_sample.statement: Independent verification methodology: rebuild the falsification fixtures from scratch through the canonical mechanism rather than re-running the author's own regression tests, so that a false-positive shared bug in the original tests could not silently pass twice.

b_rows_sample.anchor: the prior verification artifact self-declares verifier d1612e03; the independent-verification registration attributes it to 8a525719 ... the naming inconsistency should be reconciled before the adoption decision
b_rows_sample.statement: A prior verification artifact and its Governance registration attribute the same act to two different process identities (d1612e03 vs 8a525719); both may be genuine (different producing vs registering processes) but the inconsistency should be reconciled before any adoption decision.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 'no record = ungoverned = free' is forbidden reasoning
b_rows_sample.statement: When a work item is named but no authoritative workflow record yet exists for it, the mechanism reports UNRESOLVABLE rather than treating the absence of a record as freedom to act; nothing can be registered or started until the record exists and a lane is attributed.

b_rows_sample.anchor: FU-1 · The authoritative workflow store is not durable ... .claude/runtime/workflow/*.json is the authoritative record ... A lost or reset working tree loses every governed lane, every recorded human START act, and therefore every attribution the system relies on.
b_rows_sample.statement: The entire governance chain's trust anchor — the transition log every REGISTER/HANDOFF/START in this batch is written into — lives only in a git-ignored working-tree file with no durability mechanism outside it; a lost or reset working tree would lose every governed lane and every recorded human act, sharpening a previously weaker concern about evidence durability into a concern about the durability of the registration mechanism itself.

b_rows_sample.anchor: FU-2 · Identity-label extraction cannot distinguish an assignment from a mention ... a8ce5a39 is the registered actor of S5 and, in S6, merely named in prose ... Both lanes therefore 'reference' a8ce5a39, and the resolver reports AMBIGUOUS
b_rows_sample.statement: AST-017's processLabelsReferenced() merges two semantically different matches (a lane's registered actor vs any hex-shaped token mentioned in free prose, e.g. an independence-disclosure sentence naming a prior actor) into one set, producing a false AMBIGUOUS verdict whose surface grows monotonically as governed lanes accumulate prose referencing prior actors by design; the verdict stays safe (fail-closed) but is reasoned about for the wrong cause.

b_rows_sample.anchor: the label character class includes '.', so a label written immediately before a sentence-ending period is captured with the period ... A lane whose only label carried the period would not be attributable to its own actor at all: the actor would resolve UNRESOLVED despite holding an ACTIVE lane.
b_rows_sample.statement: A narrower artifact of the same extraction regex: a label immediately followed by a sentence-ending period is captured with the trailing period attached, which could in the worst case leave a legitimately ACTIVE lane's own actor resolving UNRESOLVED because its only recorded label form does not match.

group_evidence.why_grouped: labels share the notation 'session-bootstrap.php'

a_rows_sample.anchor: Goal\neq EpistemicContract
a_rows_sample.statement: A goal (e.g. 'Migrate Nexus to the target architecture') does not itself contain all knowledge conditions necessary to execute it safely (e.g. RollbackVerified, FirewallRequirementsKnown are not stated by the goal); therefore Goal ≠ EpistemicContract. States this was already discovered in Step 25D and now needs formalizing.

a_rows_sample.anchor: DeriveContract(G,S)\rightarrow EC_G
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines the conceptual operation DeriveContract(G,S) -> EC_G, where S is the set of governing sources {Constitution, Policy, ADR, Rule, Scope, HumanInstruction, RiskModel, DomainModel, Law, Standard}.

a_rows_sample.anchor: EC\in KnowledgeState
a_rows_sample.statement: The epistemic contract EC is itself an artifact needing identity, version, scope, owner, source, derivation, validity period, authority, and status; therefore EC ∈ KnowledgeState — 'the system needs knowledge to define what knowledge is required.'

a_rows_sample.anchor: EC=(R,\Gamma,A,V)
a_rows_sample.statement: First contract tuple definition: EC=(R,Γ,A,V) where R=requirements, Γ=satisfaction rules, A=authority/provenance, V=validity/version; R={r1,...,rn}, each requirement individually traceable (e.g. r1: RollbackVerified derived via MigrationGoal -> ArchitecturePolicy -> RiskRule -> RollbackVerified).

a_rows_sample.anchor: RequirementLineage
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines RequirementLineage: a traceable derivation tree from Goal through governing artifacts (Architecture Constitution, Security Policy, Migration Risk Rule) to a concrete requirement (Rollback Verification), enabling the system to answer 'why does KnowledgeOS require a rollback test?' with a traced derivation rather than 'the AI thought it was important.'

a_rows_sample.anchor: HumanInstruction\rightarrow Goal/Intent. Then Goal+Governance\rightarrow Contract.
a_rows_sample.statement: A human instruction (e.g. 'Please migrate Nexus next weekend') contributes only Intent/Goal, not an automatic requirement like RollbackVerifiedRequired; requirements arise from Goal+Governance -> Contract, which 'prevents instructions from silently becoming rules.'

a_rows_sample.anchor: Scope=Production... A requirement concerning a development Nexus instance may therefore be NotApplicable
a_rows_sample.statement: Scope must be an explicit contract dimension: a requirement scoped to Production is NotApplicable to a development instance, demonstrated via example.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Suppose the architecture constitution says: Production changes require architectural assurance... r_{architecture-assurance} becomes part of R_G
a_rows_sample.statement: A constitution-derived requirement (architecture-assurance) is 'not an opinion' but a normative consequence of the constitution, illustrating Constitution -> Requirement derivation.

a_rows_sample.anchor: ADR\rightarrow Requirement
a_rows_sample.statement: An ADR fixing TargetArchitecture=ContainerizedNexusPro can satisfy TargetArchitectureKnown if authoritative/current, and may also generate additional derived requirements (e.g. r_container-security) from the target architecture's own security constraints — ADR -> Requirement.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Suppose a risk analysis identifies RISK: DataLoss... The contract can derive RollbackVerified. This is important because the requirement may not come directly from an architecture rule. It may emerge from Goal+Risk.
a_rows_sample.statement: A risk-model-derived requirement path: RISK:DataLoss -> Control:VerifiedRestore -> RollbackVerified, showing requirements can emerge from Goal+Risk rather than only from architecture rules.

a_rows_sample.anchor: CandidateRequirement\neq ContractRequirement
a_rows_sample.statement: Distinguishes valid derivation (Source+Rule -> Requirement) from mere AI suggestion (LLM -> CandidateRequirement): the latter is not automatically binding, giving 'another deterministic assurance boundary': CandidateRequirement ≠ ContractRequirement.

a_rows_sample.anchor: SourceExists? SourceApplicable? AuthorityValid? RuleSatisfied? ... CandidateRequirement\rightarrow ContractRequirement
a_rows_sample.statement: Describes the LLM's role as proposing candidate requirements from unstructured sources (e.g. reading a 300-page policy), which KnowledgeOS records as CandidateRequirement; only after a deterministic/governed check (SourceExists?, SourceApplicable?, AuthorityValid?, RuleSatisfied?) does CandidateRequirement -> ContractRequirement.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Knowledge requirement / Evidence requirement / Validation requirement / Governance requirement / Operational requirement
a_rows_sample.statement: Introduces a five-way requirement-type taxonomy with predicate forms and examples: Knowledge requirement Known(r) (e.g. TargetVersionKnown), Evidence requirement EvidenceExists(r) (e.g. BackupEvidenceAvailable), Validation requirement Validated(r) (e.g. RestoreTestPassed), Governance requirement Authorized(r) (e.g. ArchitectureApprovalGranted), Operational requirement State(r) (e.g. TargetEnvironmentProvisioned).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Epistemic-Governance Contract ... or simply AssuranceContract. I would not rename it yet
a_rows_sample.statement: Because the requirement taxonomy now spans Knowledge+Evidence+Validation+Authorization+State rather than only 'what must be known,' proposes the more precise terms 'Epistemic-Governance Contract' or 'AssuranceContract,' but explicitly declines to rename yet since 'Epistemic Contract' retains conceptual value — records the naming issue rather than resolving it.

a_rows_sample.anchor: EC_{Nexus}=\{r_1,\ldots,r_8\}
a_rows_sample.statement: Worked example contract for Nexus with an 8-row requirement table (current version known, target architecture known, repository inventory verified, backup verified, rollback verified, network requirements resolved, security assessment complete, architecture approval), each tagged by Type and Blocking?=Yes, giving 'Zero something precise to evaluate.'

a_rows_sample.anchor: r_1\land r_2\Rightarrow r_3 ... r_4\lor r_5
a_rows_sample.statement: Requirements may have logical relations: conjunction (BackupExists AND RestoreTestPassed => RollbackCapabilityEstablished) and disjunction (either approved rollback procedure A OR B suffices), concluding 'EpistemicContract is a constraint system.'

a_rows_sample.anchor: BackupExists ... RestoreValidated ... RollbackVerified ... MigrationEligible
a_rows_sample.statement: Requirement dependency graph diagram lets Zero determine not just which requirements are unmet but 'which gap blocks downstream requirements' — e.g. if BackupExists=Unknown, RestoreValidated and RollbackVerified cannot be established, so RootGap=BackupExists rather than three unrelated gaps; described as 'much more efficient' and 'extremely useful for Lord.'

a_rows_sample.anchor: Closed(EC)
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines contract closure: Closed(EC) holds if every requirement has a semantic definition, an authority, a satisfaction rule, applicable scope, validity, and dependency definition; otherwise Closed(EC)=False, becoming 'another assurance gate.'

a_rows_sample.anchor: UndefinedRequirement\Rightarrow InvalidContract
a_rows_sample.statement: An AI-created requirement like r9: SystemMustBe"HighlySecure" with no satisfaction predicate makes Evaluate(K,r9) non-deterministic; therefore UndefinedRequirement => InvalidContract — 'the contract is defective.'

a_rows_sample.anchor: Contract normalization: natural-language sources normalized into canonical requirements like RollbackProcedureExists and RollbackProcedureTested; natural language remains provenance
a_rows_sample.statement: Describes contract normalization: an LLM can help normalize vague natural-language sources ('Make sure the migration is safe') into canonical, structured, executable requirements while the natural language remains provenance.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Until now we have used Zero intuitively as 'the gap between where we are and where we need to be.' We now need to make that statement mathematically precise. The decisive test is: Can Zero(K,G,EC) be computed from the KnowledgeState? If yes, Zero becomes a genuine computational primitive of Knowledg
b_rows_sample.statement: Frames Step 25D's decisive test: can Zero(K,G,EC) be computed from the KnowledgeState, making Zero a genuine computational primitive rather than an AI metaphor.

b_rows_sample.anchor: A conventional system might define Delta=Target-Current. That is insufficient for KnowledgeOS. ... Nexus version known/3.69 known, Rollback verified/unknown, Firewall permitted/conflicting, Architecture approval/missing. There are four fundamentally different situations. Therefore Zero != simple sub
b_rows_sample.statement: Corrects the naive Delta=Target-Current model of Zero using a four-requirement worked example (known/unknown/conflicting/missing), establishing Zero≠simple subtraction — it must compare requirements against epistemic state.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Let the goal be G. The goal induces a set of required knowledge conditions: R_G={r_1,r_2,...,r_n}. For Nexus migration ... r_1=CurrentVersionKnown ... r_7=GovernanceApprovalObtained. This is crucial: Zero cannot be computed from the goal alone. We need the Epistemic Contract that tells us what must
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines the Knowledge Requirement set R_G induced by a goal G (worked with seven Nexus-migration requirements r1-r7), establishing that Zero cannot be computed from the goal alone and requires an Epistemic Contract.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Define EC_G=(R_G,Gamma_G) where R_G = required conditions; Gamma_G = rules determining sufficiency. So EC_G = what must be established + how sufficiency is judged. This gives Zero a formal input.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines the Epistemic Contract EC_G=(R_G,Γ_G) — required conditions plus sufficiency rules — as Zero's formal input.

b_rows_sample.anchor: For each requirement r_i, we evaluate its status against K_t. Define Sat(K_t,r_i). Initially I propose the following state set: S={Satisfied, PartiallySatisfied, Unknown, Insufficient, Conflicted, Stale, Invalid, Prohibited, NotApplicable}. This is already much richer than Boolean logic.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines a nine-value requirement-satisfaction status set (Satisfied, PartiallySatisfied, Unknown, Insufficient, Conflicted, Stale, Invalid, Prohibited, NotApplicable), explicitly richer than Boolean logic.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Suppose Sat(K,r)=False. That could mean: we know it is false; we don't know; evidence conflicts; evidence is stale; evidence was invalidated; governance prohibits the action. These are operationally very different. Therefore Sat != Boolean.
b_rows_sample.statement: Argues Sat≠Boolean: a bare False collapses six operationally distinct situations (known-false, unknown, conflicting, stale, invalidated, prohibited) into one indistinguishable value.

b_rows_sample.anchor: We can define Z_i=Status(K_t,r_i,EC_G). Then Zero(K_t,G,EC_G)={(r_i,Z_i) | r_i in R_G}. This gives us a Zero vector. For example Z(K)=[Satisfied,Satisfied,Unknown,Insufficient,Conflicted,Satisfied,Missing]. Now Zero is computationally representable.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines Zero(K_t,G,EC_G)={(r_i,Z_i)} as a computationally representable 'Zero vector' of per-requirement statuses.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Case A: No evidence exists: Evidence(r)=empty. Status: Unknown. Case B: Governance requires approval, and no approval exists. That is Missing. These are different. So I recommend Missing as a separate status where the requirement itself is an expected governed artifact/action.
b_rows_sample.statement: Distinguishes Unknown (no evidence exists at all) from Missing (an expected governed artifact/action, such as an approval, that does not exist) as two different status values.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Suppose current KnowledgeState contains A_1: NexusVersion=3.69, A_2: RepositoryCount=43, but nothing about rollback. Then Status(r_1)=Satisfied but Status(r_3)=Unknown. If Architecture Board approval is explicitly required and has not been issued: Status(r_7)=Missing. Therefore Zero(K)={r_3:Unknown,
b_rows_sample.statement: Worked Nexus example computing a concrete Zero(K)={r3:Unknown, r7:Missing} from partial knowledge state evidence.

b_rows_sample.anchor: We can therefore define Zero(K,G,EC)=R_G \ Satisfied(K,R_G) but this is only a shorthand. The real result must retain why each requirement is not satisfied. So Zero={Requirement, Status, Evidence, Reason, Dependencies}.
b_rows_sample.statement: Corrects a shorthand set-difference definition of Zero (R_G minus satisfied requirements) into the fuller structured form Zero={Requirement,Status,Evidence,Reason,Dependencies}, retaining why each requirement is unsatisfied.

b_rows_sample.anchor: A Zero item should look conceptually like: Requirement: RollbackVerified; Status: Unknown; SupportingEvidence: none; BlockingReason: no successful restore test; RequiredAction: perform restore test; DecisionCriticality: high. This is already implementable.
b_rows_sample.statement: Gives a concrete implementable structured-Zero-item template with six fields (Requirement, Status, SupportingEvidence, BlockingReason, RequiredAction, DecisionCriticality).

b_rows_sample.anchor: Suppose E_1 supports RollbackVerified=True. Is that enough? Not necessarily. The epistemic contract may require 2 independent tests. Or 1 test witnessed by a designated authority. Or Probability(success)>=0.99. Therefore Satisfied = ContractSpecific.
b_rows_sample.statement: Establishes that satisfaction of a requirement is ContractSpecific — the same supporting evidence may or may not count as satisfied depending on the epistemic contract's own sufficiency rule (independent-test count, witness authority, or probability threshold).

b_rows_sample.anchor: We therefore need Satisfied(K,r,EC) which may invoke the appropriate reasoning model. For example Satisfied(K,r,EC)=RuleEngine(K,r,EC) or =StatisticalCriterion(K,r,EC) or =HumanAuthorization(K,r). This is another reason Zero must not contain one universal inference mechanism.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines the satisfaction predicate Satisfied(K,r,EC) as potentially delegating to RuleEngine, StatisticalCriterion, or HumanAuthorization — reinforcing that Zero must not embed one universal inference mechanism.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Zero should not calculate everything itself. Instead: Zero -> RequirementEvaluation -> AppropriateReasoningModel. ... Zero aggregates the results.
b_rows_sample.statement: Establishes Zero as an orchestrator that dispatches requirement evaluation to the appropriate reasoning model (Rules/Statistics/Authority) and aggregates results, rather than being an inference engine itself.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Operational Zero: Z_W=Distance(W_t,W*) where W* is the target world state. Epistemic Zero: Z_K=Distance(K_t,K*_EC) where K*_EC is the knowledge required by the epistemic contract. These are fundamentally different.
b_rows_sample.statement: Formally splits Operational Zero Z_W=Distance(W_t,W*) from Epistemic Zero Z_K=Distance(K_t,K*_EC), reaffirming the two are fundamentally different quantities.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Target: Nexus Pro running in target environment. Current world: Nexus OSS 3.69 running. Operational gap: Z_W>0. But suppose Target architecture known, Current version known, Backup status unknown, Firewall status unknown, Approval missing. Then Z_K>0. Even if an engineer knows exactly how to perform
b_rows_sample.statement: Worked example showing Z_K (epistemic gap) can independently block execution even when the operational how-to is fully known, illustrating Z_W and Z_K as genuinely separate blocking gaps.

b_rows_sample.anchor: I recommend Zero=(Z_world, Z_knowledge, Z_governance, Z_decision) at the conceptual level. Z_world: What differs in reality? Z_knowledge: What required facts are unknown/uncertain? Z_governance: What required approvals/rules are missing? Z_decision: What prevents a defensible decision? This is much
b_rows_sample.statement: Decomposes Zero into four conceptual dimensions (Z_world, Z_knowledge, Z_governance, Z_decision), each answering a distinct question, stronger than a single scalar distance.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Suppose Z_knowledge=5 and Z_governance=1. Can we say Zero=6? No. The six missing items are not necessarily comparable. One missing governance approval could be more blocking than five low-priority informational gaps. Therefore Zero is primarily a structured object, not a scalar.
b_rows_sample.statement: Counterexample against summing dimension counts into a scalar Zero=6: a single governance gap can outweigh five informational gaps in blocking severity, so Zero must remain primarily a structured object, not a scalar.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Once the structured Zero exists, we may calculate: GapCount. Or CriticalGapCount. Or WeightedGapScore. Or ContractCoverage. For example Coverage(K) = satisfied required conditions / total required conditions. But these are projections of Zero, not Zero itself.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines four derivable scalar projections of the structured Zero object (GapCount, CriticalGapCount, WeightedGapScore, ContractCoverage), explicitly distinguished as projections, not Zero itself.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Each requirement can have Criticality(r) such as {Critical,High,Medium,Low}. But again, we should be careful with arbitrary scores. A critical requirement might be RollbackVerified. If Status=Unknown, then migration could be blocked regardless of all other results. This gives us BlockingCondition.
b_rows_sample.statement: Introduces per-requirement Criticality with a caution against arbitrary scoring, deriving the concept of a BlockingCondition — a single unresolved critical requirement that blocks regardless of all other results.

group_evidence.why_grouped: explicit agent-stated uncertainty: 'epistemic-contract-derivation-algebra' POSSIBLY relates to 'formal-zero-algebra' (batch B0022). Note: S0897's Step 25E: formalizes derivation of the Epistemic Contract EC referenced (but not yet formalized) in Step 25D's Zero(K,EC); requirement types, lineage graph, closure, versioning, temporal/scope validity, and five governance experiments.

a_rows_sample.anchor: We should not jump from multiple Zeros to therefore probability to therefore infinite-dimensional probability space. Those are three separate claims.
a_rows_sample.statement: Explicit warning against conflating three separate, sequentially-testable claims: multidimensional state, need for probability, and state-space cardinality; proposes KR-STATE-01/02/03 as the corresponding disciplined research ladder.

a_rows_sample.anchor: K_t=P_t(\Omega_E)
a_rows_sample.statement: Proposes that knowledge at time t is a probability distribution P_t over the epistemically possible states Omega_E, replacing 'K_t = set of things we know' with a distributional object.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Knowledge Śūnya does not mean probability zero. ... P(x)=0 means something very different from Determine(x)=\varnothing.
a_rows_sample.statement: Distinguishes probability-zero from Determine(x,K_t)=empty from x=empty; a proposition can have nonzero probability mass across several possible truth values while still having no contract-justified determination.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Effect=0 \quad\not\Rightarrow\quad Cause/history=0
a_rows_sample.statement: Reinterprets the Nilakantha containment result inside the probability-space model: the epistemic state can transform so that P(destructive propagation)->0 while P(poison trace)>0.

a_rows_sample.anchor: K_t\equiv(\Omega_E,\mathcal F,P_t,\mathcal H_t)
a_rows_sample.statement: Proposes the candidate signature K_t=(Omega_E, F, P_t, H_t) combining dimensions (what varies) with probability (uncertainty over that space) and history H_t, and a candidate Knowledge Algebra signature KA=(Omega_E,F,P,T,Q,Pi,C,Ch,Gamma,equiv,I).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Does every important KnowledgeOS epistemic transition require uncertainty over alternative states, and if so, what is the minimum mathematical structure needed to represent that uncertainty?
a_rows_sample.statement: Names the next experiment before committing to probability theory as a foundation: whether KnowledgeOS transitions actually require representing uncertainty over alternative states, and what minimal structure suffices.

b_rows_sample.anchor: K subseteq (Omega, F, P) where (Omega,F,P) is an infinite probability space, and a knowledge element is not necessarily a scalar/vector but an element or measurable structure associated with that space. In measure theory, an element of the probability space is normally an outcome omega in Omega. A 'knowledge element' can therefore be modelled as an outcome, random variable, event, measurable function, or probability distribution -- but we must decide which one.
b_rows_sample.statement: Proposes a new measure-theoretic foundation K subseteq (Omega, F, P), an infinite probability space (Omega=possible states/observations, F=measurable events, P=probability measure), replacing the vector-space/topological foundations of prior files. Immediately corrects itself: a 'knowledge element' is ambiguous among at least five candidate mathematical objects (an outcome omega, a random variable, an event, a measurable function, a probability distribution) and this choice must be made explicitly -- flagged as possibly the key to making the theory rigorous.

b_rows_sample.anchor: k: Omega -> K as a knowledge interpretation/mapping. This is much more powerful than simply saying knowledge is a point in a vector space. ... K_t = K(E_{<=t}) where E_{<=t}={E_1,...,E_t}. The knowledge state is therefore not fixed. It is conditional on observations. P(omega|E_{<=t}). KnowledgeOS doesn't simply store what is known. It maintains a probability distribution over possible knowledge states given evidence.
b_rows_sample.statement: Introduces a knowledge interpretation mapping k: Omega -> K and redefines K_t as K(E_{<=t}), conditional on the accumulated evidence sequence E_{<=t}={E_1,...,E_t}, formalized as a conditional probability P(omega|E_{<=t}) -- the core conceptual shift: KnowledgeOS maintains a probability distribution over possible knowledge states given evidence, rather than storing 'what is known' as a fixed fact.

b_rows_sample.anchor: V_i=X_i(omega) for a particular realization omega. But under uncertainty X_i is a random variable, and its value isn't necessarily known. KnowledgeOS may have E[X_i|E_t] and Var(X_i|E_t). So each dimension could have (value, uncertainty) rather than just V_i.
b_rows_sample.statement: Refines the value concept: rather than a bare V_i, each dimension carries a (value, uncertainty) pair, formalized via the conditional expectation E[X_i|E_t] and variance Var(X_i|E_t) of the underlying random variable X_i.

b_rows_sample.anchor: P_t -> P_{t+1} where P_t=P(.|E_{<=t}). New evidence produces P_{t+1}(omega)=P(omega|E_{<=t+1}). This means the Kernel is potentially a probability-distribution transformation engine. ... frakK: (P_t,E_t) -> (P_{t+1},D_{t+1},Pi_{t+1}). The Kernel performs: Observe -> Measure -> Discriminate -> Update -> Validate -> Persist.
b_rows_sample.statement: Reframes knowledge transformation as probability-distribution transformation: P_t -> P_{t+1} (Bayesian conditioning on new evidence), redefining the Kernel as frakK: (P_t,E_t) -> (P_{t+1},D_{t+1},Pi_{t+1}) executing a six-step pipeline: Observe -> Measure -> Discriminate -> Update -> Validate -> Persist -- described as the biggest consequence of the probability-space foundation, making the Kernel 'a probability-distribution transformation engine.'

b_rows_sample.anchor: (Omega,F,P,tau) or an appropriate relationship between measurable and topological structures. Probability -> uncertainty. Measure -> quantification. Topology -> structure/connectivity. Dimension system -> degrees of freedom. Statistics -> inference. Operators -> transformation. DDD -> domain semantics. Gītā lens -> philosophical interpretation. This is beginning to form a coherent multidimensional theory.

b_rows_sample.anchor: I would not yet state as a theorem: knowledge is an element of an infinite probability space, because mathematically we need to decide exactly what knowledge element means. A more rigorous initial statement is: KnowledgeOS models possible knowledge states over an infinite measurable probability space, with knowledge represented by measurable variables, events, assertions, or derived structures conditioned on evidence. Then we can investigate whether a knowledge element itself should formally be omega, or X(omega), or A in F, or P(.|E). That distinction could itself be the next breakthrough. Because once we settle it, we can derive the Kernel's mathematical domain and codomain, and then finally start deriving -- not inventing -- the operator algebra of KnowledgeOS.
b_rows_sample.statement: Refuses to state 'knowledge is an element of an infinite probability space' as a theorem, since 'knowledge element' remains genuinely ambiguous, proposing instead a weaker, more rigorous initial statement: KnowledgeOS models possible knowledge states over an infinite measurable probability space, with knowledge represented by measurable variables, events, assertions, or derived structures conditioned on evidence. Names resolving which formal object a 'knowledge element' actually is (an outcome omega, a random variable X(omega), an event A in F, or a conditional distribution P(.|E)) as potentially the next breakthrough itself, since settling it would let the Kernel's mathematical domain/codomain, and hence its operator algebra, be DERIVED rather than invented.

a_rows_sample.anchor: **The multiplicity burden is driven by the joint extreme-value behaviour of the family, not by pairwise separability.**
a_rows_sample.statement: Restates FR-001's core finding (already frozen and extracted): pairwise semantic/evidential distinguishability cannot by itself carry family-level epistemic complexity, established via two independent failure mechanisms (non-transitivity of the tolerance relation ~_Λ; delta-packing's failure under correlation, up to 222x) — the burden is a property of the family's joint behaviour, not of pairs.

a_rows_sample.anchor: | **C-1** | **Do not put statistical mechanisms into the kernel merely because KnowledgeOS can use them.** ... | **C-2** | **Identity → Distinguishability → Joint behaviour.** ... | **C-3** ... | **C-4** ... | **C-5** |
a_rows_sample.statement: Restates the five standing consequences carried out of FR-001, applying programme-wide: C-1 statistical mechanisms are capabilities, not necessarily irreducible kernel operators; C-2 identity->distinguishability->joint-behaviour, levels 1-2 insufficient for level 3; C-3 ≡sem and family-level complexity remain separate concepts; C-4 a homogeneous test space can conceal a relation-level defect; C-5 good fit on a narrow design space does not imply a structural law.

b_rows_sample.anchor: | **DECISION** | Conceptual choice required | Factivity, ⪰ |
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines six TODO types used to classify all open KnowledgeOS work items: DECISION (conceptual choice), EXPERIMENT (empirical/mathematical test), DEFINITION (formal semantics missing), REDUCTION (determine kernel-essentiality), GOVERNANCE (ratification/adoption), RESEARCH (foundational investigation).

b_rows_sample.anchor: > **Does KnowledgeOS claim truth, or only epistemic warrant?**
b_rows_sample.statement: TODO Group A (Factivity): does KnowledgeOS claim truth, or only epistemic warrant? Sub-todos: define 'knowledge' without truth in its domain (A1), decide factivity (A2), locate factivity as mathematical property/external assumption/architectural boundary/not-required (A3), choose among Rename/Externalize/Hybrid (A4).

b_rows_sample.anchor: The v1.1 witness established that \(K_t = \Gamma(E_t, Q, C, EC)\) cannot simultaneously be an attributive knowledge construction and be factive if truth is absent from Γ's domain.
b_rows_sample.statement: Restates the v1.1 witness finding: K_t=Γ(E_t,Q,C,EC) cannot be simultaneously an attributive construction and factive when truth is absent from Γ's domain; two possible worlds with identical epistemic input but different truth values produce the same epistemic state.

b_rows_sample.anchor: | **Externalize** | Factivity is verified outside the kernel; kernel emits claims | 88.25% survival rate measurable (under tested conditions) |
b_rows_sample.statement: Three factivity-resolution candidates: Rename (A_t=Attributed State, 'Knows' external — honest but weaker), Externalize (factivity verified outside kernel; 88.25% survival rate measured under tested conditions — an experimental result, not an architectural recommendation), Hybrid (some attributed states factive, some not — most complex/expressive).

b_rows_sample.anchor: > **Can contradiction be represented without confusing it with uncertainty, absence, insufficient evidence, or theory incompleteness?**
b_rows_sample.statement: TODO Group B (Contr), status OPEN — NEXT EXPERIMENT, does not depend on Factivity: can contradiction be represented without confusing it with uncertainty, absence, insufficient evidence, or theory incompleteness? Sub-todos B1-B4: run the contradiction experiment against four candidates, define Contr semantics, define Zero under contradiction, resolve minimum evaluation domain (C may or may not emerge).

b_rows_sample.anchor: `Sat_content` is not a function on contradictory states. Both \(p \in K\) and \(\neg p \in K\) can hold simultaneously. The current codomain `{T, F, U}` cannot represent this.
b_rows_sample.statement: Sat_content is not a well-defined function on contradictory states: both p∈K and ¬p∈K can hold simultaneously, and the current three-value codomain {T,F,U} cannot represent this.

b_rows_sample.anchor: | **Structured Evaluation** | `EVal = (value, reason, provenance)` | Most expressive; keeps contradiction distinct |
b_rows_sample.statement: Four candidate resolutions for the contradiction/evaluation-domain problem: Fourth Value (add C to codomain, changes whole evaluation algebra), Delegate to Consistency (Sat_content returns U on contradiction, makes content depend on a blocked class), Exclusive by Construction (⊥≡(¬p∈K∧p∉K), silently loses the contradiction), Structured Evaluation (EVal=(value,reason,provenance), most expressive, keeps contradiction distinct).

b_rows_sample.anchor: > **Determine the minimum evaluation domain required** — then `C` may emerge, or may not. Do not let the simulator force the theory to supply a value merely because the simulator needs one.
b_rows_sample.statement: States a methodological principle guarding against a specific failure mode: determine the minimum evaluation domain required for contradiction semantics first; do not let implementation/simulator needs force the theory to manufacture a value it does not independently require.

b_rows_sample.anchor: > **How does KnowledgeOS order epistemic progress?**
b_rows_sample.statement: TODO Group C (⪰, progress ordering): how does KnowledgeOS order epistemic progress? 1,491 claims specify no ordering; progress is meaningless without one. Sub-todos C1-C5: define what is ordered, define x⪰y explicitly, determine order type (preorder/partial/total/preference/dominance/admissibility), keep admissibility≠ranking≠selection explicit, allow multiple orderings (accuracy/coverage/decision/robustness).

b_rows_sample.anchor: > There may be **no universal total ordering**. Progress may be multi-dimensional.
b_rows_sample.statement: Hypothesizes that there may be no universal total ordering of epistemic progress in KnowledgeOS; progress may instead be irreducibly multi-dimensional.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The Linga-Yoni experiment showed that generation ≠ progress. A system can change without improving.
b_rows_sample.statement: Restates a finding attributed to the (prior-batch) Linga-Yoni experiment: generation is not progress — a system can change state without that change constituting improvement, motivating the need for an explicit progress ordering.

b_rows_sample.statement: States that reduction plausibly requires more than semantic equivalence alone: equivalence + required invariants + observability + adequacy + operational preservation may all be jointly necessary (this same composite requirement recurs verbatim under TODO Group I).

a_rows_sample.anchor: CR-1 — Contr: what is contradiction predicated of, and does it explode?
a_rows_sample.statement: Formal conflict record: signature alternatives (proposition / proposition-pair / state-proposition-pair / scope) and consequence alternatives (GlobalInvalidity vs LocalConflict) are independent axes; constraining evidence exists (KR-CONTR-EVAL: no flat domain of any cardinality is adequate; KR-CONTR-FDE: FDE preserves all five DirectContradiction|X pairs but collapses two boundary distinctions; five non-collapse constraints) but nothing selects a resolution; DECISION REQUIRED on both the signature and the explosion policy.

a_rows_sample.anchor: CR-2 — ⪰: one ordering, or several kept apart?
a_rows_sample.statement: Three orderings (state progress K_{t+1}>=_EC K_t, evidence-strength ES_Kt(p)>=s_min, and refinement/subsumption C⊑_S D) are shown to have different mathematical types (state preorder vs scalar threshold vs structural relation), with the corpus itself stating 'two independent paths exist and must stay independent'; cost of leaving it open is measured at 83% of progress claims (1491/1793) specifying no ordering and 0 of 5 axes ordered in one prior experiment; DECISION REQUIRED on whether >= is one relation or a typed family.

a_rows_sample.anchor: CR-3 — δ: reactive or commanded, total or partial?
a_rows_sample.statement: Event-indexed delta(K_t,e_t) (reactive) vs operation-indexed delta(K,o) (commanded) are genuinely competing and interact with the estate's own Command!=Transformation result (I-C); a third, orthogonal axis adds a Reject(r) codomain branch found explicitly in two corpus files; the executed 'commit case' finding (Gamma is derived, not a component of K, so delta has nowhere to write; K1 is K0) is a defect under all three choices and is not resolved by choosing among them; DECISION REQUIRED on event-vs-operation and total-vs-partial-with-Reject.

a_rows_sample.statement: CLOSURE-4's executable definition is a correct definition of a different relation in a seven-relation structure (K's approx_obs slot, not its equiv_sem slot); CLOSURE-4 was declared CLOSED/RATIFIED but two independent reviews and every later register call it open/too-strong/unsupported, and the rejection has temporal precedence and is unanswered; the cheapest, nearly self-resolving decision — adopt A as approx_{Q,Gamma,O} and leave equiv_sem open, or keep both open.

a_rows_sample.statement: Four incompatible Qualify signatures are catalogued with four different codomains (Evidence-constructor; a four-valued classifier including a substantive 'Terminus' value meaning justification may legitimately terminate; an EpistemicStatus-evaluator from five inputs; and the differently-framed Knowledge Qualification Problem Phi:Khat_t->{Knowledge,Not-Knowledge}); judged the most consequential because the codomain choice is prior to any derivation, making 'derive Qualify' not yet a well-posed task.

b_rows_sample.statement: A 12-link dependency chain (Theory -> canonical concepts -> formal definitions -> invariants -> operations -> state transitions -> contracts/specs -> architecture -> implementation) is shown to break at the second link because four rival vocabularies exist for K with only an unratified characterized relation between two of them; every link below is downstream of that break plus five conflict records.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Five of the seven are GOVERNANCE ACTS, not derivations. ... A sub-kernel — hold a graph, compute lineage, check structural equality, detect orphans — is implementable today. It is not the KnowledgeOS kernel, and shipping it must not be reported as one.
b_rows_sample.statement: Names seven ordered blockers (the carrier OQ-1, Qualify's codomain CR-5, delta's argument type CR-3, Contr's signature/policy CR-1, the ordering relation CR-2, DECISION-02 OQ-2, and the equiv_sem naming CR-4) and states the programme is blocked on choices no derivation is entitled to make, not on mathematics it cannot do; explicitly distinguishes an implementable 'sub-kernel' (lineage/equality/orphan/identity) from the actual KnowledgeOS kernel and warns against reporting the former as the latter.

group_evidence.why_grouped: labels share the notation 'CR-1..CR-5'

a_rows_sample.anchor: The document contains many useful conceptual correspondences between Bhagavad-gītā Chapter 4 and KnowledgeOS, but most of the displayed equations are not mathematical derivations from the verses. They are newly invented quantitative models. Several are mathematically under-specified, and some are outright invalid as stated.
a_rows_sample.statement: A systematic mathematical audit of S1321 rejects its central framing claim (that Chapter 4 provides a 'complete mathematical foundation' culminating in a formula for KnowledgeOS) and works through specific defects: exponential knowledge decay K_t^decayed = K_0*e^(-lambda*t) has no basis in the verses and lambda is never defined from observations, so 'lineage = useful architectural lens' but 'exponential decay = invented hypothesis'; the memory integral M(t) = integral_0^t K(tau) dtau is unjustified unless K(tau) is defined as measurable and the measure and meaning of integration are specified, and is replaced by a cleaner subset relation AccessibleHistory_t subset-or-equal HistoricalState_t; the intervention threshold I(t)=1 iff Delta(K_t,I_t)>theta invents an arbitrary scalar threshold with no textual basis, so 'condition-triggered intervention' is retained as a research lens while 'the specific threshold equation' is rejected as a derivation; the multiple-evidence-paths summation (sum W_i = Total Evidence) is judged particularly problematic because the corpus's own EXP-01 work already established that dependency and evidence relationships matter before aggregation and a simple sum can double-count dependent evidence, so the formula is 'not acceptable as an evidence calculus without a dependence model'; the Faith(K_t)=Confidence(K_t)/Uncertainty(K_t) ratio is rejected because it requires undefined semantics for both quantities and becomes undefined when Uncertainty=0 (the code's return of infinity is called 'a programming convention, not a mathematical derivation'); the wise-state vector W=(0,0,C,infinity) is rejected as not a valid mathematical structure until the vector space, coordinates, codomain, and whether infinity is legitimate in that space are all defined, and should be treated as metaphorical notation; and the final closing equation KnowledgeOS = Wisdom*Action/(Doubt+Attachment) is rejected outright: no defined units or domains, no derivation, no normalization, no reason KnowledgeOS should be a scalar, a possibly-zero denominator, and not following from any prior equation -- called 'a metaphorical synthesis presented in equation form,' exactly what the mathematical verification protocol must prevent.

a_rows_sample.anchor: `is_verified() = true` cannot simply mean "true knowledge." The document collapses precisely the distinction our architecture worked hard to preserve.
a_rows_sample.statement: Further specific defects identified in S1321: the reward function R(K) treating knowledge.is_verified() as a truth oracle collapses the architecture's own load-bearing distinctions (Evidence != Determination; Accepted != Truth), and is judged a major epistemic issue, not a minor one; the Guna-to-Dimension mapping (Sattva->Knowledge, Rajas->Action, Tamas->Material) and the non-doer Agency(A)=Actor!=Executor claim are not mathematically derived and are philosophical analogy only, which should never be promoted into the architecture without independent evidence; the non-attachment derivative Attachment(A) = partial(Outcome)/partial(Expectation) is called a classic example of 'mathematical decoration replacing mathematical derivation,' since outcome-as-differentiable-function, units, and domain are all undefined; the action/inaction dual-state additive model A_t = A_physical + A_mental is under-defined (what does addition mean; are physical and mental actions elements of the same algebra) though its underlying conceptual distinction (ObservedExecution != ActionSemantics) is judged genuinely useful; and the learning function K_{t+1}=K_t+L(K_t,Teacher) with Teacher=argmax(Trust*Knowledge) requires many unstated assumptions (K supports addition, teacher knowledge is commensurable with learner state, trust and knowledge are both scalar) though the underlying lens (knowledge acquisition mediated through a source/teacher relationship) is reasonable.

a_rows_sample.anchor: I concur with the audit's assessment. ... The audit identifies 17 specific mathematical problems. I accept all of them. Below, I provide the corrected formulation.
a_rows_sample.statement: A formal corrective ruling (dated 2026-08-28, status ACCEPTED AS CORRECTIVE, authority 'Senior Mathematician/Statistician Review') accepts all 17 mathematical problems identified in the audit of S1321, and adopts a five-level status vocabulary to prevent future conflation: conceptual lens (valid, e.g. 'provenance matters'), research hypothesis (valid, e.g. 'action semantics depend on epistemic context'), architectural candidate (valid, e.g. 'accessible history != total history'), metaphorical analogy (analogy only, e.g. Guna -> Dimensions), and mathematical derivation (invalid unless actually proven, e.g. the exponential decay formula). The ruling reclassifies the whole S1321 document from '[implicitly] new architecture' to a non-authoritative research artifact, with a recommended document path research/external/deepseek/gita-chapter-4-conceptual-lenses.md and a final status of PROPOSED, NON-AUTHORITATIVE, RESEARCH HYPOTHESES.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Provenance(A) ≠ ∅ ⇒ Established(A) may hold ... AccessibleHistory(A_t, H_t) ⊆ H_t ... Condition(K_t, G_t, I_t) ⇒ Intervention
a_rows_sample.statement: The corrective ruling replaces six of S1321's equations with corrected, non-quantitative reformulations, each explicitly typed as a research hypothesis or invariant candidate, not a derived theorem: provenance (replacing exponential decay) becomes Provenance(A) != empty-set => Established(A) may hold, an invariant candidate rather than a decay law; memory/history (replacing the integral M(t)) becomes AccessibleHistory(A_t, H_t) subset-or-equal H_t, a set-theoretic relation; intervention (replacing the threshold equation) becomes Condition(K_t, G_t, I_t) => Intervention, a relational trigger with the condition explicitly not specified as a threshold; multiple evidence paths (replacing the weighted sum) becomes a set of approaches {Path_1,...,Path_n} plus the explicit requirement that evidence aggregation must account for dependency between pathways; action/inaction duality (replacing the additive model) becomes the semantic relation ObservedAction != ActionMeaning, with Semantics(Action_t) = f(K_t, Context_t, Authorization_t, Intention_t); and faith/doubt (replacing the ratio) becomes Faith and Doubt as elements of an EpistemicState set, explicitly not necessarily reciprocal or ratio-scaled; the wise-person state (replacing the vector with an infinite component) becomes a labelled attribute record (expectations: None, fears: None, contentment: Present, peace: Complete) rather than a coordinate tuple.

a_rows_sample.anchor: "Conceptual Lenses (Validated as Useful)". I would change that wording. We should say: **Conceptual Lenses — Accepted as Research Candidates** ... the Gītā material establishes the *textual/philosophical pattern*, but it does not establish that the pattern is a correct KnowledgeOS architectural principle.
a_rows_sample.statement: Agrees in substance with the prior corrective ruling's core distinction (the DeepSeek Chapter-4 document is valuable research material but not a mathematical derivation of KnowledgeOS) and endorses its four-stage pipeline (Gita concept -> observed structural property -> abstract pattern -> research hypothesis -> possible KnowledgeOS correspondence) as mathematically and epistemically sound, in place of the rejected Gita concept -> equation -> architecture shortcut. Proposes one wording refinement: the ruling's table header 'Conceptual Lenses (Validated as Useful)' should be changed to 'Conceptual Lenses -- Accepted as Research Candidates' (or 'Considered Useful for Further Investigation'), because the Gita material establishes only a textual/philosophical pattern, not that the pattern is a correct KnowledgeOS architectural principle -- illustrated with AccessibleHistory(A_t,H_t) subset-or-equal H_t, a reasonable abstraction that the Gita does not mathematically prove and KnowledgeOS has not yet ratified.

a_rows_sample.anchor: That equation has no derivation, no defined units, no established scalar semantics, and no relationship to the ratified KnowledgeOS model. Rejecting it is absolutely correct.
a_rows_sample.statement: Explicitly reaffirms which prior formulations to retain and which to reject. Retained as genuinely promising research lines: provenance/lineage as a transmission chain A -> S_0 -> S_1 -> ... -> S_n; history vs accessibility (H_t^accessible subset-or-equal H_t^total), called one of the strongest candidates because it connects directly to the distinction between actual state, observation, and available knowledge; purpose-conditioned intervention (Condition(K_t,G_t,I_t) => Intervention), judged a better abstraction than the earlier arbitrary threshold equation; action semantics (ObservedAction != ActionMeaning, and Semantics(Action_t) = f(K_t,Context_t,Authorization_t,Intention_t)), particularly relevant to the existing open question OQ-4; and faith/doubt as non-scalar epistemic dimensions rather than a ratio. Explicitly reaffirmed as rejected: the exponential decay formula, the memory integral M(t), the weighted evidence sum, the wise-state vector with an infinite component, and especially the final closing equation KnowledgeOS = Wisdom*Action/(Doubt+Attachment) -- which has no derivation, no defined units, no established scalar semantics, and no relationship to the ratified KnowledgeOS model.

a_rows_sample.anchor: I would **not ask Claude to incorporate this document into Edition 2 now**. Instead, save it exactly as the external research artifact, with the corrective classification attached.
a_rows_sample.statement: Final ruling: ACCEPT the corrective methodology (four-stage pipeline); ACCEPT the conceptual lenses as research candidates (not 'validated'); REJECT the unsupported equations as derivations; DO NOT promote any of them to architecture yet. The document should not be incorporated into Edition 2 now; instead it should be saved as an external research artifact (status: EXTERNAL RESEARCH, NON-AUTHORITATIVE, CONCEPTUAL LENSES, HYPOTHESES), with the corrective classification attached, and a seven-stage discipline preserved before anything could enter architecture: Gita source -> textual interpretation -> structural abstraction -> KnowledgeOS research hypothesis -> mathematical test -> architecture test -> governance decision. After the ongoing Part III mathematical/architectural audit, the Gita-derived hypotheses should be compared against the formal KnowledgeOS model to identify convergences, tensions, and genuinely new questions.

a_rows_sample.anchor: **Knowledge is operationally incomplete if it cannot support discrimination between permissible and impermissible action.** ... **Wisdom is an ongoing discriminative activity, not a stored possession.**
a_rows_sample.statement: Chapter 4's wisdom pattern (knowledge/wisdom -> discernment -> what-should/should-not-be-done -> right action) is interpreted architecturally as: knowledge is operationally incomplete if it cannot support discrimination between permissible and impermissible action -- with emphasis on the word 'support', explicitly not claiming that wisdom decides everything, since the architecture deliberately separates Evidence, Determination, Proposal, Decision, Authorization, and Action. The Gita insight is argued to reinforce this separation rather than replace it: wisdom is an ongoing discriminative activity, not a stored possession, suggesting a possible research-stage reformulation Determination -> Discrimination -> Proposal rather than treating knowledge as something that simply sits static in K_t. Explicitly marked as a research hypothesis, not yet a change to architecture.

a_rows_sample.anchor: the verses concerning action, inaction, and forbidden action are essentially saying that **mere observable activity is insufficient to classify action**. ... $$\text{Observed activity} \neq \text{Action meaning} \neq \text{Action consequence}$$
a_rows_sample.statement: Sharpens the action/inaction/forbidden-action reading into a three-way distinction: Observed activity != Action meaning != Action consequence, directly relevant to the unresolved open question OQ-4, and proposes a research-stage formalization ActionMeaning = f(K_t, Purpose, Intention, Authorization, Context) as more valuable than a bare equation like 'Karma = Action'. Also proposes that Chapter 4 supplies an independent philosophical rationale, not an architectural source, for an existing KnowledgeOS non-collapse principle: Evidence != Determination != Decision != Authorization != Execution -- 'a knowledge system should not move directly from available information to execution without a discriminative stage.' This is framed as a stronger intellectual relationship than manufacturing architecture from scripture: the philosophy independently challenges and illuminates the architecture.

a_rows_sample.anchor: DeepSeek's original document tried to do: Gītā verse → KnowledgeOS object → equation → code. We should instead do: Gītā verse / philosophical teaching → philosophical principle → abstract principle → KnowledgeOS question → architecture comparison → mathematical formalization → hypothesis → test
a_rows_sample.statement: Proposes replacing DeepSeek's original four-step pipeline (Gita verse -> KnowledgeOS object -> equation -> code, i.e. S1321's method) with an eight-step pipeline: Gita verse/philosophical teaching -> philosophical principle -> abstract principle -> KnowledgeOS question -> architecture comparison -> mathematical formalization -> hypothesis -> test, worked through end-to-end on one example (wisdom discriminates action from non-action -> a knowledge system should support action discrimination, not merely information accumulation -> does K_t->Zero->Proposal->Decision adequately represent action discrimination -> is there a missing explicit distinction between possible action and appropriate action -> only after investigation, a possible formalization D(K_t,G,Policy) -> {PermissibleActions, ImpermissibleActions}, explicitly labelled research, not architecture). Recommends continuing the whole Chapter-4 effort not as 'deriving KnowledgeOS from Chapter 4' but as building a 'Gita -> Philosophy -> Architecture Inquiry', testing philosophical principles against Determination, Proposal, Decision, Authorization, Action, Governance, OQ-4, and the architecture's non-collapse invariants -- framed as potentially more profound than a one-to-one mapping: Chapter 4 as an independent philosophical stress test of the KnowledgeOS theory of action and decision.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Problem-first ... ✅ Confirmed | Conflict of frames ... ✅ Confirmed | State vs. Frame ... ✅ Confirmed | Equanimity ... ✅ Not reduced | Action relational ... ⚠️ OPEN | Duty ≠ Action ... ⚠️ Candidate | Non-attachment ... ⚠️ Candidate | Yajña ... ✅ Transformation | Provenance ... ✅ Confirmed | Knowledge-Action ... ✅ Confirmed
a_rows_sample.statement: A ten-item test matrix runs each philosophical principle against the actual architecture, each with a textual observation, abstract principle, KnowledgeOS hypothesis, architectural candidate formula, and a test question: (1) problem-first architecture (Information != Determination) -- confirmed, the architecture begins with Knower+Goal+IdealState; (2) conflict of valid frames (Missing != Unknown != Conflicted) -- confirmed, Zero includes Conflict as a first-class object; (3) state vs frame (State != Frame) -- confirmed, Knower/Purpose/IdealState/KnowledgeState are kept separate; (4) equanimity vs signal magnitude (Decision != argmax Utility) -- confirmed, Decision is separated from Action and requires Authorization; (5) action is relational (Meaning(Action_t)=f(Purpose,Role,Context,Policy,Consequences)) -- OPEN, this maps directly onto the existing open question OQ-4; (6) duty != action (Possible != Permissible != Required) -- candidate, the action vocabulary is judged under-specified; (7) non-attachment (Action != Outcome != ExpectedOutcome) -- candidate, the outcome-vs-expectation comparison is under-specified; (8) yajna as transformation (KnowledgeOS is a transformation system, not a repository, S_{t+1}=T(S_t,Event_t,Policy_t)) -- confirmed, already defined in the architecture; (9) provenance and lineage -- confirmed, Provenance is a first-class object; (10) knowledge-action transformation (Action=Execute(Decision,Knowledge,Context,Authorization)) -- confirmed.

a_rows_sample.anchor: ### Weak Point 1: Action Semantics (OQ-4) ... ### Weak Point 2: Action Vocabulary ... `Possible` ... `Permissible` ... `Recommended` ... `Decided` ... `Authorized` ... `Executed` ... ### Weak Point 3: The Feedback Loop
a_rows_sample.statement: Three weak points in the architecture are independently highlighted by the Gita-derived philosophy: (1) action semantics -- OQ-4 is open, action/execution semantics are under-specified, judged a strong candidate for architectural refinement; (2) action vocabulary -- since Possible != Permissible != Required in the text, a six-stage action-status vocabulary is recommended: Possible (technically feasible), Permissible (allowed by policy), Recommended (suggested by Sarathi), Decided (selected by the Knower), Authorized (approved by governance), Executed (actually performed); (3) the feedback loop -- since Action != Outcome != ExpectedOutcome in the text, the feedback loop should be strengthened to Action -> Outcome -> Compare with Expectation -> New Knowledge State.

a_rows_sample.anchor: **Wisdom is the active capacity to discriminate among possible actions in relation to purpose, duty, consequences and knowledge.** ... this suggests that what we currently call **Proposal** may be one component of a larger **discernment process**.
a_rows_sample.statement: Proposes 'discernment' as a candidate concept deeper than mere Knowledge: Wisdom = Knowledge + Discrimination + Appropriate Action, explicitly not proposed as an architecture equation, restated more carefully as 'wisdom is the active capacity to discriminate among possible actions in relation to purpose, duty, consequences and knowledge.' Raises the research question of where KnowledgeOS performs this function, along the existing chain KnowledgeState -> Zero/discrepancy -> Determination -> Proposal -> Decision, suggesting that what the architecture currently calls Proposal may be only one component of a larger discernment process -- flagged as worth investigating, not resolved here.

a_rows_sample.anchor: **Technical ability to perform an action does not establish normative permission to perform it.** ... $$Capability \neq Authority$$ ... That could be valuable for AI agents.
a_rows_sample.statement: Derives from Chapter 3's repeated framing of action in relation to duty/context/role/consequences a candidate invariant: technical ability to perform an action does not establish normative permission to perform it (Action != Permission; Capability != Authority) -- explicitly noted as stronger than the existing Decision != Authorization separation because it introduces a prior stage, Capability. Applied to an AI-safety scenario: an AI agent's technical ability to call delete(), deploy(), approve(), publish(), or modify-policy() does not mean Authorized(Action)=True, and even authorization does not mean Action=AppropriateAction. Proposes a richer AI-safety action chain: Capability -> Proposal -> Determination -> Decision -> Authorization -> Execution -> Observation, framed as a place where Gita philosophy and KnowledgeOS architecture can have a meaningful dialogue without either deriving the other.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Doubt_t = f(Conflict_t, Missing_t, Ambiguity_t, InsufficientEvidence_t, CompetingFrames_t) ... **Should doubt be represented as a derived condition over unresolved epistemic discrepancies rather than as a scalar?**
a_rows_sample.statement: Reading Chapter 1's paralysis-from-unresolved-conflict together with Chapter 4's call to cut doubt and act, hypothesizes that doubt is not simply the complement of confidence but a function of multiple unresolved epistemic conditions: Doubt_t = f(Conflict_t, Missing_t, Ambiguity_t, InsufficientEvidence_t, CompetingFrames_t) -- explicitly contrasted with and preferred over the earlier rejected formula Doubt = 1 - Confidence (from S1321, the DeepSeek document). Poses the research question directly: should doubt be represented as a derived condition over unresolved epistemic discrepancies rather than as a scalar?

a_rows_sample.anchor: we may discover that the Gītā-derived philosophy independently highlights the **same weak points** Claude's archaeological and mathematical work is finding—particularly **state continuity, action semantics, determination, conflict, provenance, authority, and transformation**.
a_rows_sample.statement: Proposes explicitly comparing the emerging Gita-derived research track against the corpus's own formal findings registers (PF-1..PF-9, AF-F-1..AF-F-23, MV-F-1..MV-F-22), hypothesizing that the philosophically-derived weak points would independently converge on the same architectural weak points the mathematical/archaeological audit work separately finds -- named specifically as state continuity, action semantics, determination, conflict, provenance, authority, and transformation. Framed as a much stronger result than claiming the Gita 'contains KnowledgeOS': independent convergence between two unrelated methodologies (philosophical reading vs formal mathematical audit) would be more persuasive than either alone.

a_rows_sample.anchor: This remains **outside the architecture**. We should eventually save the DeepSeek material as external research and build the more rigorous research track we discussed
a_rows_sample.statement: Confirms the project-level disposition of the Gita/DeepSeek research thread as of this snapshot: it remains explicitly outside the ratified architecture, to be saved as external research material and pursued via the more rigorous pipeline discussed elsewhere in this batch (Gita -> philosophical principle -> abstract pattern -> KnowledgeOS question -> mathematical/architectural test), rather than the rejected Gita -> equation -> architecture shortcut -- and the Chapters 1-4 work is explicitly permitted to continue independently of the book production schedule.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Reality ≠ Observation ≠ Information ≠ Evidence ≠ Knowledge ≠ Decision ≠ Action.
b_rows_sample.statement: Axiom A1 (Semantic Separation) opens Part I of the v2.0 rewrite: reality, observation, information, evidence and knowledge are held to occupy different semantic roles unless a formal equivalence is explicitly established, giving the epistemic lifecycle Reality->Observation->Information->Knowledge->Gap->Inquiry->Determination->Decision->Action->New Knowledge.

b_rows_sample.anchor: If there exist ω1,ω2 ∈ Ω such that ω1≠ω2 and ρ(ω1)=ρ(ω2), then ρ is not injective and therefore cannot uniquely identify the underlying state of reality.
b_rows_sample.statement: Proposition 3.1 with proof: an observation map rho:Omega->I need not be injective, so KnowledgeOS must never silently infer Observed(x)=>Reality(x).

b_rows_sample.anchor: Adequate(R,Q,Γ) ⟺ 𝓡_req(Q,Γ) ⊆ Dist(R)
b_rows_sample.statement: The Representation Adequacy Principle: a representation is adequate only if it preserves the distinctions required to answer the declared inquiry under context Gamma, avoiding the impossible requirement of preserving every conceivable distinction.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Suppose there exist x1,x2 ∈ X such that x1≠x2 but π(x1)=π(x2). Then any question Q whose required distinction includes x1≠x2 cannot, in general, be answered correctly from π(x) alone.
b_rows_sample.statement: Theorem 16.1 (Loss of Required Distinction), with proof by the impossibility of a deterministic function distinguishing two values a projection maps identically; establishes that a system can be perfectly internally consistent and still epistemically inadequate.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Δ_t = {r ∈ Req_t : ¬Sat(K_t,r)} ... Gap = Unsatisfied Requirements.
b_rows_sample.statement: Redefines the Knowledge Gap as a set-theoretic construction (unsatisfied requirements under the current epistemic contract) rather than a subtraction Delta=IdealKnowledge-Knowledge, explicitly rejecting the latter as generally undefined because the two objects need not belong to a common algebraic space.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Zero(K_t,EC_t) ⟺ Δ_t = ∅ ... Therefore Zero is contract-relative.
b_rows_sample.statement: Definition 23.1 (Epistemic Zero): Zero means no requirement of the declared epistemic contract remains unsatisfied; explicitly not K_t=Reality and not 'all possible knowledge is known.'

b_rows_sample.anchor: Δ_{t+1} ⊆ Δ_t ... every requirement satisfied at t remains satisfied at t+1 ... This theorem depends on the contract remaining fixed.
b_rows_sample.statement: Theorems 24.1 (Zero Equivalence) and 25.1 (Gap Reduction) are proved, with an explicit limitation that gap comparison across differing contracts (EC_t != EC_{t+1}) requires an explicit compatibility mapping — 'moving the goalposts' is formally blocked by the Contract Compatibility principle GapComparison=>ContractCompatibility.

b_rows_sample.anchor: V(K_t) ⊆ V(K_{t+1}) ∧ H(K_t) ⊆ H(K_{t+1}) ... Historical existence ≠ Current epistemic standing.
b_rows_sample.statement: Axiom A6 (Historical Preservation) plus the constitutional distinction between historical existence and current epistemic standing: a proposition can move Supported->Retracted without deleting the historical fact that it was once asserted and supported; replaces 'universal epistemic monotonicity' with this weaker, correct invariant.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Truth ≠ Evaluation ≠ Determination ≠ Decision.
b_rows_sample.statement: Axiom A2 (Epistemic Pipeline Separation), with the worked consequence that EVal(p)=Supported does not mean Decision=Permit (a governance policy may instead require HumanReview) — epistemic status is explicitly not equivalent to operational authorization.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Contr(p) ⇏ ∀q ∈ 𝒫, q. ... Local contradiction ⇏ Global epistemic collapse.
b_rows_sample.statement: Axiom A5 (Non-Explosion): KnowledgeOS explicitly rejects the classical explosion principle as a system rule, requiring contradiction to be scoped and represented rather than collapsing all propositions.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 𝒪_core = {ASSERT, LINK, REVISE, RETRACT, ISOLATE}
b_rows_sample.statement: Names the frozen candidate core operation interface (introduce an assertion, establish a relation, change content while preserving history, withdraw standing without erasing history, and restrict propagation of a contradiction or dangerous structure), with full preconditions/postconditions/composition laws deferred to later parts.

b_rows_sample.anchor: ABK-1 is a validated candidate-adequate architecture for the target problem class.
b_rows_sample.statement: Explicitly withdraws the earlier claim that ABK-1 is 'the universally unique minimal KnowledgeOS kernel' as circular, replacing it with the weaker, defensible claim that global minimality remains unproven unless the candidate representation space and equivalence relation are formally characterized.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Ontology defines what kinds of things KnowledgeOS reasons about. Representation defines how those things are encoded.
b_rows_sample.statement: States the ontology/representation boundary underlying Part II's many-sorted type system (Ent, Val, Attr, Dim, Prop, Asrt, Obs, Evd, Src, Rel, Evt, St, Ctx, Part, Prov, ES, Req, Inq, EC, Pol, Dec, Act), asserting a database/graph/JSON/RDF/object-model representation is never the ontology itself.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Let D be a value domain and n:D→ℝ a numerical encoding. If no semantic operation corresponding to subtraction is defined on D, then n(x)−n(y) cannot ... be interpreted as a valid semantic difference.
b_rows_sample.statement: Theorem 2.1 (Representation does not imply arithmetic validity), with proof, establishing that numerical computability of a difference does not by itself establish semantic validity of that difference.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Supports(e,p) ⇏ Truth(p).
b_rows_sample.statement: Proposition 2.1, proved by the type-mismatch argument that support is an epistemic evidence-proposition relation while truth is a semantic proposition-model relation with different domains and meanings; called one of the most important anti-confusion principles in KnowledgeOS.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Let R:𝕂→X be a representation function. Suppose there exist K1≠K2 such that R(K1)=R(K2). If there exists an inquiry Q such that Answer(Q,K1,Γ)≠Answer(Q,K2,Γ), then R is inadequate for Q,Γ.
b_rows_sample.statement: Theorem 2.3 (Semantically lossy representation), with proof, generalizing Part I's Theorem 16.1 to the knowledge-state level and formally establishing why representation adequacy must be question-relative.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Status_Γ,EC(p)=σ ... We deliberately do not define one universal ordered list such as Unknown<Supported<Proven<Rejected.
b_rows_sample.statement: Epistemic Status is defined as contract- and context-dependent rather than a single universal total order, giving formal meaning to 'unknown' as neither true nor false rather than as a weaker degree of falsity.

b_rows_sample.anchor: If Conflict is represented as a local relation on propositions, then the existence of a conflict concerning p does not by itself entail conflict concerning arbitrary q.
b_rows_sample.statement: Theorem 2.5 (Locality theorem for contradiction), with proof, giving the formal ontological grounding for the non-explosion axiom stated in Part I.

b_rows_sample.anchor: KnowledgeOS SHALL NOT treat stored data as knowledge merely because it is stored.
b_rows_sample.statement: Ten Foundational Type Invariants (I1-I10) close Part II — proposition/evidence separation, observation/proposition separation, decision/action separation, epistemic-status/truth separation, identity/state separation, evidence/truth separation, contract relativity, historical preservation, non-explosion, and representation independence — as the boundaries preventing KnowledgeOS from collapsing into an ordinary information system.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Truth → Evidence → Evaluation → Determination → Decision ... The arrows indicate dependency possibilities, not logical equivalence.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines five explicit semantic layers (Truth_M(p), Evid(e,p), Eval(K,p,Gamma), Det(K,p,EC,Gamma), Dec(K,Q,P,A,Gamma)) to prevent classical truth, evidence, uncertainty, contradiction and operational determination from being silently collapsed into one binary logic with metadata.
