b_rows_sample.statement: Introduces an Evidence Provenance Taxonomy (E1 direct source evidence, E2 project artifact, E3 external theory, E4 derived synthesis, E5 model inference, E6 critique/counterargument, E7 decision/authority) requiring every formal claim to record (source, evidence class, generation mode, date, authority), and a Tension Taxonomy (T1 synonymous, T2 complementary, T3 different abstraction level, T4 different bounded context, T5 conditional tension, T6 genuine contradiction, T7 unresolved) to replace 'genuine contradiction = 0' as a success criterion, arguing the goal should be 'every apparent conflict is explicitly typed' rather than a raw zero count. Downgrades the 6-vs-8-vs-10 Kernel-formulation-count debate to provenance metadata, proposing four semantic dimensions (Boundary, Admission, Lifecycle, Accountability) as sufficient for Phase 1 instead.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Knowledge Space != Epistemic State != Knowledge Attribution ... Knowledge Space: The **semantic universe of discourse** ... Epistemic State: E(a,c,t) ... Knowledge Attribution: Knows(a,p,c,t) ... This should **not** be reduced to a probability, confidence score or evidence score.
b_rows_sample.statement: Sharpens a three-way non-collapse: Knowledge Space (the semantic universe of discourse: entities, events, states, propositions, relations, institutions, contexts, not yet metric/probabilistic/measurable) != Epistemic State E(a,c,t) (a participant's position at a time/context, containing commitments/hypotheses/questions/uncertainties) != Knowledge Attribution Knows(a,p,c,t) (a factive semantic relation not reducible to probability, confidence or evidence score).

b_rows_sample.anchor: $$\mathcal{K}=(D,P,T,C,I,E,\mathsf{Rel},H,\Theta)$$ ... **Knowledge Space is not merely a set. It is a many-sorted relational structure.** ... type safety at the mathematical level. For example: observes:PxIxT is meaningful. But: observes:PxPxT is not automatically meaningful.
b_rows_sample.statement: Restates and re-derives the many-sorted relational structure K=(D,P,T,C,I,E,Rel,H,Theta) (domain objects, participants, time, contexts, information, epistemic states, typed relations, history, transitions) as replacing an undifferentiated Omega, giving mathematical type-safety analogous to DDD bounded vocabulary: e.g. observes:PxIxT is well-typed while observes:PxPxT is not automatically meaningful.

b_rows_sample.anchor: $$DomainObject \neq Proposition$$ ... x=Nexus Server ... p="Nexus Server listens on port 8081." The proposition is *about* the domain object. Therefore we need a relation: refersTo(p,x)
b_rows_sample.statement: Introduces DomainObject != Proposition with an explicit refersTo(p,x)/about(p,x) relation connecting a proposition to the domain object it is about, arguing KnowledgeOS must preserve the things propositions are about, not only the propositions themselves.

b_rows_sample.anchor: $$Knows\subseteq P\times\mathsf{Prop}\times C\times T$$ ... The factivity constraint is: $$Knows(a,p,c,t)\Rightarrow True(p,c,t)$$ ... $$Knows \neq f(Evidence,Probability,Inference)$$ as a universal definition. Those mechanisms may **justify, assess, challenge or reconstruct** knowledge attribution, but they do not necessarily define the semantic relation itself.
b_rows_sample.statement: Restates Knowledge Attribution as the relation Knows subset of PxPropxCxT with the factivity constraint Knows(a,p,c,t) => True(p,c,t) (when factivity is adopted), explicitly rejecting Knows = f(Evidence,Probability,Inference) as a universal definition -- evidence/probability/inference may justify, assess, challenge or reconstruct a knowledge attribution without defining the semantic relation itself.

b_rows_sample.anchor: **The type of E_t should be fixed before kernel minimality is claimed.** That follows directly from the earlier kernel experiments. ... $$E_{a,c,t}=\{Believes(p),Hypothesizes(q),Rejects(r)\}$$ does not imply: Knows(a,p,c,t). ... Belief != Knowledge, Hypothesis != Knowledge, Assertion != Knowledge, Evidence != Knowledge, Probability != Knowledge.
b_rows_sample.statement: Argues, citing the kernel experiments' own lesson, that the internal decomposition/type of an Epistemic State E_{a,c,t} must be fixed before kernel minimality can be meaningfully claimed, deliberately leaving E's tuple type abstract (E in the admissible epistemic-state domain) rather than freezing a specific field list; derives a five-way non-collapse Belief != Knowledge, Hypothesis != Knowledge, Assertion != Knowledge, Evidence != Knowledge, Probability != Knowledge from the fact that holding beliefs/hypotheses/rejections about p does not itself entail Knows(a,p,c,t).

a_aliases: Knowledge Modelling & KnowledgeOS Kernel -- Knowledge Transfer for New Session

group_evidence.why_grouped: explicit agent-stated uncertainty: 'knowledge-transfer-phase1-measure-theory-doc' POSSIBLY relates to 'relational-structure-core-regime-model' (batch B0017). Note: S0675/S0676's session-transfer synthesis document: converges the phase_measure_theory research thread into a candidate Core (P,T,B,I,E,K,R,H,Theta), a DDD bounded-context map, a Zero Lens admission test, Roberts measurement governance, Shani invariants, a Core Admission Matrix, and explicit corrections/prohibitions; declares itself a synthesis artifact, not primary authority. Its Core tuple closely parallels but is not identical to relational-structure-core-regime-model's Kfrak=(P,C,T,X,I,E,R,Lambda) (B0014) -- flagged as possibly the same evolving object, not confirmed.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The KnowledgeOS Gap should not initially be defined as I_t-K_t, because K_t and I_t are generally heterogeneous semantic objects and may not live in a vector space. Instead, the fundamental Gap is a **set of unsatisfied epistemic requirements**.
a_rows_sample.statement: States the file's central correction: the Gap must not be initially defined as I_t-K_t (K_t and I_t are heterogeneous semantic objects that may not live in a vector space); the fundamental Gap is instead a set of unsatisfied epistemic requirements, with numerical gap measures derived from that set only once additional structure (weights, costs, probabilities, metrics, utilities) is explicitly supplied.

a_rows_sample.anchor: I=[1,1,1,1], K_t=[1,0.8,0.4,0]. Then: I-K_t=[0,0.2,0.6,1]. ... what do the values mean? The 0.2 might mean: insufficient evidence, probability of correctness, measurement uncertainty, incomplete coverage, stale information, disagreement between sources. ... Numerical difference != Epistemic Gap in general.
a_rows_sample.statement: Gives a worked numerical counterexample (I=[1,1,1,1], K_t=[1,0.8,0.4,0], I-K_t=[0,0.2,0.6,1]) showing the resulting numbers are semantically ambiguous (0.2 could mean insufficient evidence, probability of correctness, measurement uncertainty, incomplete coverage, staleness, or source disagreement), establishing Numerical difference != Epistemic Gap in general -- valid only once the semantics and scale of every coordinate is established.

a_rows_sample.anchor: $$r=(id,type,scope,content,standard,priority,validity)$$ ... $$I_t=\mathcal R_t$$ semantically. ... The Ideal State is therefore **the set of epistemically relevant requirements**. ... knowledge sufficient for the declared purpose.
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines a formal Epistemic Requirement r=(id,type,scope,content,standard,priority,validity) and re-derives the Ideal State semantically as I_t = R_t, the set of epistemically relevant requirements (knowledge sufficient for the declared purpose), rather than a mysterious perfect object.

a_rows_sample.anchor: [DEF-G1] Epistemic Gap: $$\Delta_t=\{r\in\mathcal R_t: Sat(K_t,r)=0\}.$$ ... It does not require: subtraction, Euclidean geometry, probability, vectors, finite dimensionality. That makes it much more general.
a_rows_sample.statement: [DEF-G1] States the fundamental Gap Definition: Delta_t = {r in R_t : Sat(K_t,r)=0}, the set of currently unsatisfied epistemic requirements, requiring no subtraction, Euclidean geometry, probability, vectors, or finite dimensionality -- making it substantially more general than any arithmetic-difference formulation.

a_rows_sample.anchor: [DEF-G2] Zero_t iff Delta_t=empty. ... [THM-G1] ... Proof: By definition, Delta_t=empty iff there exists no requirement unsatisfied. Therefore every requirement is satisfied ... which is exactly K_t|=EC_t.
a_rows_sample.statement: [DEF-G2]/[THM-G1] Formalizes Zero_t iff Delta_t=empty iff (for all r in R_t, Sat(K_t,r)=1) iff K_t models EC_t, with an explicit proof by direct definitional unfolding -- much stronger than saying Zero is 'distance zero.'

a_rows_sample.anchor: G1 Coverage Gap ... purest form of missing knowledge. G2 Value Gap: Dimension(r) exists AND Value_Kt(r)=bottom. Unknown Value != Unknown Dimension. G3 Uncertainty Gap: P(p|E,C,M) below required threshold. G4 Evidence/Warrant Gap: Having an answer != Having justified knowledge.
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines the first four of ten gap classes: G1 Coverage Gap (required knowledge item not established at all, the purest missing-knowledge case); G2 Value Gap (dimension known but value unknown, formalized as Dimension(r) exists AND Value_Kt(r)=bottom, giving Unknown Value != Unknown Dimension); G3 Uncertainty Gap (a claim exists but its probability falls below the contract's required threshold); G4 Evidence/Warrant Gap (a claim exists but its evidence is absent or below the required strength threshold, giving Having an answer != Having justified knowledge).

a_rows_sample.anchor: G5 Contradiction Gap: Conflict(p,not p)=1 ... The KnowledgeOS state should not silently select one. G6 Model Gap: observations sufficient for correlation, insufficient for causal determination. G7 Observability Gap: Observable(r,K_t)=0 ... must not automatically become Value(r)=False.
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines gap classes G5-G7: G5 Contradiction Gap (two admissible sources produce p and not-p; KnowledgeOS must represent Conflict(p,not-p) rather than silently selecting one, worked with a Nexus-version-disagreement example); G6 Model Gap (facts known but the required interpretive model, e.g. causal vs correlational, is inadequate, drawn from the causal/statistical experiments); G7 Observability Gap (Observable(r,K_t)=0 because the required observation is currently unavailable, e.g. no network access to check a firewall rule -- must not automatically collapse into Value(r)=False).

a_rows_sample.anchor: G8 Temporal/Staleness Gap: Age(p)>TTL_EC ... Superseded != False. G9 Identity/Referential Gap: the required claim cannot be reliably attached to the required domain identity. Identity != State. G10 Representation Gap: Expressible_r(p)=0 ... different representation algebras can produce different apparent primitive counts.
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines gap classes G8-G10: G8 Temporal/Staleness Gap (Age(p) exceeds the contract's TTL, giving Superseded != False); G9 Identity/Referential Gap (a true proposition that cannot be reliably attached to the required domain identity is unusable for the inquiry, giving Identity != State); G10 Representation Gap (Expressible_r(p)=0, the current representation cannot express a required semantic distinction -- connected explicitly to the kernel experiments' finding that different representation algebras produce different apparent primitive counts).

a_rows_sample.anchor: $$\Delta_t=(G_{cov},G_{val},G_{unc},G_{warrant},G_{con},G_{model},G_{obs},G_{stale},G_{id},G_{repr})$$ ... **not a numerical vector yet**. It is a **typed semantic gap vector**.
a_rows_sample.statement: Assembles the complete typed Gap vector Delta_t=(G_cov,G_val,G_unc,G_warrant,G_con,G_model,G_obs,G_stale,G_id,G_repr), explicitly a typed semantic gap vector, not yet a numerical one, worked through a comparative example table showing this preserves epistemic meaning that a bare I-K difference would flatten.

a_rows_sample.anchor: K_t != Delta_t. And: K_t != I_t. Therefore: K_t != I_t-K_t. ... The derivation correctly warned against collapsing Knowledge and Knowledge Gap.
a_rows_sample.statement: States the crucial theoretical correction Gap is not Knowledge: K_t != Delta_t and K_t != I_t, therefore K_t != I_t - K_t (guarding against collapsing the Knowledge state, Ideal state, and Gap into interchangeable objects).

a_rows_sample.anchor: $$K_{t+1}\succeq_{EC}K_t \iff \Delta(K_{t+1},EC)\subseteq\Delta(K_t,EC)$$ ... [THM-G2] If Delta_{t+1} subset-eq Delta_t, then K_{t+1} >=_EC K_t. If Delta_{t+1} subset Delta_t, then K_{t+1} >_EC K_t. This finally gives us a mathematically defensible notion of **knowledge improvement** without requiring a numerical metric.
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines a partial order of knowledge adequacy K_{t+1} >=_EC K_t iff Delta_{t+1} subset-or-equal Delta_t (subject to preservation of previously valid requirements), with [THM-G2] the Gap-reduction theorem giving strict improvement K_{t+1} >_EC K_t when the inclusion is strict -- a mathematically defensible notion of knowledge improvement requiring no numerical metric.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Suppose K_t={p,q,r} but q is later discovered unsupported. Then K_{t+1}={p,r}. The cardinality decreased ... Yet epistemic quality may improve. ... |K_{t+1}|<|K_t| not=> K_{t+1} prec K_t.
a_rows_sample.statement: Gives a worked example (K_t={p,q,r} shrinking to K_{t+1}={p,r} after q is found unsupported) showing knowledge can improve while cardinality decreases, giving |K_{t+1}|<|K_t| does not imply K_{t+1} is epistemically worse -- the reason knowledge quantity and knowledge quality must remain separate.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Negative Gap ... Ideal State requires p. But current knowledge contains not-p. The issue is not simply "missing p." It is: Contradictory State. ... Delta^+ = missing required knowledge and Delta^- = currently held knowledge violating requirements. Delta_t=(Delta_t^+,Delta_t^-).
a_rows_sample.statement: Introduces Negative Gap: when the Ideal State requires p but current knowledge contains not-p, the issue is a Contradictory State, not simple absence; formalizes a directional split Delta_t=(Delta_t^+, Delta_t^-) where Delta^+ is missing required knowledge and Delta^- is currently-held knowledge violating requirements -- more informative than an undirected absolute distance.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Positive deficit: Missing ... Negative conflict: Contradictory ... Epistemic insufficiency: Insufficient ... Gap = Deficit union Conflict union Insufficiency.
a_rows_sample.statement: Consolidates the ten gap classes into three fundamental gap directions -- Positive deficit (Missing: required but absent), Negative conflict (Contradictory: present but incompatible with requirements), and Epistemic insufficiency (Insufficient: present but below required evidence/uncertainty/model standard) -- giving Gap = Deficit union Conflict union Insufficiency as the top-level decomposition of which the detailed taxonomy is a refinement.

a_rows_sample.anchor: $$G_{coverage}=1-Coverage_t$$ ... g_r^unc=max(0,tau_r-p_r) ... g_r^evidence=max(0,tau_e-e_r) ... g_r^time=max(0,age_r-L_r) ... g_r^model=1-Sat(M_t,A_r) ... g_r^obs=1-O_r. But this is **not** the probability that the requirement is false.
a_rows_sample.statement: Derives six named numerical gap measures (each a DERIVED view, not the Gap's definition) once explicit scales exist: coverage gap 1-Coverage_t; uncertainty gap max(0,tau_r-p_r); evidence gap max(0,tau_e-e_r); temporal gap max(0,age_r-L_r); model gap 1-Sat(M_t,A_r); observability gap 1-O_r (explicitly NOT the probability the requirement is false, but uncertainty about observability itself).

a_rows_sample.anchor: $$G(K_t,EC_t)=\sum_{r\in\mathcal R_t}w_r d_r(K_t,EC_t).$$ ... [THM-G3] Zero equivalence ... Proof: If G=0 and every term is non-negative, then every term must be zero ... Therefore: G=0 iff Zero.
a_rows_sample.statement: Derives the master weighted Gap functional G(K_t,EC_t)=sum over required r of w_r*d_r(K_t,EC_t) (d_r>=0, d_r=0 iff satisfied), and proves [THM-G3] the Zero-equivalence theorem G(K_t,EC_t)=0 iff Delta_t=empty, with an explicit non-negative-sum proof -- the rigorous bridge from semantic Gap to statistical/numerical Gap that was previously missing.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Level 1 -- Semantic: Delta_t. Level 2 -- Structured: Delta_t^typed. Level 3 -- Numerical: G_t. Thus: Semantic Gap -> Typed Gap -> Numerical Gap. Not the reverse.
a_rows_sample.statement: States the three-level Gap hierarchy discipline: Semantic Gap (Delta_t, what is missing/contradictory/uncertain/stale) -> Typed Gap (how each requirement is deficient) -> Numerical Gap (G_t, magnitude under an explicit loss/weighting model) -- and explicitly never the reverse order.

a_rows_sample.anchor: $$\mathfrak G=(\mathcal R,Sat,Type,\oplus,\preceq)$$ ... $$\Delta_1\oplus\Delta_2=\Delta_1\cup\Delta_2.$$ ... [THM-G4] ... If EC_t=EC_{t+1}, then Gap reduction is directly comparable. If EC_t != EC_{t+1}, then a direct comparison requires an explicit mapping M: Req(EC_t)->Req(EC_{t+1}). Without such mapping: Delta_t not~ Delta_{t+1} in general. This protects KnowledgeOS against "moving the goalposts."
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines a formal Gap algebra G=(R,Sat,Type,+,<=) with gap composition Delta1 (+) Delta2 = union (with identity-based normalization needed under requirement overlap), and proves [THM-G4] the Contract Invariance theorem: gap comparison across time is only valid when EC_t=EC_{t+1}, or else requires an explicit mapping M:Req(EC_t)->Req(EC_{t+1}) between requirement sets -- protecting KnowledgeOS against artificially achieving Zero by silently changing requirements ('moving the goalposts').

a_rows_sample.anchor: Ideal State is therefore not arbitrary. ... Prov(I_t)=(Knower,Goal,Inquiry,Context,Contract,Time,Authority). ... its origin is auditable.
a_rows_sample.statement: Gives the Ideal State its own provenance object Prov(I_t)=(Knower,Goal,Inquiry,Context,Contract,Time,Authority), making the Ideal State's origin auditable rather than an arbitrary given, following the earlier conclusion that the Knower owns the epistemic frame and Ideal State.

a_rows_sample.anchor: $$\Delta_t=Gap(K_t,EC_t)$$ not simply: Gap(K_t). The same knowledge state can have Zero for one purpose and LargeGap for another. ... For "What operating system does Nexus use?" the gap may be empty. For "Is Nexus ready for migration?" the gap may be large. Gap is purpose relative.
a_rows_sample.statement: States the Gap is fundamentally relational (Gap(K_t,EC_t), never Gap(K_t) alone), worked through a concrete Nexus example where the same knowledge (OS=RHEL9.8, 8vCPU, Nexus OSS 3.69.0) has Delta=empty for 'what OS does Nexus use?' but a large gap for 'is Nexus ready for migration?' -- Gap is purpose-relative.

b_rows_sample.anchor: [DEF-1] Knowledge ... $$Knows(s,p,c,t)$$ ... $$Knows(s,p,c,t)\Rightarrow True(p,c,t)$$ ... deliberately stronger and cleaner than defining knowledge as probability, data, evidence or belief.
b_rows_sample.statement: [DEF-1] Knowledge: Knows(s,p,c,t) as a factive epistemic relation between participant s, proposition p, context c and time t, with Knows(s,p,c,t) => True(p,c,t) when the epistemic contract is factive.

b_rows_sample.anchor: [AX-1] Category non-collapse: Distinct semantic categories may not be identified merely because one can be represented by another. O!=K, Evidence!=Knowledge, Claim!=Truth, Probability!=Knowledge, Proposal!=Decision, Representation!=Identity.
b_rows_sample.statement: [AX-1] Category non-collapse: distinct semantic categories may not be identified merely because one can be represented by another, giving six named non-collapses: Observation!=Knowledge, Evidence!=Knowledge, Claim!=Truth, Probability!=Knowledge, Proposal!=Decision, Representation!=Identity.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Domain ontology: $$\mathfrak O=\{W,S,O,E,P,C,Q,K,I,\Delta,Pr,Dc,A,H,EC,R\}$$ ... These are **semantic sorts**, not necessarily database tables or classes.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines a sixteen-sort domain ontology (World, participant/knower, observation, evidence, proposition, context, inquiry, knowledge state, ideal state, epistemic gap, proposal, decision, action, history, epistemic contract, representation/regime), explicitly semantic sorts, not database tables or classes.

b_rows_sample.anchor: [DEF-2] World state: $$W_t\not\equiv O_t$$ ... [DEF-3] Observation: $$O_t^s=Obs(s,W_t,m_t,c_t)$$ ... Observation != Reality and Observation != Knowledge.
b_rows_sample.statement: [DEF-2] World state W_t (KnowledgeOS does not require complete access to it, W_t not-equivalent O_t); [DEF-3] Observation O_t^s=Obs(s,W_t,m_t,c_t) as a method-mediated relation between participant and reality, giving Observation != Reality and Observation != Knowledge.

b_rows_sample.anchor: [DEF-4] Knower: $$F_s=(G_s,C_s,Q_s,EC_s,M_s)$$ ... [AX-2] Knower-frame ownership: $$Frame(K,s)=F_s$$ KnowledgeOS may calculate, extract, compare or propose, but it may not silently redefine: the purpose, context, acceptance criteria, inquiry, or epistemic contract.
b_rows_sample.statement: [DEF-4] Knower: a participant with an epistemic frame F_s=(G_s,C_s,Q_s,EC_s,M_s) (purpose, context, inquiry, epistemic contract, admissible methods); [AX-2] Knower-frame ownership: the frame belongs to the knower or explicitly authorized epistemic authority, and KnowledgeOS may calculate/extract/compare/propose but may never silently redefine the purpose, context, acceptance criteria, inquiry, or epistemic contract.

b_rows_sample.anchor: [DEF-5] Proposition ... Proposition != Claim. [DEF-6] Claim: Claim=(p,c,t,s) ... supported, unsupported, uncertain, challenged, accepted, rejected, superseded. But: Claim != Truth.
b_rows_sample.statement: [DEF-5] Proposition: semantic content capable of being true or false under an interpretation and context, explicitly Proposition != Claim; [DEF-6] Claim=(p,c,t,s), a proposition presented for epistemic evaluation, admitting seven possible statuses (supported/unsupported/uncertain/challenged/accepted/rejected/superseded), with Claim != Truth.

b_rows_sample.anchor: [DEF-7] Evidence ... Supports(e,p) is directional. Therefore: Supports(e,p) not=> Truth(p) and Evidence != Knowledge. ... prov(e)=(source,method,agent,time,context,integrity) ... Knowledge <- Evidence <- Provenance.
b_rows_sample.statement: [DEF-7] Evidence: a directional support relation Supports(e,p) between information and proposition, giving Supports(e,p) does not imply Truth(p) and Evidence != Knowledge; evidence provenance is defined as prov(e)=(source,method,agent,time,context,integrity), giving the dependency chain Knowledge <- Evidence <- Provenance.

b_rows_sample.anchor: [DEF-8] Extraction: Extract:E->X ... [DEF-9] Determination: Determine(X,EC)->Status ... [AX-3] Extraction-Determination separation: Extraction != Determination. Therefore an extraction mechanism cannot silently become epistemic authority.
b_rows_sample.statement: [DEF-8] Extraction: Extract:E->X (retrieves/transforms information from evidence); [DEF-9] Determination: Determine(X,EC)->Status (establishes epistemic status warranted by evidence under standards); [AX-3] Extraction-Determination separation: Extraction != Determination, so an extraction mechanism cannot silently become epistemic authority.

b_rows_sample.anchor: [DEF-10] Knowledge atom: the smallest independently meaningful epistemic assertion that contributes to the semantic state under a declared representation. $$k_i$$ ... Sentence != Dimension != KnowledgeAtom automatically. The semantic independence must be established.
b_rows_sample.statement: [DEF-10] Knowledge atom k_i: the smallest independently meaningful epistemic assertion contributing to the semantic state under a declared representation, defined semantically (since its exact tuple is representation-dependent) rather than syntactically, giving Sentence != Dimension != KnowledgeAtom automatically -- semantic independence must be separately established for any candidate atom.

b_rows_sample.anchor: [DEF-11] Semantic Knowledge State: $$K_t\in\mathbb K$$ ... We deliberately do **not** initially require: K_t={k_1,...,k_n} nor K_t=(p,e,c,t,...) as a universal implementation tuple. Instead: K = space of admissible semantic epistemic states ... a concrete representation r provides: r(K_t)=x_t.
b_rows_sample.statement: [DEF-11] Semantic Knowledge State: K_t is an element of an abstract space K of admissible semantic epistemic states, deliberately NOT initially required to be a specific tuple (neither a bare atom-set nor a fixed (p,e,c,t,...) record); a concrete representation r maps it to a carrier value r(K_t)=x_t -- explicitly resolving the earlier conflict between multiple candidate K_t tuples by keeping the type abstract.

b_rows_sample.anchor: v1.0 requires that a sufficiently expressive state preserve at least the following semantic dimensions: $$K_t=(Content_t,Support_t,Uncertainty_t,Model_t,Alternatives_t,History_t,Identity_t,Context_t,Inquiry_t,Status_t)$$ This is a **semantic decomposition**, not a mandatory storage tuple.
b_rows_sample.statement: Requires that any sufficiently expressive v1.0-conformant state preserve at least ten named semantic dimensions (Content, Support, Uncertainty, Model, Alternatives, History, Identity, Context, Inquiry, Status), explicitly a semantic decomposition (a minimum expressiveness requirement) rather than a mandatory storage tuple.

b_rows_sample.anchor: [DEF-12] Knowledge projection: $$K_t^s=Projection_s(W_{\leq t})$$ conceptually. Therefore: K_t != W_t and K_t != CompleteReality.
b_rows_sample.statement: [DEF-12] Knowledge projection: a participant's knowledge state K_t^s is conceptually a bounded projection of accumulated world history K_t^s=Projection_s(W_{<=t}), giving K_t != W_t and K_t != CompleteReality.

b_rows_sample.anchor: [DEF-13] Semantic Knowledge Space: (K,Sem) is the space of admissible semantic epistemic states. [DEF-14] Representation space: for representation r, (X_r,A_r) is its mathematical carrier. This distinction is crucial. ... [DEF-15] Semantic equivalence: r1=_sem r2 iff [[r1(x)]]=[[r2(y)]] for corresponding semantic states ... r1=_sem r2 iff B_r1=B_r2 over the admissible test domain.
b_rows_sample.statement: [DEF-13] Semantic Knowledge Space (K,Sem) kept distinct from [DEF-14] a specific Representation space (X_r,A_r) for representation r; [DEF-15] Semantic equivalence r1=_sem r2 defined via matching semantic interpretation of corresponding states, or more generally via matching observable behaviour B_r1=B_r2 over the admissible test domain -- explicitly named as the missing concept that explains the 13-vs-8 kernel result.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Measurable Knowledge Space = (X,A) and probability is an additional structure. ... [DEF-16] An epistemic observable is a measurable function Y_j:Omega->V_j. ... A = sigma(Y_j: j in J). ... Infinite-dimensional Knowledge Space X=prod X_j, A=bigotimes A_j ... |X|=infinity is **not** a v1.0 axiom. It is an admissible model.
b_rows_sample.statement: Fixes Measurable Knowledge Space = (X,A) != Probability Space; [DEF-16] epistemic observable Y_j:Omega->V_j generating the measurable structure A=sigma(Y_j:j in J); infinite-dimensional Knowledge Space X=product of X_j with product sigma-field, explicitly noted as an ADMISSIBLE MODEL, not a v1.0 axiom (infinite dimensionality is not mandated).

b_rows_sample.anchor: Partial knowledge as a measurable region: cylinder C=A1xA2xA3x(prod j>3 X_j). ... Unknown = Unconstrained in the representation, not a fabricated value. Therefore: Unknown != False != ProbabilityZero. ... [DEF-17] $$\mathcal F_t$$ ... filtration.
b_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes partial knowledge as a finite-dimensional cylinder set, giving Unknown=Unconstrained (not a fabricated value) and reinforcing Unknown != False != ProbabilityZero; [DEF-17] epistemic filtration F_t (the sigma-field of all epistemically available measurable information through t), non-decreasing F_0 subset F_1 subset ....

b_rows_sample.anchor: F_t != K_t. F_t describes **available information**. K_t describes **semantic epistemic state**. Hence: $$K_t=\Phi(\mathcal F_t,S_t,Q_t,C_t,EC_t,M_t,H_t)$$ for an epistemic determination function Phi. This is a **theoretical construction**, not a theorem that measure theory supplies.
b_rows_sample.statement: States F_t != K_t (available information vs semantic epistemic state) as a formal distinction, with K_t = Phi(F_t,S_t,Q_t,C_t,EC_t,M_t,H_t) for an epistemic determination function Phi explicitly flagged as a theoretical construction, not a theorem measure theory itself supplies.

b_rows_sample.anchor: [DEF-18] If a target variable X has a probabilistic model: Pi_t=L(X|F_t) ... Pi_t != K_t. ... Epistemic uncertainty: U_t=U(K_t) may use probability, confidence intervals, likelihood, possibility, belief functions, intervals, qualitative states, logical alternatives, evidence strength. Probability subsetneq EpistemicAssessment.
b_rows_sample.statement: [DEF-18] Probability as an optional, regime-dependent conditional law Pi_t=L(X|F_t), explicitly Pi_t != K_t; separately defines a general epistemic uncertainty function U_t=U(K_t) that MAY be realized by probability, confidence intervals, likelihood, possibility, belief functions, intervals, qualitative states, logical alternatives, or evidence strength, giving Probability as a proper subset of EpistemicAssessment.

b_rows_sample.anchor: [DEF-19] Epistemic requirement: EC_t=EC(S_t,G_t,Q_t,C_t) ... $$\mathbb I(EC_t)=\{K\in\mathbb K: Sat(K,EC_t)\}$$ ... IdealState != AbsoluteKnowledge. It is purpose-relative.
b_rows_sample.statement: [DEF-19] Epistemic requirement: the epistemic contract EC_t=EC(S_t,G_t,Q_t,C_t), used to define the admissible ideal REGION I(EC_t)={K in K : Sat(K,EC_t)} (a set of satisfying states, not one universal ideal state), giving IdealState != AbsoluteKnowledge -- it is purpose-relative.

b_rows_sample.anchor: [DEF-20] Adequate(K_t,EC_t) iff Sat(K_t,EC_t). ... [DEF-21] Epistemic Gap: $$\Delta_t=Gap(K_t,EC_t)=\{r\in Req(EC_t):\neg Sat(K_t,r)\}.$$ This is the canonical v1.0 definition. Therefore: Delta_t=empty iff Adequate(K_t,EC_t).
b_rows_sample.statement: [DEF-20] Epistemic adequacy Adequate(K_t,EC_t) iff Sat(K_t,EC_t); [DEF-21] Epistemic Gap declared as the CANONICAL v1.0 definition: Delta_t=Gap(K_t,EC_t)={r in Req(EC_t): not Sat(K_t,r)}, a requirement-set (not a subtraction of heterogeneous structures), with Delta_t=empty iff Adequate(K_t,EC_t) -- explicitly resolving the earlier mathematically-invalid K_t*-K_t formula.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Typed gap: $$\Delta_t=(\Delta^{content},\Delta^{uncertainty},\Delta^{model},\Delta^{observability},\Delta^{requirement})$$ ... In v1.0 we resolve the conceptual problem by making the **requirement-set representation canonical**, while allowing numerical projections later.
b_rows_sample.statement: Retains the five-component typed-gap vector (content, uncertainty, model, observability, requirement) as an optional further classification, but resolves the underlying representation problem by making the requirement-SET formulation Delta_t subset Req(EC_t) canonical, while allowing numerical projections of it to be defined later as needed.

group_evidence.why_grouped: explicit agent-stated uncertainty: 'knowledgeos-gap-theory-v1-0' POSSIBLY relates to 'knowledgeos-theory-v1-0-definitions-axioms-theorems' (batch B0057). Note: A fully self-contained formal sub-theory of the Knowledge Gap, developed the same day as and explicitly building on this batch's v1.0 Definitions/Axioms/Theorems document (reusing its DEF-21/DEF-22/THM-4 Gap/Zero apparatus but developing it into its own DEF-G1/DEF-G2/THM-G1..G6 numbering): rejects Delta=I-K as mathematically too strong, defines the Gap as the set of unsatisfied epistemic requirements Delta_t={r in R_t : Sat(K_t,r)=0} with no arithmetic/vector-space assumption; derives Zero as the bottom element of the gap lattice (P(R_t),subseteq); introduces a ten-class gap taxonomy (Coverage/Value/Uncertainty/Evidence-Warrant/Contradiction/Model/Observability/Temporal-Staleness/Identity-Referential/Representation gaps); a positive-deficit/negative-conflict/epistemic-insufficiency three-way reduction; a three-level Semantic->Typed->Numerical gap hierarchy with a derived weighted gap functional G(K_t,EC_t) and the Zero-equivalence theorem G=0 iff Delta_t=empty (THM-G3); a partial order K_{t+1} >=_EC K_t iff Delta_{t+1} subseteq Delta_t with a proven gap-reduction theorem (THM-G2); a contract-invariance theorem (THM-G4, gap comparison requires contract compatibility, preventing 'moving the goalposts'); the gap-increase-does-not-imply-knowledge-decrease result (an investigation can enlarge the known gap while improving epistemic honesty); a gap-composition/algebra structure (P(R),Sat,Type,union,subseteq); reformalized Lord/Sarathi roles as Gap->Proposal->Decision; a Gap Control theorem (THM-G5); a two-measure Progress vector (Adequacy, GapObservability, Warrant, UncertaintyReduction, ModelAdequacy); a Gap Decomposition theorem (THM-G6, non-exclusive overlapping gap classes); and a closing ten-item explicitly OPEN list. Possibly the same milestone object as knowledgeos-theory-v1-0-definitions-axioms-theorems (a companion/extension chapter of the same v1.0 specification), possibly a distinct standalone artifact -- not resolved within this batch.

a_rows_sample.anchor: we should distinguish definitions, mathematical propositions/theorems, empirical findings, conjectures, and research heuristics. In particular, some equations that appeared earlier as if they were empirical results are actually mathematical consequences of the definitions under explicit assumptions.
a_rows_sample.statement: States the governing improvement of this pass over the prior consolidated draft: strictly distinguish definitions, proven mathematical propositions/theorems, empirical findings, conjectures, and research heuristics, since some equations previously presented as empirical results are actually mathematical consequences of the definitions under explicit assumptions.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Theorem 1 -- Functional recoverability criterion. Let D be a random variable, R=T(D), and Q=Q(D) ... H(Q|R)=0 if and only if Q is almost surely a deterministic function of R. Proof: H(Q|R) = sum_r P(R=r) H(Q|R=r) ... Q=g(R) almost surely.
a_rows_sample.statement: Proves Theorem 1 (functional recoverability criterion): for discrete finite-valued random variables, H(Q|R)=0 if and only if Q is almost surely a deterministic function of R, with a complete proof via the decomposition H(Q|R)=sum_r P(R=r)H(Q|R=r) and the observation that each conditional distribution with positive probability must be degenerate.

a_rows_sample.anchor: N_viol=0 => empirical adequacy on the tested sample. This does not imply population adequacy. That distinction is fundamental.
a_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes the finite-sample operational adequacy criterion: a deterministic empirical decoder exists iff every representation value corresponds to at most one inquiry value in the test set (equivalently N_viol=0), which implies only empirical adequacy on the tested sample, never population adequacy.

a_rows_sample.anchor: H(R) = H(Q) + H(R|Q) - H(Q|R) ... If the representation is adequate, H(Q|R)=0. Therefore H(R)=H(Q)+H(R|Q). Hence H(R)>=H(Q). Equality occurs iff H(R|Q)=0. Therefore H(R)=H(Q) iff H(Q|R)=0 and H(R|Q)=0.
a_rows_sample.statement: Derives the general chain-rule identity H(R)=H(Q)+H(R|Q)-H(Q|R), specializing under adequacy (H(Q|R)=0) to H(R)=H(Q)+H(R|Q), hence H(R)>=H(Q) with equality iff H(R|Q)=0 as well -- the mathematically precise form of the earlier informal 'no representational excess' idea.

a_rows_sample.anchor: NoExcess(R,Q) iff H(R|Q)=0. ... Adequacy: H(Q|R)=0. No excess: H(R|Q)=0. These are logically independent conditions in general. ... Adequate with excess: H(Q|R)=0, H(R|Q)>0. Inadequate: H(Q|R)>0. ... Sufficiency != Minimality.
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines NoExcess(R,Q) iff H(R|Q)=0 and formally establishes that adequacy (H(Q|R)=0) and no-excess (H(R|Q)=0) are logically independent conditions in general -- a representation can be 'adequate with excess' (H(Q|R)=0 but H(R|Q)>0) or inadequate (H(Q|R)>0) -- yielding the new distinction Sufficiency != Minimality.

a_rows_sample.anchor: R1 ~_Q R2 when Q(decode(R1)) = Q(decode(R2)). However, the theory should not call this Q-isomorphism. ... equality of inquiry outcomes does not establish structural isomorphism. Q-equivalent != Q-isomorphic. The latter requires additional structural conditions.
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines Q-equivalence between representations (R1 ~_Q R2 iff Q(decode(R1))=Q(decode(R2))) and explicitly distinguishes it from 'Q-isomorphism', since equality of inquiry outcomes does not establish structural isomorphism, which requires additional structural conditions not implied by Q-equivalence alone.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Theorem 2 -- Conditional entropy monotonicity under deterministic reduction. Let Q -> R_n -> R_{n-1} form a Markov chain, with R_{n-1}=T_n(R_n) deterministically. Then H(Q|R_{n-1}) >= H(Q|R_n). Proof: data-processing inequality gives I(Q;R_{n-1}) <= I(Q;R_n) ... cancel H(Q) ... QED.
a_rows_sample.statement: Proves Theorem 2 (conditional entropy monotonicity under deterministic reduction): for a Markov chain Q->R_n->R_{n-1} with R_{n-1}=T_n(R_n) deterministic, H(Q|R_{n-1})>=H(Q|R_n), derived rigorously from the data-processing inequality I(Q;R_{n-1})<=I(Q;R_n) via I(Q;R)=H(Q)-H(Q|R); the corollary chain H(Q|R5)<=H(Q|R4)<=H(Q|R3)<=H(Q|R2) shows information sufficiency cannot spontaneously reappear once lost.

a_rows_sample.anchor: A_n = 1{H(Q|R_n)=0}. Then, under exact population adequacy and deterministic degradation: A_n=1 => A_{n-1}<=A_n. Equivalently, adequacy can transition 1->0 but cannot transition 0->1. Thus a preservation boundary can be defined as the first transition: R_k adequate, R_{k-1} inadequate.
a_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes the preservation boundary using an adequacy indicator A_n=1{H(Q|R_n)=0}: under deterministic sequential degradation, adequacy can only transition from 1 to 0, never from 0 to 1, so the preservation boundary is precisely defined as the first transition point R_k adequate, R_{k-1} inadequate.

a_rows_sample.anchor: min_{T in T} C(T(D)) subject to H(Q(D)|T(D))=0. ... C(R) = w1 bytes(R) + w2 latency(R) + w3 storage(R) + ... but the weights must be business-defined. Reduction is an optimization problem subject to preservation.
a_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes reduction as a constrained optimization problem: minimize a business-defined representation-cost functional C(T(D)) (e.g. weighted bytes, latency, storage) subject to the adequacy constraint H(Q(D)|T(D))=0, explicitly marked as a candidate mathematical formulation, not yet an established KnowledgeOS law.

a_rows_sample.anchor: desc != (n+1)-asc [for D with ties, e.g. D=[23000,46000,46000]] ... The implemented ascending/descending rank transformations were not proven to be simple invertible recodings. ... A representational convention can carry operational consequences. But the pure 'decoder-only effect' attribution was to
a_rows_sample.statement: Records the formal audit correction that the ascending/descending rank transformations were not proven to be simple invertible recodings, since deterministic tie-breaking on data with repeated values (e.g. D=[23000,46000,46000]) makes desc != (n+1)-asc; the broader lesson survives (a representational convention can carry operational consequences) but the pure 'decoder-only effect' attribution was too strong and had to be corrected after audit.

a_rows_sample.anchor: f(a otimes_A b) = f(a) otimes_B f(b) [homomorphism]. If this equality fails, define the defect: Delta_f(a,b) = f(a otimes_A b) - f(a) otimes_B f(b) only when an appropriate difference operation exists. Otherwise define a typed defect relation: Def_f(a,b). The theory must not assume homomorphism. It
a_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes the homomorphic-defect quantity for structure-preserving transformations: when f(a otimes_A b) != f(a) otimes_B f(b), define Delta_f(a,b)=f(a otimes_A b) - f(a) otimes_B f(b) if a difference operation exists in the target space, otherwise a typed defect relation Def_f(a,b) when it does not, establishing that homomorphism must be measured, never assumed.

a_rows_sample.anchor: A specific decoder is: O: R -> Y. Realization requires: O(R) = Q(D). A representation can therefore contain sufficient information while a particular decoder fails to recover it. Adequacy != Realization. ... Decoder theorem: if Q is recoverable from R, then there exists an ideal decoder g* such that
a_rows_sample.statement: Proves the decoder theorem: if Q is recoverable from R there exists an ideal decoder g* with g*(R)=Q, but an arbitrary decoder O need not equal g*, so H(Q|R)=0 does not imply O(R)=Q without additional conditions on O -- formally separating representation sufficiency (adequacy) from implementation realization.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Q(D1)=Q(D2) ... This relation IS an equivalence relation because equality is reflexive, symmetric, transitive. Therefore Q partitions the source space: D/~_Q. A representation T is adequate for Q precisely when it distinguishes enough classes to recover the Q-class. Q(D1)!=Q(D2) => T(D1)!=T(D2).
a_rows_sample.statement: Establishes that the relation D1~D2 iff Q(D1)=Q(D2) is a genuine equivalence relation (equality being reflexive, symmetric, transitive), partitioning the source space into D/~_Q classes, with T adequate for Q precisely when it distinguishes enough classes to recover the Q-class, equivalently Q(D1)!=Q(D2) implies T(D1)!=T(D2).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Theorem 3. For deterministic T, the following are equivalent on a domain D0: 1. H(Q|T(D))=0. 2. There exists g such that Q=g.T. 3. Whenever T(D1)=T(D2), then Q(D1)=Q(D2). Proof: 1<=>2 follows from Theorem 1. 2=>3 ... 3=>2: define g(r)=Q(D) for any D with T(D)=r; well-defined by condition 3. QED. Thi
a_rows_sample.statement: Proves Theorem 3, establishing the equivalence, for deterministic T, of (1) H(Q|T(D))=0, (2) existence of g with Q=g.T, and (3) T(D1)=T(D2) implies Q(D1)=Q(D2), with a complete proof; judged extremely useful for KnowledgeOS because it converts semantic preservation into a concrete fiber-separation condition.

a_rows_sample.anchor: T^{-1}(r) = {D: T(D)=r}. Adequacy means: Q is constant on every fiber of T. ... Representation reduction is safe iff every representation fiber is Q-homogeneous.
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines the fiber T^{-1}(r)={D:T(D)=r} of a representation and characterizes adequacy as Q being constant on every fiber of T, giving the clean formulation that representation reduction is safe if and only if every representation fiber is Q-homogeneous -- judged a stronger conceptual formulation than merely 'information was preserved'.

a_rows_sample.anchor: A reduction transformation T1 -> T2 crosses a preservation boundary precisely when T2 creates at least one Q-heterogeneous fiber: exists D1,D2: T2(D1)=T2(D2) but Q(D1)!=Q(D2). Boundary iff first occurrence of a Q-heterogeneous representation fiber. This gives a very concrete mathematical interpretat
a_rows_sample.statement: Characterizes a preservation-boundary crossing as the first occurrence of a Q-heterogeneous representation fiber (T2 collapsing two source states D1,D2 with T2(D1)=T2(D2) but Q(D1)!=Q(D2)), giving a concrete mathematical interpretation of the experimental N_viol statistic as counting such fiber collisions.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Hhat(Q|R)=0 does not establish H(Q|R)=0 in the population. It establishes only a sample-level result under the estimator and observed support. Hhat=0 !=> H=0 without additional statistical assumptions. This distinction is mandatory.
a_rows_sample.statement: Mandates the population-vs-sample distinction as a formal requirement: the empirical estimator result Hhat(Q|R)=0 establishes only a sample-level result under the given estimator and observed support, never the population-level H(Q|R)=0, without additional statistical assumptions.

a_rows_sample.anchor: the representation-reduction audit discovered that a proposed bootstrap confidence interval for conditional entropy was invalid because sparse resampling changed the support structure. ... define the estimator, establish its assumptions, evaluate finite-sample bias, use appropriate corrections, vali
a_rows_sample.statement: Details the specific audit finding that a proposed bootstrap confidence interval for conditional entropy was invalid because sparse resampling changed the support structure, listing six required remedial steps (define estimator, establish assumptions, evaluate finite-sample bias, apply corrections, validate bootstrap conditions, distinguish empirical from population support), while noting the main preservation conclusion survived since it rested on exact violation counts and train/test agreement rather than the invalid confidence interval.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Level 1 -- Observed: Hhat(Q|R) or N_viol. Level 2 -- Experimental conclusion: within the tested sample and design, preservation was/was not observed. Level 3 -- Statistical generalization: requires sampling assumptions, estimator validity, uncertainty quantification, population model. Level 4 -- Mat
a_rows_sample.statement: Establishes a formal four-level statistical-generalization hierarchy that must never be collapsed: Level 1 Observed (Hhat(Q|R) or N_viol), Level 2 Experimental conclusion (within the tested sample/design), Level 3 Statistical generalization (requiring sampling assumptions, estimator validity, uncertainty quantification, population model), Level 4 Mathematical theorem (requiring proof).

a_rows_sample.anchor: K = (D, R, T, Q, Pi, E, O) where D = source domain, R = representation space, T = transformations, Q = inquiries, Pi = preservation observations/contracts, E = elimination operators, O = realization/decoder operators. This is a candidate meta-structure. It is not yet an algebra.
a_rows_sample.statement: Proposes a seven-element candidate meta-structure K=(D,R,T,Q,Pi,E,O) -- source domain, representation space, transformations, inquiries, preservation observations/contracts, elimination operators, and realization/decoder operators -- explicitly marked as only a candidate meta-structure, distinct from the five-element K=(R,T,O,P,E) proposed in the prior consolidated draft.

b_rows_sample.anchor: N_viol(R)=0 <=> H_hat(Q|R)=0, not merely N_viol=0 => H_hat(Q|R)=0 ... The asymmetry is diagnostic rather than logical.
b_rows_sample.statement: Strengthens a stated implication into a full equivalence: for finite empirical support, N_viol(R)=0 and H_hat(Q|R)=0 are logically equivalent adequacy conditions (since zero conditional entropy forces every observed R-fiber to a single Q-value and vice versa), but the two remain diagnostically distinct -- N_viol as a structural witness locating collisions, H_hat(Q|R) as an information summary of remaining uncertainty.

b_rows_sample.anchor: R_{n*} is adequate, R_{n*-1} is inadequate, B_{n*}: R_{n*} -> R_{n*-1}. If adequacy is non-monotone across the chain, record that as an experimental finding rather than assuming a single boundary.
b_rows_sample.statement: Requires the boundary transition B_{n*} to be defined only when both the adjacency condition (R_{n*} adequate) and its failure (R_{n*-1} inadequate) are established, distinguishing 'lowest adequate level,' 'first preservation failure,' and 'boundary transition' as three concepts that coincide only under monotone preservation behaviour across the reduction chain.

b_rows_sample.anchor: H(R|Q)>0 => R contains variation not determined by Q ... This variation is Q-extraneous relative to the inquiry, but is not necessarily useless information.
b_rows_sample.statement: Refines the interpretation of H(R|Q)>0 from 'R contains non-inquiry payload' to the more precise 'R contains variation not determined by Q,' explicitly noting this Q-extraneous variation may still be valuable for provenance, auditability, explainability, or answering a different future inquiry -- so H(R|Q)=0 means 'no Q-extraneous variation,' not 'nothing else is useful.'

b_rows_sample.anchor: A: Is R sufficient? <-> N_viol, H_hat(Q|R). B: Does O realize the contract? <-> A(R), F(R). C: How much Q-extraneous representation remains? <-> H_hat(R|Q). D: Where does reduction cross the boundary? <-> n*.
b_rows_sample.statement: Freezes a four-question decomposition of the KR-REP-REDUCTION protocol (sufficiency, contract realization, excess representation, boundary) each matched to a specific empirical observable (N_viol/H_hat(Q|R); A(R)/F(R); H_hat(R|Q); n*), and separates three independently-diagnosable boundary-failure kinds (Representation Boundary: N_viol>0 or H(Q|R)>0; Contract Boundary: A(R)<1; Operator Boundary: H(Q|R)=0 but F(R)<1), noting 'information was lost != contract was violated != decoder was inadequate' as three genuinely different failure modes that a reduction can exhibit.

b_rows_sample.anchor: A two-state representation can have entropy close to 1 bit, while a larger representation can have much lower entropy if its distribution is highly concentrated. ... distinguish representation capacity, storage cost, Shannon entropy, minimality.
b_rows_sample.statement: Rejects a proposed requirement of strictly decreasing entropy H(R_n)<H(R_{n+1}) across the reduction chain as too strong, since entropy depends on the induced probability distribution rather than representation size; recommends requiring strictly decreasing representation CAPACITY instead, and measuring entropy, storage cost, and minimality as independent, separately reported quantities.

b_rows_sample.anchor: A failed representation transition Rn -> Rn-1 demonstrates that the transformation does not preserve the contract for that sample. It does not automatically identify a unique payload S that was removed.
b_rows_sample.statement: Warns against over-interpreting a failed reduction step: multiple eliminated components, interaction effects, transformation-induced changes, recombination, or loss of relational structure could all produce the same observed failure, so a specific eliminated set S notin Elim_{T,Pi}(D) may only be inferred when T_n has an explicit, declared elimination decomposition T_n=E_{S_n} -- otherwise report only 'T_n crosses the preservation boundary for D_i,' connecting this directly to the KR-ZERO-ORDER finding that transformation loss should not be assumed to decompose element-wise.

b_rows_sample.anchor: H(T)=H(Q)+H(T|Q), therefore H(T)>=H(Q), with equality iff H(T|Q)=0 ... T(D) = G(Q(D)) almost surely ... T(D) and Q(D) are mutually deterministically recoverable almost surely.
b_rows_sample.statement: Confirms Theorem 3's corrected attainability condition H(T(D)|Q(D))=0 and its consequence H(T)=H(Q)+H(T|Q); corrects the proposed 'Level 4: Q-Isomorphic Representation' (from Q=O∘T alone) to 'Q-Equivalent Representation,' since factorization through T establishes only that T contains enough information to determine Q, not a bijection between the full codomains Y and Q-space; the stronger, correct claim requires both H(Q(D)|T(D))=0 and H(T(D)|Q(D))=0, giving mutual a.s. recoverability T(D) <-> Q(D) rather than an unproven isomorphism.

b_rows_sample.anchor: sim_{Pi,T} = sim_Q restricted to X_{Pi,T} ... T(D) cannot literally be an element of [D]_{sim_Pi} ... D sim_{Pi,T} E_S(D) because Q(D)=Q(E_S(D)).
b_rows_sample.statement: Repairs two structural errors: (1) the equivalence relation sim_Pi must be defined as the global Q-induced relation sim_Q restricted to the T-dependent admissible domain X_{Pi,T}, not as an independent relation whose domain and defining condition are conflated; (2) a 'same fiber' claim mixing source-space [D]_{sim_Pi} (subset of X) with representation-space elements T(D), T(E_S(D)) (elements of Y) is type-incorrect -- the correct statement is D sim_{Pi,T} E_S(D) in source space, with O(T(D))=O(T(E_S(D))) as the separate representation-space consequence.

b_rows_sample.anchor: T_Adeq(Q) = {T: H(Q(D)|T(D))=0} ... T_Real(Pi) = {T: P(D in X_{Pi,T})=1 and P(O(T(D))=Q(D))=1}.
b_rows_sample.statement: Separates a previously ambiguous family T_adequate(Pi) into two explicitly distinct families -- T_Adeq(Q) (transformations adequate for the inquiry alone) and T_Real(Pi) (transformations that additionally realize the whole contract, both admissibility and the fixed decoder) -- and cautions that entropy minimization T*=argmin H(T(D)) should be stated as an infimum unless existence of the minimizer is separately established.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Zero_{T_n,Pi}(S_n;R^n) => Adeq(R^{n-1},Q,Pi) as the Zero-boundary hypothesis. I would not formulate it that strongly anymore ... Zero is itself a judgment produced by (D,T,Pi,S).
b_rows_sample.statement: Rejects a proposed strong 'Zero-boundary hypothesis' (Zero at a reduction step implies adequacy of the next representation) as formulated too strongly, arguing instead that Zero is one observable judgment produced by the underlying tuple (D,T,Pi,S), with an unnamed interaction structure I_{T,Pi}(D,S) as the real open mathematical object -- reframing the research question from 'what does Zero predict?' to 'what structure determines the boundary at which reduction ceases to preserve the contract, of which Zero is one detection mechanism?'

b_rows_sample.anchor: KR-ZERO discovered empirical constraints on context-dependent eliminability and revealed that relational structure may enter through the transformation/preservation pair. KR-REP-REDUCTION now independently investigates representation reduction ... using the KR-ZERO findings as controlled experimental factors and hypotheses -- not as definitions or conclusions.
b_rows_sample.statement: Revises the relationship between the two experiment families: rather than 'KR-ZERO discovers eliminability; KR-REP-REDUCTION tests whether Zero predicts adequacy,' the corrected position is that KR-ZERO's findings become controlled experimental factors and hypotheses for KR-REP-REDUCTION, never definitions or conclusions it inherits; elevates the representation carrier (individual element vs subset vs relational structure/hypergraph/rewriting state) to a first-class unresolved research question that must be settled before R5->R2 can be properly designed.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Adequacy != Contract Realization ... otherwise a representation could look mathematically sufficient while failing the actual preservation/operational contract.
b_rows_sample.statement: Adopts Adequacy != Contract Realization as a hard experimental rule for KR-REP-REDUCTION, distinguishing T_Adeq(Q) (sufficient information exists) from T_Real(Pi) (the specified operator O actually realizes it, and admissibility holds), so that a mathematically sufficient representation is never conflated with one that actually satisfies the operational contract.

b_rows_sample.anchor: KR-ZERO: When can source material be eliminated while preserving the contract? KR-REP-REDUCTION: How far can the representation be reduced while retaining inquiry adequacy and contract realization? The bridge is a hypothesis to test, not an established implication.
b_rows_sample.statement: States the final, precise research-question separation between the two experiment families and explicitly classifies the connecting arrow (Zero_{T_n,Pi} -> candidate elimination -> R^{n-1} -> Adequacy/Realization) as a hypothesis to be tested by KR-REP-REDUCTION, never an established implication inherited from KR-ZERO; freezes a status ledger distinguishing [CORPUS] established facts, [EXP] established mathematical results (H(Q|T)=0 adequacy; H(T|Q)=0 no-excess; hence H(T)=H(Q)+H(T|Q)), [PROP] proposed measures (Excess_Q(T)=H(T|Q); Zero predicting adequacy), and five explicit [OPEN] questions (existence of a general R5->R2 chain; the representation carrier; monotonicity; whether Zero predicts the boundary; whether relational structure in T,Pi predicts reduction difficulty).

b_rows_sample.anchor: X_Q(R) = H(R|Q) as Q-relative residual representation, with excess representation as an interpretation only when the contract explicitly says those distinctions are unnecessary.
b_rows_sample.statement: Names the final residual-representation quantity X_Q(R)=H(R|Q) as 'Q-relative residual representation,' explicitly reserving the normatively loaded term 'excess representation' only for cases where the preservation contract itself declares the residual distinctions unnecessary, on the principle that what is unnecessary for one inquiry is not thereby unnecessary for every inquiry (provenance, uncertainty bounds, or lineage may be irrelevant to Q while still required by the broader contract Pi).

b_rows_sample.anchor: R(Q,Pi) = (D, {R_n}, {T_n}, O, Q, Pi) ... M_n = (A_n, F_n, H_hat(Q|R_n), X_Q(R_n), H_hat(R_n), N_viol,n) ... n* = min{n in {1..5} : Comp_n=1.0 and A_n=1.0 and N_viol,n=0 and H_hat(Q|R_n)=0}.
b_rows_sample.statement: Presents the fully frozen KR-REP-REDUCTION experimental protocol as the object R(Q,Pi)=(D,{R_n},{T_n},O,Q,Pi) with directional chain D->T5->R5->T4->R4->T3->R3->T2->R2->T1->R1, entropy/size/count recorded independently per level (monotonicity treated as an empirical hypothesis, never assumed), a completeness-declared per-level measurement vector M_n=(A_n,F_n,H_hat(Q|R_n),X_Q(R_n),H_hat(R_n),N_viol,n), the closed-form fiber-violation formula N_viol,n=sum_r [(sum_q c_{r,q})^2 - sum_q c_{r,q}^2]/2, and the boundary definition n*=min{n: Comp_n=1, A_n=1, N_viol,n=0, H_hat(Q|R_n)=0}, with R_{n*} confirmed as the chain-specific preservation boundary only if the next-lower level fails at least one of those conditions.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The current design does not yet fully test H-RR3 (T-Pi interaction) ... the controlled 2x2 experiment is deferred ... the next useful review is of the actual implementation and its FT-1...FT-7 execution results.
b_rows_sample.statement: Notes that the frozen protocol design defers the controlled 2x2 (T_extreme/realistic x Pi_extreme/realistic) test of transformation-preservation interaction (hypothesis H-RR3), so the design phase can investigate the reduction boundary and observe an association with Zero but cannot yet establish a general T-Pi interaction law; records that the theoretical/protocol design phase is complete and the next required review step is of the actual implementation's FT-1 through FT-7 execution results, i.e. an experiment run beyond the scope of this file.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Contract failure: NO / Operator-only failure: NO / Representation failure: YES ... A_n = 1.000 at every level ... You need a representation where H(Q|R)=0 while simultaneously O(R)!=Q.
b_rows_sample.statement: Reports that hypothesis H-B (intending to separate representation failure, contract failure, and operator failure) found only representation failure occurring, since admissibility A_n=1.000 held at every level and the fixed decoder F=1.000 at the only adequate level R5, so no empirical state arose where Q was recoverable from R (H(Q|R)=0) yet the fixed operator O failed to recover Q (O(R)!=Q); concludes that a fixed decoder alone does not create an operator-boundary experiment -- a representation must retain enough information (H(Q|R)=0) while the chosen decoder still fails to use it -- and this chain never produced such a state, so adequacy and realization remain conceptually distinct even though this experiment did not empirically separate them along the reduction chain.

b_rows_sample.anchor: ascending: F_argmax = 0.8667 / descending: F_argmax = 0.3230 ... a difference of 54.37 percentage points ... yet H(Q|R2) 3.3937 vs 3.3965 is essentially unchanged.
b_rows_sample.statement: Reports a strong empirical demonstration that representation adequacy is distinct from fixed-decoder realization: reversing a rank encoding convention (ascending vs descending) leaves Hhat(Q|R2) essentially unchanged (3.3937 vs 3.3965) and N_viol similar, yet the fixed decoder's F_argmax swings by 54.37 percentage points (0.8667 vs 0.3230); interprets this as same recoverable information under different encoding convention producing very different fixed-decoder performance, i.e. a representation can preserve the same recoverable information while a particular fixed decoder performs very differently because it interprets the representation differently.

b_rows_sample.anchor: "A change carrying NO information about D..." ... The ascending and descending rank conventions are information-equivalent recodings of the same rank representation, yet they produce substantially different performance for the fixed decoder O.
b_rows_sample.statement: Requests softening the phrase 'a change carrying no information about D' to the more formal 'the ascending and descending rank conventions are information-equivalent recodings of the same rank representation, yet they produce substantially different performance for the fixed decoder O', on the ground that what matters theoretically is not an informal claim of 'no information' but that the transformation between conventions is information-preserving/invertible; connects this directly to the project's Q-equivalence concept.

b_rows_sample.anchor: bytes: 37 -> 37 -> 37 -> 25 / fields: 2 -> 2 -> 2 -> 2 / cardinality: 26826 -> 5696 -> 3288 -> 162 / entropy: 15.04 -> 12.31 -> 11.10 -> 7.17 ... there is no single obvious scalar called "amount of reduction"
b_rows_sample.statement: Reports the four measured reduction-dimension trajectories (bytes, fields, cardinality, entropy) across R5..R2 and argues the evidence only establishes that no single scalar 'amount of reduction' captures all four dimensions -- i.e. reduction is multidimensional and the measured dimensions do not collapse into one common trajectory -- but four observations along a single chain cannot establish statistical independence, so hypothesis H-D's claim that 'the four dimensions move independently' should be softened to that weaker, corpus-supported statement.

a_rows_sample.statement: Part 3 schema (ID|Invariant|Dimensions|Forbidden Collapse|Evidence|Strength|Validation Target|Notes/Boundary) plus the expected 8-family protect-statements: Identity (Representation != Identity: 'knowledge identity survives representation changes'; Expression != Meaning; Context Preservation: 'meaning requires semantic frame'); Evidence ('Observation != Interpretation', 'Evidence != Authority'); Authority ('Source authority is assigned, not intrinsic'); Transformation ('Knowledge evolution must preserve lineage'); Temporal ('Knowledge exists with temporal validity'); Reasoning ('Observation != Inference'; 'Inference requires preserved justification'); Contradiction ('Contradiction != Failure'; 'Conflicting knowledge may coexist'); Agent ('Knower identity is part of epistemic state').
