a_rows_sample.anchor: 83.67 — New invariants: I_TemporalTruth, I_EventTime, I_HistoricalIntegrity, I_TemporalAuthority, I_TemporalUncertainty, I_TemporalSupersession
a_rows_sample.statement: States six new named invariants: I_TemporalTruth (claims whose truth can change must have explicit temporal interpretation), I_EventTime (event/observation/processing times must remain distinguishable when materially relevant), I_HistoricalIntegrity (historical decisions must be interpreted using knowledge/models/policies/authorities valid at decision time), I_TemporalAuthority (authorization must be evaluated at time of action), I_TemporalUncertainty (unknown/interval timestamps must not be converted into false point precision), I_TemporalSupersession (superseded knowledge remains historically reconstructable).

a_rows_sample.anchor: 82.72 — New invariants: I_UncertaintyPreservation, I_Dependence, I_ModelUncertainty, I_Calibration, I_EpistemicPrecision, I_DecisionSensitivity, I_UncertaintyImpact
a_rows_sample.statement: States seven new named invariants: I_UncertaintyPreservation (transformations must not silently discard material uncertainty), I_Dependence (dependencies between uncertain variables must be represented when material), I_ModelUncertainty (model-structure uncertainty must be distinguished from parameter uncertainty), I_Calibration (probabilistic claims should have defined semantics and empirical calibration where applicable), I_EpistemicPrecision (output precision must not misrepresent evidence quality), I_DecisionSensitivity (when uncertainty can change the selected action, sensitivity must remain visible), I_UncertaintyImpact (material upstream evidence changes must permit identification of affected downstream knowledge/decisions).

a_rows_sample.anchor: 84.63 — New invariants: I_Intervention, I_CounterfactualProvenance, I_CounterfactualUncertainty, I_TemporalCausalSeparation, I_CounterfactualGovernance, I_Interference
a_rows_sample.statement: States six new named invariants: I_Intervention (observed association must not be represented as causal intervention without justification), I_CounterfactualProvenance (material counterfactual claims retain their model, evidence, and assumptions), I_CounterfactualUncertainty (counterfactual results preserve uncertainty and model sensitivity), I_TemporalCausalSeparation (observed historical outcomes must remain distinct from unobserved alternative outcomes), I_CounterfactualGovernance (causal feasibility of an intervention does not imply authorization to execute it), I_Interference (counterfactual analysis must account for material interactions between agents, components, or interventions).

a_rows_sample.anchor: 85.77 — New strategic invariants: I_IncentiveAlignment, I_MetricIntegrity, I_StrategicRobustness, I_AuthorizationUnknown, I_GovernanceBoundary, I_MetaGovernance, I_IncentiveObservability
a_rows_sample.statement: States seven new strategic invariants: I_IncentiveAlignment (material incentives must not systematically reward behavior violating higher-level objectives), I_MetricIntegrity (governance metrics must not be equated with the underlying objective without justified relationship), I_StrategicRobustness (governance evaluation should consider adaptive/optimizing-against-mechanism behavior), I_AuthorizationUnknown (unknown authorization must not be interpreted as permission), I_GovernanceBoundary (material governance constraints must account for alternative execution paths), I_MetaGovernance (changes to governance mechanisms are themselves governed changes), I_IncentiveObservability (where strategic behavior is material, the system should model incentives and information as part of the behavioral model).

a_rows_sample.anchor: 87.75 — New invariants: I_Aggregation, I_AuthorityExpertise, I_CollectiveConstraint, I_Quorum, I_Delegation, I_HistoricalAggregation, I_RecommendationDecision, I_DecisionAuthorization
a_rows_sample.statement: States eight new invariants: I_Aggregation (every collective decision must use an explicitly defined aggregation mechanism), I_AuthorityExpertise (expertise, evidence quality, preference, and decision authority must not be conflated), I_CollectiveConstraint (collective preference cannot override higher-order mandatory constraints), I_Quorum (a decision requiring quorum must not become valid without sufficient authorized participation), I_Delegation (delegated authority cannot exceed the authority validly delegated by the delegator), I_HistoricalAggregation (historical decisions must be interpreted using the aggregation rules valid at decision time), I_RecommendationDecision (recommendation must not automatically become decision without required authority), I_DecisionAuthorization (a decision does not automatically grant execution authority unless the governance model explicitly defines that transition).

a_rows_sample.anchor: 86.83 — New invariants: I_Mechanism, I_IncentiveCompatibility, I_IndependentVerification, I_GovernanceSurface, I_StrategicRobustness2, I_MechanismVersioning, I_FeasibleActionSpace
a_rows_sample.statement: States seven new invariants: I_Mechanism (governance mechanisms must be evaluated by resulting behavior, not only formal rules), I_IncentiveCompatibility (where truthful/desired behavior is required, the mechanism must not create a systematic incentive to deviate), I_IndependentVerification (material claims should not depend exclusively on self-reported evidence when independent verification is feasible and material), I_GovernanceSurface (material alternative execution paths must be governed, restricted, or recognized as exception paths), I_StrategicRobustness2 (governance must be evaluated under plausible strategic responses, not only cooperative behavior), I_MechanismVersioning (changes to governance mechanisms must be versioned, authorized, and historically reconstructable), I_FeasibleActionSpace (optimization must occur within the set of constitutionally, governance, and authority-valid actions).

a_rows_sample.anchor: 88.80 — New mathematical invariants: I_InformationPreservation, I_Sufficiency, I_CompressionProvenance, I_CompressionTime, I_CompressionUncertainty, I_NegativeKnowledge, I_RetrievalAssurance, I_DerivedReproducibility, I_RepresentationSeparation
a_rows_sample.statement: States nine new invariants: I_InformationPreservation (a transformation must preserve all information required for its declared assurance purpose), I_Sufficiency (a representation declared sufficient must specify the question, model, and assurance context), I_CompressionProvenance (compression must not destroy required provenance relationships), I_CompressionTime (material temporal semantics must survive representation changes), I_CompressionUncertainty (compression must not convert uncertainty into unjustified certainty), I_NegativeKnowledge (failure to retrieve evidence must not automatically imply falsity), I_RetrievalAssurance (evidence completeness requirements must be proportional to decision criticality), I_DerivedReproducibility (material derived knowledge should retain sufficient references to reproduce/audit its derivation), I_RepresentationSeparation (derived representations such as embeddings/summaries/indexes must remain distinguishable from authoritative evidence).

a_rows_sample.anchor: 89.73 — New invariants: I_Decidability, I_ComputationalFeasibility, I_ProofScope, I_ModelReality, I_VerificationState, I_Approximation, I_ComputationProvenance, I_SafetyLiveness, I_GovernanceConsistency, I_ProofEstimation
a_rows_sample.statement: States ten new invariants: I_Decidability (distinguish undecidable from merely unknown), I_ComputationalFeasibility (infeasibility must not be represented as logical impossibility), I_ProofScope (verification claims must identify model, assumptions, scope), I_ModelReality (proof of a model property must not automatically be proof of the real-world property), I_VerificationState (verification must support True/False/Unknown), I_Approximation (approximate computation must remain distinguishable from exact), I_ComputationProvenance (material derived results must retain sufficient computational-derivation information for their assurance level), I_SafetyLiveness (governance verification must distinguish safety from liveness properties), I_GovernanceConsistency (mandatory governance rules must not contain unresolved logical contradictions), I_ProofEstimation (statistical/probabilistic support must not be represented as formal proof without explicit justification).

a_rows_sample.anchor: 90.73 — New invariants: I_Complexity, I_Incremental, I_CacheValidity, I_DecisionPrecision, I_GracefulDegradation, I_DistributedTime, I_Correlation, I_AssuranceOptimization, I_CriticalityBudget
a_rows_sample.statement: States nine new invariants: I_Complexity (material computational limits must be distinguishable from logical impossibility), I_Incremental (incremental recomputation must be semantically equivalent to required full recomputation under the declared model), I_CacheValidity (cached knowledge must retain the versions/validity conditions it depends on), I_DecisionPrecision (computational precision must be sufficient relative to the decision boundary and required assurance), I_GracefulDegradation (resource exhaustion must not silently convert incomplete computation into a definitive result), I_DistributedTime (observations from distributed sources must preserve their temporal semantics), I_Correlation (multiple computational outputs must not be treated as independent evidence when they share material dependencies), I_AssuranceOptimization (performance optimization must not silently reduce declared assurance), I_CriticalityBudget (computational resources and verification depth should be proportional to decision criticality where governance permits optimization).

a_rows_sample.anchor: 91.80 — New invariants: I_Refinement, I_Representation, I_Contract, I_Trace, I_MeaningTechnology, I_SpecSync, I_Composition, I_ExecutableInvariant, I_AssuranceProvenance
a_rows_sample.statement: States nine new invariants: I_Refinement (every implementation behavior affecting governed semantics must correspond to a permitted formal-model behavior), I_Representation (every concrete state exposed as valid must map to a valid abstract state), I_Contract (component implementations must satisfy declared preconditions/postconditions/invariants), I_Trace (observable implementation traces must remain within the permitted specification trace space), I_MeaningTechnology (implementation technology must not silently redefine domain semantics), I_SpecSync (material specification changes must trigger assessment of affected implementations), I_Composition (component-level correctness must not be promoted to system-level correctness without validating interaction contracts), I_ExecutableInvariant (where feasible, critical invariants should be represented as executable contracts/tests/enforcement), I_AssuranceProvenance (implementation-correctness claims must retain evidence of how they were established).

a_rows_sample.anchor: 92.79 — New invariants: I_AtomicInvariant, I_Concurrency, I_Conflict, I_Version, I_CausalOrder, I_Idempotency, I_AuthorizationFreshness, I_AuthorityUniqueness, I_DecisionSnapshot, I_GlobalInvariant, I_IrreversibleAction
a_rows_sample.statement: States eleven new invariants: I_AtomicInvariant (every atomic transition must preserve declared transaction-scope invariants), I_Concurrency (concurrent executions must not produce a state forbidden by the sequential spec), I_Conflict (unmergeable concurrent modifications must become explicit conflicts, not silent overwrites), I_Version (material writes must identify the state version validated against), I_CausalOrder (causal relationships must not be inferred solely from arrival order), I_Idempotency (idempotent operations must preserve semantic result under duplicate execution), I_AuthorizationFreshness (authorization decisions must satisfy freshness requirements per criticality), I_AuthorityUniqueness (distributed systems must prevent simultaneous conflicting authoritative states where exclusive authority is defined), I_DecisionSnapshot (material decisions must identify the evidence/policy/model/authority state used), I_GlobalInvariant (a multi-component invariant must be enforced at a boundary observing the combined state), I_IrreversibleAction (irreversible actions require assurance proportional to impact and rollback inability).

a_rows_sample.anchor: 93.75 — The strongest recovery invariant ... I_Recovery: for every supported failure mode F, recovery must either restore a valid state, or explicitly enter a declared degraded/unknown state. The system must never silently fabricate validity.
a_rows_sample.statement: States the strongest recovery invariant I_Recovery: for every supported failure mode, recovery must restore a valid state or explicitly enter a declared degraded/unknown state — never silently fabricate validity.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 93.78 — New invariants: I_AtomicRecovery, I_Durability, I_RecoveryValidity, I_FailureHistory, I_Reconciliation, I_RecoveryFreshness, I_RetrySafety, I_Compensation, I_FailureEpistemics, I_RecoveryAssurance
a_rows_sample.statement: States nine further new invariants: I_AtomicRecovery (failed atomic transitions must not leave semantically invalid committed states), I_Durability (a committed authoritative state must remain recoverable per its durability contract), I_RecoveryValidity (recovery must produce a valid state or explicitly degraded/unknown state), I_FailureHistory (recovery must not silently erase evidence of failure/partial execution/compensation), I_Reconciliation (recovered state must be reconciled with surviving authoritative state where divergence is possible), I_RecoveryFreshness (a recovered state must not be represented as current unless freshness is established), I_RetrySafety (retryable operations must have explicit duplicate-execution semantics), I_Compensation (compensation must remain distinguishable from perfect rollback and preserve residual effects), I_FailureEpistemics (observed failure, inferred cause, and unresolved cause must remain distinct knowledge states), I_RecoveryAssurance (recovery assurance must include correctness, completeness, freshness, and provenance appropriate to criticality).

a_rows_sample.anchor: 94.71 — New invariants: I_AuthorityIntegrity, I_AINonAuthority, I_TrustBoundary, I_AuthSeparation, I_LeastPrivilege, I_ProvenanceSecurity, I_IntegrityTruth, I_TemporalTrust, I_AdversarialEvidence, I_SeparationOfDuties, I_MultiPartyAuthorization, I_SecurityEvidence
a_rows_sample.statement: States twelve new security invariants: I_AuthorityIntegrity (authority must originate from an authorized governance mechanism, not an untrusted claim), I_AINonAuthority (AI-generated statements must not acquire authoritative status solely through generation), I_TrustBoundary (crossing a trust boundary must not automatically increase authority/trust level), I_AuthSeparation (identity verification must remain distinct from permission verification), I_LeastPrivilege (actors must possess no more capability than required), I_ProvenanceSecurity (material claims must retain sufficient provenance to distinguish authoritative/verified/unverified/untrusted origins), I_IntegrityTruth (integrity verification must not be represented as proof of semantic truth), I_TemporalTrust (trust/identity/authority/credentials must be evaluated within their applicable time interval), I_AdversarialEvidence (evidence exposed to material adversarial manipulation must carry a trust/risk assessment), I_SeparationOfDuties (no single actor may perform mutually exclusive roles in the same decision process where required), I_MultiPartyAuthorization (actions requiring multiple authorities must not execute until all required independent authorizations are established), I_SecurityEvidence (material security events must remain observable and attributable so they can become auditable evidence).

a_rows_sample.anchor: 95.69 — Privacy as a mathematical invariant ... I_Privacy: for every actor, purpose, time, and context, the information accessible through the system must remain within the authorized information boundary.
a_rows_sample.statement: States the core privacy invariant I_Privacy: accessible information must remain within the authorized information boundary for every actor/purpose/time/context.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 95.75 — New invariants: I_InformationAuthorization, I_PurposeLimitation, I_DataMinimization, I_InformationFlow, I_DerivedProtection, I_AuthorizedRetrieval, I_PrivacyComposition, I_TemporalPrivacy, I_DeletionPropagation, I_AuditPrivacy, I_AIContextBoundary
a_rows_sample.statement: States eleven further new invariants: I_InformationAuthorization (permission to act must not automatically imply permission to access all relevant information), I_PurposeLimitation (knowledge access must respect the declared/authorized purpose), I_DataMinimization (only information necessary for the purpose should be exposed where practicable), I_InformationFlow (restricted information must not flow into less-protected representations without authorized transformation), I_DerivedProtection (derived knowledge/summaries/embeddings/predictions/AI outputs remain subject to applicable information controls), I_AuthorizedRetrieval (access policy should constrain retrieval, not merely final presentation, wherever feasible), I_PrivacyComposition (repeated disclosures must be evaluated collectively), I_TemporalPrivacy (information authorization/classification must remain valid for the applicable time interval), I_DeletionPropagation (material deletion requirements must evaluate derived representations/downstream artifacts), I_AuditPrivacy (conflicts between audit retention and privacy requirements must be explicitly governed, not silently resolved), I_AIContextBoundary (an AI agent must receive only knowledge within its authorized epistemic boundary).

b_rows_sample.anchor: We now challenge an important assumption ... U_i=U_i(a_i,a_{-i}) ... The organization is no longer merely a collection of decision-makers. It becomes a strategic system.
b_rows_sample.statement: Challenges the prior assumption that agents optimize independently (a_i*=argmax U_i(a_i)), replacing it with U_i=U_i(a_i,a_{-i}) where a_{-i} is other agents' actions; the organization becomes a strategic system.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 85.1 — Local optimization becomes insufficient ... a_i*=argmax_{a_i} U_i(a_i,a_{-i}). The optimal action depends on expectations about others.
b_rows_sample.statement: States that under U_i(a_i,a_{-i}), an agent's optimal action depends on expectations about other agents' actions, making purely local optimization insufficient.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 85.2 — Experiment 1: strategic interaction ... Agent A chooses A_1 if B chooses B_1, A_2 if B chooses B_2. Expected: A* cannot be determined independently of B. Result: PASS
b_rows_sample.statement: Experiment 1: agent A's optimal choice depends on agent B's choice (A_1 if B_1, A_2 if B_2), so A* cannot be determined independently of B; result PASS.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 85.3 — The organization has multiple utility functions ... U_1,...,U_n for agents and U_org. No guarantee U_i=U_org. Individual rationality ≠ organizational rationality.
b_rows_sample.statement: States there is no guarantee individual agent utility U_i equals organizational utility U_org; individual rationality ≠ organizational rationality.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 85.4 — Experiment 2: conflicting incentives ... Agent bonus for NumberOfChanges; organization values SystemStability. U_A=Changes, U_org=Stability. Expected: IncentiveConflict. Result: PASS
b_rows_sample.statement: Experiment 2: an agent bonused on NumberOfChanges while the organization values SystemStability produces IncentiveConflict; result PASS.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 85.5 — Strategic adaptation ... Agent knows GovernanceRule: Reject if Risk>Threshold. The agent can potentially modify how risk is measured. Instead of reducing ActualRisk, it optimizes MeasuredRisk. This is a classic governance problem.
b_rows_sample.statement: Describes the classic governance problem of an agent, knowing a risk threshold rule, optimizing MeasuredRisk rather than ActualRisk.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 85.6 — Experiment 3: gaming the metric ... True risk R=80. Governance observes hat-R=40. Agent intentionally lowers hat-R without lowering R. Expected: MetricGaming. Result: PASS
b_rows_sample.statement: Experiment 3: an agent intentionally lowering the measured risk (hat-R=40) while true risk stays R=80 is MetricGaming; result PASS.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 85.7 — Goodhart's Law ... When a measure becomes a target, it may cease to be a good measure. M=f(S) correlated with S. Once the agent optimizes max M, the relationship M→S may change.
b_rows_sample.statement: States Goodhart's Law formally: a measure M=f(S) correlated with a desired state S can decouple from S once agents optimize directly for M.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 85.8 — Experiment 4 ... M=DeploymentFrequency, target M≥20/month. Teams split trivial changes into many deployments. M↑ but meaningful delivery does not. Expected: MetricDecoupling. Result: PASS
b_rows_sample.statement: Experiment 4 (Goodhart example): a deployment-frequency target causes teams to split trivial changes, raising the metric without raising true delivery value — MetricDecoupling; result PASS.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 85.9 — KnowledgeOS must therefore distinguish metric optimization from goal achievement ... Metric ≠ Objective. ObservedMetric ≠ TrueObjective.
b_rows_sample.statement: States KnowledgeOS must distinguish Metric ≠ Objective and ObservedMetric ≠ TrueObjective.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 85.10 — Experiment 5 ... ComplianceScore=98% but the score is optimized directly by agents. Expected: KnowledgeOS should ask whether Score remains a valid proxy for GovernanceObjective. Result: PASS
b_rows_sample.statement: Experiment 5: a 98% ComplianceScore directly optimized by agents should prompt KnowledgeOS to question whether the score remains a valid proxy for the true governance objective; result PASS.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 85.11 — Principal-agent problem ... Principal wants U_P. Agent controls actions a. Principal may not observe a perfectly. Agent may have incentive to act differently from principal's desired behavior.
b_rows_sample.statement: Introduces the principal-agent problem: a principal wanting U_P cannot perfectly observe the agent's actions a, giving the agent incentive to deviate from desired behavior.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 85.12 — Experiment 6: hidden action ... Principal cannot observe how an agent performs a task. Agent rewarded on ReportedSuccess, can report success without achieving the objective. Expected: MoralHazard. Result: PASS
b_rows_sample.statement: Experiment 6: rewarding an agent on self-reported success (ReportedSuccess) when the principal cannot observe the actual action is MoralHazard; result PASS.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 85.13 — Hidden information ... Agent may possess information I_A that the principal does not have. Information_A ≠ Information_P. This creates InformationAsymmetry.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines InformationAsymmetry: the agent may hold information I_A the principal lacks (Information_A ≠ Information_P).

b_rows_sample.anchor: 85.14 — Experiment 7 ... Developer knows a dependency is fragile. Architecture board does not. Developer recommends migration plan without disclosing the risk. Expected: InformationAsymmetry. Result: PASS
b_rows_sample.statement: Experiment 7 (engineering example): a developer knowing a dependency is fragile but not disclosing it to the architecture board is InformationAsymmetry; result PASS.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 85.15 — KnowledgeOS changes the information structure ... KnowledgeOS can potentially reduce InformationAsymmetry by making relevant evidence accessible and traceable. But it cannot assume AllInformation=AvailableInformation.
b_rows_sample.statement: Argues KnowledgeOS can reduce InformationAsymmetry via accessible/traceable evidence, but must not assume all information is thereby captured (AllInformation ≠ AvailableInformation).

b_rows_sample.anchor: 85.16 — Experiment 8 ... Developer knows about an undocumented production workaround. KnowledgeOS has no observation of it. Expected: HiddenInformation. Result: PASS. This connects directly back to Step 81. Observability remains fundamental even in strategic environments.
b_rows_sample.statement: Experiment 8: an undocumented production workaround known only to a developer and unobserved by KnowledgeOS is HiddenInformation; result PASS; explicitly links back to Step 81's observability foundations.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 85.17 — Strategic information withholding ... An agent may intentionally withhold information because disclosure changes its payoff. Disclosure itself can become a strategic action.
b_rows_sample.statement: Argues disclosure itself becomes a strategic action when an agent's payoff depends on whether information is revealed.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 85.18 — Experiment 9 ... Agent knows evidence E. If disclosed U_A=5, if withheld U_A=10. Agent has incentive to withhold E. Expected: StrategicNondisclosure. Result: PASS
b_rows_sample.statement: Experiment 9: an agent whose withholding payoff (U_A=10) exceeds its disclosure payoff (U_A=5) for evidence E exhibits StrategicNondisclosure; result PASS.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 85.19 — Evidence cannot simply be trusted because it exists ... SourceIntent and IncentiveStructure. This does not mean every source is untrustworthy. It means source incentives can be relevant to evidence evaluation.
b_rows_sample.statement: States that source incentive structure and intent are relevant to evidence evaluation (without implying blanket distrust of sources).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Reality ≠ Observation ≠ Information ≠ Evidence ≠ Knowledge ≠ Decision ≠ Action.
a_rows_sample.statement: Axiom A1 (Semantic Separation) opens Part I of the v2.0 rewrite: reality, observation, information, evidence and knowledge are held to occupy different semantic roles unless a formal equivalence is explicitly established, giving the epistemic lifecycle Reality->Observation->Information->Knowledge->Gap->Inquiry->Determination->Decision->Action->New Knowledge.

a_rows_sample.anchor: If there exist ω1,ω2 ∈ Ω such that ω1≠ω2 and ρ(ω1)=ρ(ω2), then ρ is not injective and therefore cannot uniquely identify the underlying state of reality.
a_rows_sample.statement: Proposition 3.1 with proof: an observation map rho:Omega->I need not be injective, so KnowledgeOS must never silently infer Observed(x)=>Reality(x).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Adequate(R,Q,Γ) ⟺ 𝓡_req(Q,Γ) ⊆ Dist(R)
a_rows_sample.statement: The Representation Adequacy Principle: a representation is adequate only if it preserves the distinctions required to answer the declared inquiry under context Gamma, avoiding the impossible requirement of preserving every conceivable distinction.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Suppose there exist x1,x2 ∈ X such that x1≠x2 but π(x1)=π(x2). Then any question Q whose required distinction includes x1≠x2 cannot, in general, be answered correctly from π(x) alone.
a_rows_sample.statement: Theorem 16.1 (Loss of Required Distinction), with proof by the impossibility of a deterministic function distinguishing two values a projection maps identically; establishes that a system can be perfectly internally consistent and still epistemically inadequate.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Δ_t = {r ∈ Req_t : ¬Sat(K_t,r)} ... Gap = Unsatisfied Requirements.
a_rows_sample.statement: Redefines the Knowledge Gap as a set-theoretic construction (unsatisfied requirements under the current epistemic contract) rather than a subtraction Delta=IdealKnowledge-Knowledge, explicitly rejecting the latter as generally undefined because the two objects need not belong to a common algebraic space.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Zero(K_t,EC_t) ⟺ Δ_t = ∅ ... Therefore Zero is contract-relative.
a_rows_sample.statement: Definition 23.1 (Epistemic Zero): Zero means no requirement of the declared epistemic contract remains unsatisfied; explicitly not K_t=Reality and not 'all possible knowledge is known.'

a_rows_sample.anchor: Δ_{t+1} ⊆ Δ_t ... every requirement satisfied at t remains satisfied at t+1 ... This theorem depends on the contract remaining fixed.
a_rows_sample.statement: Theorems 24.1 (Zero Equivalence) and 25.1 (Gap Reduction) are proved, with an explicit limitation that gap comparison across differing contracts (EC_t != EC_{t+1}) requires an explicit compatibility mapping — 'moving the goalposts' is formally blocked by the Contract Compatibility principle GapComparison=>ContractCompatibility.

a_rows_sample.anchor: V(K_t) ⊆ V(K_{t+1}) ∧ H(K_t) ⊆ H(K_{t+1}) ... Historical existence ≠ Current epistemic standing.
a_rows_sample.statement: Axiom A6 (Historical Preservation) plus the constitutional distinction between historical existence and current epistemic standing: a proposition can move Supported->Retracted without deleting the historical fact that it was once asserted and supported; replaces 'universal epistemic monotonicity' with this weaker, correct invariant.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Truth ≠ Evaluation ≠ Determination ≠ Decision.
a_rows_sample.statement: Axiom A2 (Epistemic Pipeline Separation), with the worked consequence that EVal(p)=Supported does not mean Decision=Permit (a governance policy may instead require HumanReview) — epistemic status is explicitly not equivalent to operational authorization.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Contr(p) ⇏ ∀q ∈ 𝒫, q. ... Local contradiction ⇏ Global epistemic collapse.
a_rows_sample.statement: Axiom A5 (Non-Explosion): KnowledgeOS explicitly rejects the classical explosion principle as a system rule, requiring contradiction to be scoped and represented rather than collapsing all propositions.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 𝒪_core = {ASSERT, LINK, REVISE, RETRACT, ISOLATE}
a_rows_sample.statement: Names the frozen candidate core operation interface (introduce an assertion, establish a relation, change content while preserving history, withdraw standing without erasing history, and restrict propagation of a contradiction or dangerous structure), with full preconditions/postconditions/composition laws deferred to later parts.

a_rows_sample.anchor: ABK-1 is a validated candidate-adequate architecture for the target problem class.
a_rows_sample.statement: Explicitly withdraws the earlier claim that ABK-1 is 'the universally unique minimal KnowledgeOS kernel' as circular, replacing it with the weaker, defensible claim that global minimality remains unproven unless the candidate representation space and equivalence relation are formally characterized.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Ontology defines what kinds of things KnowledgeOS reasons about. Representation defines how those things are encoded.
a_rows_sample.statement: States the ontology/representation boundary underlying Part II's many-sorted type system (Ent, Val, Attr, Dim, Prop, Asrt, Obs, Evd, Src, Rel, Evt, St, Ctx, Part, Prov, ES, Req, Inq, EC, Pol, Dec, Act), asserting a database/graph/JSON/RDF/object-model representation is never the ontology itself.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Let D be a value domain and n:D→ℝ a numerical encoding. If no semantic operation corresponding to subtraction is defined on D, then n(x)−n(y) cannot ... be interpreted as a valid semantic difference.
a_rows_sample.statement: Theorem 2.1 (Representation does not imply arithmetic validity), with proof, establishing that numerical computability of a difference does not by itself establish semantic validity of that difference.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Supports(e,p) ⇏ Truth(p).
a_rows_sample.statement: Proposition 2.1, proved by the type-mismatch argument that support is an epistemic evidence-proposition relation while truth is a semantic proposition-model relation with different domains and meanings; called one of the most important anti-confusion principles in KnowledgeOS.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Let R:𝕂→X be a representation function. Suppose there exist K1≠K2 such that R(K1)=R(K2). If there exists an inquiry Q such that Answer(Q,K1,Γ)≠Answer(Q,K2,Γ), then R is inadequate for Q,Γ.
a_rows_sample.statement: Theorem 2.3 (Semantically lossy representation), with proof, generalizing Part I's Theorem 16.1 to the knowledge-state level and formally establishing why representation adequacy must be question-relative.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Status_Γ,EC(p)=σ ... We deliberately do not define one universal ordered list such as Unknown<Supported<Proven<Rejected.
a_rows_sample.statement: Epistemic Status is defined as contract- and context-dependent rather than a single universal total order, giving formal meaning to 'unknown' as neither true nor false rather than as a weaker degree of falsity.

a_rows_sample.anchor: If Conflict is represented as a local relation on propositions, then the existence of a conflict concerning p does not by itself entail conflict concerning arbitrary q.
a_rows_sample.statement: Theorem 2.5 (Locality theorem for contradiction), with proof, giving the formal ontological grounding for the non-explosion axiom stated in Part I.

a_rows_sample.anchor: KnowledgeOS SHALL NOT treat stored data as knowledge merely because it is stored.
a_rows_sample.statement: Ten Foundational Type Invariants (I1-I10) close Part II — proposition/evidence separation, observation/proposition separation, decision/action separation, epistemic-status/truth separation, identity/state separation, evidence/truth separation, contract relativity, historical preservation, non-explosion, and representation independence — as the boundaries preventing KnowledgeOS from collapsing into an ordinary information system.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Truth → Evidence → Evaluation → Determination → Decision ... The arrows indicate dependency possibilities, not logical equivalence.
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines five explicit semantic layers (Truth_M(p), Evid(e,p), Eval(K,p,Gamma), Det(K,p,EC,Gamma), Dec(K,Q,P,A,Gamma)) to prevent classical truth, evidence, uncertainty, contradiction and operational determination from being silently collapsed into one binary logic with metadata.

b_rows_sample.statement: Identifies three items of work blocked until governance acts: once Zero's residence is decided, the K-interface membership question must be re-run; once evidence's residence is decided, the aggregate boundary follows; once the federation-vs-product decision is made, the Delta-mapping proofs (delta embeds in Delta, tau embeds in Delta, Update/R equal Delta restricted to S_E) can proceed, each stated in TV-F-009 as an equivalence or refinement proof obligation.

a_rows_sample.anchor: EXPERIMENT ID KR-BRIDGE-01-ZERO-PRESERVATION-2026-09 ... Determine whether there is any reproducible empirical or structural relationship between: A. elimination/Transformation-relative Zero, B. representation preservation/adequacy. WITHOUT assuming that Zero is a preservation criterion. ... The exp
a_rows_sample.statement: Commissions KR-BRIDGE-01-ZERO-PRESERVATION-2026-09, a bridge/falsification experiment explicitly designed to determine whether there is any reproducible relationship between elimination/Transformation-relative Zero and representation-preservation adequacy without assuming Zero is a preservation criterion, required to remain capable of falsifying the hypothesized relationship, and prohibited from constructing an algebra, pre-selecting a carrier, modifying Theory v1.2, creating Theory v1.3, selecting a kernel operator, or merging KR-ZERO and KR-REP-REDUCTION into one formalism.

a_rows_sample.anchor: KR-ZERO: ~89.7% singleton-determined levels ... ~8.2% irreducible levels ... Does NOT establish Zero as a preservation criterion. KR-REP-REDUCTION: R5 adequate, R4 inadequate ... Found no observed Zero/boundary association in that experiment. Does NOT establish a KR-ZERO law. ... These experiments a
a_rows_sample.statement: Summarizes the existing empirical baseline the bridge experiment builds on: KR-ZERO (89.7% singleton-determined, 8.2% irreducible, does not establish Zero as a preservation criterion) and KR-REP-REDUCTION (R5 adequate/R4 inadequate, no observed Zero/boundary association), framed as complementary but analytically independent results whose missing bridge the new experiment must test rather than assume.

a_rows_sample.anchor: H0: Zero and preservation are not systematically related in the tested regime. H1: Zero is associated with preservation under specified conditions. H2: Zero is predictive of preservation only under particular transformation/observable/contract configurations. H3: Any apparent relationship is explain
a_rows_sample.statement: Specifies four competing hypotheses to be distinguished -- H0 no systematic relationship, H1 association under specified conditions, H2 predictive only under particular transformation/observable/contract configurations, H3 apparent relationship explained by a confounding factor (transformation class, contract, observable, redundancy, representation regime) -- with an explicit instruction not to privilege H1, and defines success as producing a clear positive or negative result regarding the tested relationship.

a_rows_sample.anchor: USE A PARALLEL REPRESENTATION FAMILY. Do NOT use only a deterministic sequential chain. A sequential chain ... has a data-processing constraint H(Q|Rn) <= H(Q|R(n-1)) and therefore cannot test non-monotone adequacy. The present experiment requires independently generated representations: Ra = Ta(D),
a_rows_sample.statement: Mandates the critical design rule that the bridge experiment use a parallel representation family (independently generated representations Ra=Ta(D), Rb=Tb(D), neither a deterministic function of the other) rather than only a deterministic sequential chain, since a sequential chain's data-processing constraint H(Q|Rn)<=H(Q|R(n-1)) structurally prevents testing non-monotone adequacy -- directly addressing the H-C category error found in the prior KR-REP-REDUCTION reviews.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The mathematical carrier must be the minimum structure required by the actual experiment. Do not declare: set, graph, hypergraph, lattice, matroid, closure system, rewriting system, category, algebra as the carrier before the experiment. ... clearly distinguish: experimental carrier, mathematical ca
a_rows_sample.statement: Prohibits declaring any specific mathematical carrier (set, graph, hypergraph, lattice, matroid, closure system, rewriting system, category, algebra) before the experiment runs, requiring the carrier to be the minimum structure the experiment actually needs, and mandates keeping experimental carrier, mathematical carrier, and future KnowledgeOS knowledge representation explicitly distinct with no unevidenced transfer between them.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Use a finite structured source D ... rich enough to permit: redundancy, relational dependence, context dependence, individually removable elements, jointly non-removable groups, preservation and information-loss cases. ... For every source case store D, Q(D), contract parameters, transformation para
a_rows_sample.statement: Requires the source data D to be a finite, deterministically-seeded structured source rich enough to permit redundancy, relational dependence, context dependence, individually removable elements, jointly non-removable groups, and both preservation and information-loss cases, with complete persistence of every source case's D, Q(D), contract parameters, transformation parameters, Zero ground truth, every representation, adequacy result, and decoder result, so no result depends on regenerated or hidden data.

a_rows_sample.anchor: At minimum construct representations with: R_A: information-preserving transformation, R_B: controlled lossy transformation, R_C: redundancy-removing transformation, R_D: relational/context-sensitive transformation. ... Do not optimize transformations after seeing results.
a_rows_sample.statement: Requires at minimum four independently constructed representations -- R_A (information-preserving), R_B (controlled lossy), R_C (redundancy-removing), R_D (relational/context-sensitive) -- each fully specified (transformation ID, mathematical definition, input/output type, deterministic/random status, seed, provenance, expected information effect, contract dependencies) before results are examined, with no post-hoc optimization of transformations.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Define Q BEFORE generating representations. ... Adequate(R) iff Q is recoverable from R. Operationally measure both empirical conditional information Hhat(Q|R) and exact semantic violation count Nviol ... Do not treat Hhat(Q|R)=0 as proof that population H(Q|R)=0.
a_rows_sample.statement: Requires the preservation target Q to be defined before representations are generated, with adequacy defined as Q being recoverable from R, measured operationally via both empirical conditional information Hhat(Q|R) and an exact semantic violation count Nviol, while never treating the empirical Hhat(Q|R)=0 as proof of the population-level H(Q|R)=0.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Use the existing Transformation-relative Zero definition. For elimination E_S: Zero(T,Pi,S;D) iff Pi(T(D)) = Pi(T(E_S(D))). ... NEVER DEFINE ZERO USING Q. Do NOT define: Zero(S) := Q(D) = Q(E_S(D)). That would build the desired bridge into the definition. Zero must use its own declared observable/op
a_rows_sample.statement: Reuses the existing Transformation-relative Zero definition Zero(T,Pi,S;D) iff Pi(T(D))=Pi(T(E_S(D))), calculated independently from the preservation measurement, and issues a critical prohibition against ever defining Zero in terms of Q (e.g. Zero(S):=Q(D)=Q(E_S(D))), since that would build the desired bridge directly into the definition and make the experiment circular; Zero must use its own declared observable Pi while preservation uses Q.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The experiment must deliberately seek all four cells: Zero+Adequate, Zero+Inadequate, Non-Zero+Adequate, Non-Zero+Inadequate. ... Zero+Inadequate would directly demonstrate that Zero is not sufficient for preservation. Non-Zero+Adequate would demonstrate that Zero is not necessary for preservation.
a_rows_sample.statement: Requires a four-cell crossing design (Zero+Adequate, Zero+Inadequate, Non-Zero+Adequate, Non-Zero+Inadequate) deliberately populated in all cells where possible, noting that a populated Zero+Inadequate cell would show Zero is not sufficient for preservation and a populated Non-Zero+Adequate cell would show Zero is not necessary for it, while an empty cell must be investigated for generator/contract/transformation/sample-size/mathematical-necessity/implementation causes rather than treated as a law.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Sweep the parameters that plausibly influence the relationship, including redundancy level, group size, representation loss, transformation class, observable Pi, preservation target Q, contract parameters, context dependence, relational interaction, source cardinality. Every parameter sweep must be
a_rows_sample.statement: Requires declared-in-advance parameter sweeps across ten plausibly influential parameters (redundancy level, group size, representation loss, transformation class, observable Pi, preservation target Q, contract parameters, context dependence, relational interaction, source cardinality), explicitly forbidding silent tuning to obtain balanced four-way cells.

a_rows_sample.anchor: At minimum stratify results by: transformation T, observable Pi, contract C, representation family, source structure, elimination size |S|. Report both pooled relationship and stratified relationship. An association that disappears after stratification must NOT be reported as a general Zero-preserva
a_rows_sample.statement: Mandates confounding analysis stratifying results by transformation T, observable Pi, contract C, representation family, source structure, and elimination size |S|, reporting both pooled and stratified relationships, and forbidding reporting an association as a general Zero-preservation relationship if it disappears after stratification.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Explicitly test T x Pi ... Do not classify transformations as simply relational / element-wise and stop there. Measure the actual interaction between transformation and observable. If higher-order or preservation behavior occurs under an element-wise transformation, record it. Do not resurrect the w
a_rows_sample.statement: Requires explicitly testing the transformation-times-observable interaction (T x Pi) rather than stopping at a coarse relational/element-wise classification, recording higher-order or preservation behavior even under element-wise transformations, and explicitly forbidding resurrection of the already-withdrawn claim that relational transformations produce higher order while element-wise ones do not.

a_rows_sample.anchor: retain the KR-ZERO determination-order analysis. Measure k=1,2,3,...,irreducible where feasible. Do not assume higher k -> more reduction, higher k -> less preservation, irreducibility -> information loss. Those are hypotheses to test, not definitions. In particular, do not equate determination orde
a_rows_sample.statement: Requires retaining the KR-ZERO determination-order analysis (k=1,2,3,...,irreducible) in the bridge experiment while explicitly forbidding the assumptions that higher k implies more reduction, less preservation, or that irreducibility implies information loss -- these remain hypotheses to test -- and forbidding equating determination order with preservation boundary.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Retain the KR-REP-REDUCTION principle that reduction is multidimensional. Measure independently ... encoded size, cardinality, field count, representation entropy, number of relations, number of records, other declared structural measures. Do NOT invent a single 'reduction score' ... If a decoder is
a_rows_sample.statement: Requires measuring reduction multidimensionally (encoded size, cardinality, field count, entropy, relation count, record count, other declared measures) without inventing a single reduction score or assuming statistical independence among dimensions, and requires keeping representation adequacy strictly separate from decoder realization when a decoder is used, including an invertible recoding control to rule out decoder-sensitivity confounds.

a_rows_sample.anchor: CONTROL A: A known information-preserving representation. CONTROL B: A known information-destroying representation. CONTROL C: An invertible recoding of the same representation. CONTROL D: A representation where Zero is known to vary independently of the preservation target ... CONTROL E: Positive c
a_rows_sample.statement: Specifies six mandatory controls that must execute before any interpretation: A) a known information-preserving representation; B) a known information-destroying representation; C) an invertible recoding of the same representation; D) a representation where Zero is known to vary independently of the preservation target (if the generator permits); E) a positive control that the preservation test can detect information loss; F) a positive control that the Zero test can detect elimination differences.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Use independent TRAIN and TEST populations. Declare seeds, population size, generator, parameter distributions before execution. Persist the complete populations. No training result may influence test generation. No test result may influence transformation definitions. No post-hoc filtering may be u
a_rows_sample.statement: Requires independent train/test populations with pre-declared seeds, population size, generator, and parameter distributions, complete population persistence, and strict separation preventing training results from influencing test generation, test results from influencing transformation definitions, or post-hoc filtering to manufacture desired four-way cell counts.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Q1: Can Zero occur while preservation fails? Q2: Can preservation hold while Zero fails? Q3: Does the Zero/Adequacy relationship survive changes in T? ... Q7: Does determination order predict preservation independently of T/Pi/C? Q8: Does the relationship survive an invertible recoding? Q9/Q10: Is a
a_rows_sample.statement: Mandates that the implementation explicitly answer ten falsification questions (Q1-Q10) covering whether Zero can occur without preservation and vice versa, whether the relationship survives changes in T, Pi, contract, redundancy, an invertible recoding, whether determination order predicts preservation independent of T/Pi/C, and whether any apparent relationship is explained by transformation class or by the preservation target Q itself.

a_rows_sample.anchor: OUTCOME A -- NO RELATIONSHIP OBSERVED ... does NOT prove universal independence. OUTCOME B -- CONDITIONAL RELATIONSHIP ... Do NOT generalize. OUTCOME C -- ROBUST RELATIONSHIP ... Only in this case may a formal bridge hypothesis be proposed for a new experiment. OUTCOME D -- DESIGN FAILURE ... Do NOT
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines four mutually exclusive possible outcome classes for the experiment: A) no relationship observed (does not prove universal independence); B) conditional relationship under particular configurations (must not be generalized); C) robust relationship surviving transformations/observables/contracts/controls (the only case permitting a formal bridge hypothesis for a new experiment); D) design failure, in which case results must not be interpreted theoretically and the experiment must be revised.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Create verification/zero-algebra/KR-BRIDGE-01-AUDIT-2026-09.md ... verify source generation, Q generation, Pi generation, transformation definitions, elimination definitions, Zero calculation, adequacy calculation, decoder calculation, train/test independence, seed handling, serialization, parameter
a_rows_sample.statement: Specifies two required deliverable artifacts with exact filenames -- verification/zero-algebra/KR-BRIDGE-01-AUDIT-2026-09.md, a 16-item forensic audit covering source/Q/Pi/transformation/elimination/Zero/adequacy/decoder generation, train/test independence, seeds, serialization, parameter sweeps, contingency tables, statistics, absence of post-hoc selection, and reproducibility; and verification/zero-algebra/KR-BRIDGE-01-RESULTS-2026-09.md, a 22-section result document (executive verdict through epistemic status) -- with every important empirical claim required to trace to persisted data.

b_rows_sample.anchor: N_viol(R)=0 <=> H_hat(Q|R)=0, not merely N_viol=0 => H_hat(Q|R)=0 ... The asymmetry is diagnostic rather than logical.
b_rows_sample.statement: Strengthens a stated implication into a full equivalence: for finite empirical support, N_viol(R)=0 and H_hat(Q|R)=0 are logically equivalent adequacy conditions (since zero conditional entropy forces every observed R-fiber to a single Q-value and vice versa), but the two remain diagnostically distinct -- N_viol as a structural witness locating collisions, H_hat(Q|R) as an information summary of remaining uncertainty.

b_rows_sample.anchor: R_{n*} is adequate, R_{n*-1} is inadequate, B_{n*}: R_{n*} -> R_{n*-1}. If adequacy is non-monotone across the chain, record that as an experimental finding rather than assuming a single boundary.
b_rows_sample.statement: Requires the boundary transition B_{n*} to be defined only when both the adjacency condition (R_{n*} adequate) and its failure (R_{n*-1} inadequate) are established, distinguishing 'lowest adequate level,' 'first preservation failure,' and 'boundary transition' as three concepts that coincide only under monotone preservation behaviour across the reduction chain.

b_rows_sample.anchor: H(R|Q)>0 => R contains variation not determined by Q ... This variation is Q-extraneous relative to the inquiry, but is not necessarily useless information.
b_rows_sample.statement: Refines the interpretation of H(R|Q)>0 from 'R contains non-inquiry payload' to the more precise 'R contains variation not determined by Q,' explicitly noting this Q-extraneous variation may still be valuable for provenance, auditability, explainability, or answering a different future inquiry -- so H(R|Q)=0 means 'no Q-extraneous variation,' not 'nothing else is useful.'

b_rows_sample.anchor: A: Is R sufficient? <-> N_viol, H_hat(Q|R). B: Does O realize the contract? <-> A(R), F(R). C: How much Q-extraneous representation remains? <-> H_hat(R|Q). D: Where does reduction cross the boundary? <-> n*.
b_rows_sample.statement: Freezes a four-question decomposition of the KR-REP-REDUCTION protocol (sufficiency, contract realization, excess representation, boundary) each matched to a specific empirical observable (N_viol/H_hat(Q|R); A(R)/F(R); H_hat(R|Q); n*), and separates three independently-diagnosable boundary-failure kinds (Representation Boundary: N_viol>0 or H(Q|R)>0; Contract Boundary: A(R)<1; Operator Boundary: H(Q|R)=0 but F(R)<1), noting 'information was lost != contract was violated != decoder was inadequate' as three genuinely different failure modes that a reduction can exhibit.

b_rows_sample.anchor: A two-state representation can have entropy close to 1 bit, while a larger representation can have much lower entropy if its distribution is highly concentrated. ... distinguish representation capacity, storage cost, Shannon entropy, minimality.
b_rows_sample.statement: Rejects a proposed requirement of strictly decreasing entropy H(R_n)<H(R_{n+1}) across the reduction chain as too strong, since entropy depends on the induced probability distribution rather than representation size; recommends requiring strictly decreasing representation CAPACITY instead, and measuring entropy, storage cost, and minimality as independent, separately reported quantities.

b_rows_sample.anchor: A failed representation transition Rn -> Rn-1 demonstrates that the transformation does not preserve the contract for that sample. It does not automatically identify a unique payload S that was removed.
b_rows_sample.statement: Warns against over-interpreting a failed reduction step: multiple eliminated components, interaction effects, transformation-induced changes, recombination, or loss of relational structure could all produce the same observed failure, so a specific eliminated set S notin Elim_{T,Pi}(D) may only be inferred when T_n has an explicit, declared elimination decomposition T_n=E_{S_n} -- otherwise report only 'T_n crosses the preservation boundary for D_i,' connecting this directly to the KR-ZERO-ORDER finding that transformation loss should not be assumed to decompose element-wise.

b_rows_sample.anchor: H(T)=H(Q)+H(T|Q), therefore H(T)>=H(Q), with equality iff H(T|Q)=0 ... T(D) = G(Q(D)) almost surely ... T(D) and Q(D) are mutually deterministically recoverable almost surely.
b_rows_sample.statement: Confirms Theorem 3's corrected attainability condition H(T(D)|Q(D))=0 and its consequence H(T)=H(Q)+H(T|Q); corrects the proposed 'Level 4: Q-Isomorphic Representation' (from Q=O∘T alone) to 'Q-Equivalent Representation,' since factorization through T establishes only that T contains enough information to determine Q, not a bijection between the full codomains Y and Q-space; the stronger, correct claim requires both H(Q(D)|T(D))=0 and H(T(D)|Q(D))=0, giving mutual a.s. recoverability T(D) <-> Q(D) rather than an unproven isomorphism.

b_rows_sample.anchor: sim_{Pi,T} = sim_Q restricted to X_{Pi,T} ... T(D) cannot literally be an element of [D]_{sim_Pi} ... D sim_{Pi,T} E_S(D) because Q(D)=Q(E_S(D)).
b_rows_sample.statement: Repairs two structural errors: (1) the equivalence relation sim_Pi must be defined as the global Q-induced relation sim_Q restricted to the T-dependent admissible domain X_{Pi,T}, not as an independent relation whose domain and defining condition are conflated; (2) a 'same fiber' claim mixing source-space [D]_{sim_Pi} (subset of X) with representation-space elements T(D), T(E_S(D)) (elements of Y) is type-incorrect -- the correct statement is D sim_{Pi,T} E_S(D) in source space, with O(T(D))=O(T(E_S(D))) as the separate representation-space consequence.

b_rows_sample.anchor: T_Adeq(Q) = {T: H(Q(D)|T(D))=0} ... T_Real(Pi) = {T: P(D in X_{Pi,T})=1 and P(O(T(D))=Q(D))=1}.
b_rows_sample.statement: Separates a previously ambiguous family T_adequate(Pi) into two explicitly distinct families -- T_Adeq(Q) (transformations adequate for the inquiry alone) and T_Real(Pi) (transformations that additionally realize the whole contract, both admissibility and the fixed decoder) -- and cautions that entropy minimization T*=argmin H(T(D)) should be stated as an infimum unless existence of the minimizer is separately established.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Zero_{T_n,Pi}(S_n;R^n) => Adeq(R^{n-1},Q,Pi) as the Zero-boundary hypothesis. I would not formulate it that strongly anymore ... Zero is itself a judgment produced by (D,T,Pi,S).
b_rows_sample.statement: Rejects a proposed strong 'Zero-boundary hypothesis' (Zero at a reduction step implies adequacy of the next representation) as formulated too strongly, arguing instead that Zero is one observable judgment produced by the underlying tuple (D,T,Pi,S), with an unnamed interaction structure I_{T,Pi}(D,S) as the real open mathematical object -- reframing the research question from 'what does Zero predict?' to 'what structure determines the boundary at which reduction ceases to preserve the contract, of which Zero is one detection mechanism?'

b_rows_sample.anchor: KR-ZERO discovered empirical constraints on context-dependent eliminability and revealed that relational structure may enter through the transformation/preservation pair. KR-REP-REDUCTION now independently investigates representation reduction ... using the KR-ZERO findings as controlled experimental factors and hypotheses -- not as definitions or conclusions.
b_rows_sample.statement: Revises the relationship between the two experiment families: rather than 'KR-ZERO discovers eliminability; KR-REP-REDUCTION tests whether Zero predicts adequacy,' the corrected position is that KR-ZERO's findings become controlled experimental factors and hypotheses for KR-REP-REDUCTION, never definitions or conclusions it inherits; elevates the representation carrier (individual element vs subset vs relational structure/hypergraph/rewriting state) to a first-class unresolved research question that must be settled before R5->R2 can be properly designed.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Adequacy != Contract Realization ... otherwise a representation could look mathematically sufficient while failing the actual preservation/operational contract.
b_rows_sample.statement: Adopts Adequacy != Contract Realization as a hard experimental rule for KR-REP-REDUCTION, distinguishing T_Adeq(Q) (sufficient information exists) from T_Real(Pi) (the specified operator O actually realizes it, and admissibility holds), so that a mathematically sufficient representation is never conflated with one that actually satisfies the operational contract.

b_rows_sample.anchor: KR-ZERO: When can source material be eliminated while preserving the contract? KR-REP-REDUCTION: How far can the representation be reduced while retaining inquiry adequacy and contract realization? The bridge is a hypothesis to test, not an established implication.
b_rows_sample.statement: States the final, precise research-question separation between the two experiment families and explicitly classifies the connecting arrow (Zero_{T_n,Pi} -> candidate elimination -> R^{n-1} -> Adequacy/Realization) as a hypothesis to be tested by KR-REP-REDUCTION, never an established implication inherited from KR-ZERO; freezes a status ledger distinguishing [CORPUS] established facts, [EXP] established mathematical results (H(Q|T)=0 adequacy; H(T|Q)=0 no-excess; hence H(T)=H(Q)+H(T|Q)), [PROP] proposed measures (Excess_Q(T)=H(T|Q); Zero predicting adequacy), and five explicit [OPEN] questions (existence of a general R5->R2 chain; the representation carrier; monotonicity; whether Zero predicts the boundary; whether relational structure in T,Pi predicts reduction difficulty).

b_rows_sample.anchor: X_Q(R) = H(R|Q) as Q-relative residual representation, with excess representation as an interpretation only when the contract explicitly says those distinctions are unnecessary.
b_rows_sample.statement: Names the final residual-representation quantity X_Q(R)=H(R|Q) as 'Q-relative residual representation,' explicitly reserving the normatively loaded term 'excess representation' only for cases where the preservation contract itself declares the residual distinctions unnecessary, on the principle that what is unnecessary for one inquiry is not thereby unnecessary for every inquiry (provenance, uncertainty bounds, or lineage may be irrelevant to Q while still required by the broader contract Pi).

b_rows_sample.anchor: R(Q,Pi) = (D, {R_n}, {T_n}, O, Q, Pi) ... M_n = (A_n, F_n, H_hat(Q|R_n), X_Q(R_n), H_hat(R_n), N_viol,n) ... n* = min{n in {1..5} : Comp_n=1.0 and A_n=1.0 and N_viol,n=0 and H_hat(Q|R_n)=0}.
b_rows_sample.statement: Presents the fully frozen KR-REP-REDUCTION experimental protocol as the object R(Q,Pi)=(D,{R_n},{T_n},O,Q,Pi) with directional chain D->T5->R5->T4->R4->T3->R3->T2->R2->T1->R1, entropy/size/count recorded independently per level (monotonicity treated as an empirical hypothesis, never assumed), a completeness-declared per-level measurement vector M_n=(A_n,F_n,H_hat(Q|R_n),X_Q(R_n),H_hat(R_n),N_viol,n), the closed-form fiber-violation formula N_viol,n=sum_r [(sum_q c_{r,q})^2 - sum_q c_{r,q}^2]/2, and the boundary definition n*=min{n: Comp_n=1, A_n=1, N_viol,n=0, H_hat(Q|R_n)=0}, with R_{n*} confirmed as the chain-specific preservation boundary only if the next-lower level fails at least one of those conditions.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The current design does not yet fully test H-RR3 (T-Pi interaction) ... the controlled 2x2 experiment is deferred ... the next useful review is of the actual implementation and its FT-1...FT-7 execution results.
b_rows_sample.statement: Notes that the frozen protocol design defers the controlled 2x2 (T_extreme/realistic x Pi_extreme/realistic) test of transformation-preservation interaction (hypothesis H-RR3), so the design phase can investigate the reduction boundary and observe an association with Zero but cannot yet establish a general T-Pi interaction law; records that the theoretical/protocol design phase is complete and the next required review step is of the actual implementation's FT-1 through FT-7 execution results, i.e. an experiment run beyond the scope of this file.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Contract failure: NO / Operator-only failure: NO / Representation failure: YES ... A_n = 1.000 at every level ... You need a representation where H(Q|R)=0 while simultaneously O(R)!=Q.
b_rows_sample.statement: Reports that hypothesis H-B (intending to separate representation failure, contract failure, and operator failure) found only representation failure occurring, since admissibility A_n=1.000 held at every level and the fixed decoder F=1.000 at the only adequate level R5, so no empirical state arose where Q was recoverable from R (H(Q|R)=0) yet the fixed operator O failed to recover Q (O(R)!=Q); concludes that a fixed decoder alone does not create an operator-boundary experiment -- a representation must retain enough information (H(Q|R)=0) while the chosen decoder still fails to use it -- and this chain never produced such a state, so adequacy and realization remain conceptually distinct even though this experiment did not empirically separate them along the reduction chain.

b_rows_sample.anchor: ascending: F_argmax = 0.8667 / descending: F_argmax = 0.3230 ... a difference of 54.37 percentage points ... yet H(Q|R2) 3.3937 vs 3.3965 is essentially unchanged.
b_rows_sample.statement: Reports a strong empirical demonstration that representation adequacy is distinct from fixed-decoder realization: reversing a rank encoding convention (ascending vs descending) leaves Hhat(Q|R2) essentially unchanged (3.3937 vs 3.3965) and N_viol similar, yet the fixed decoder's F_argmax swings by 54.37 percentage points (0.8667 vs 0.3230); interprets this as same recoverable information under different encoding convention producing very different fixed-decoder performance, i.e. a representation can preserve the same recoverable information while a particular fixed decoder performs very differently because it interprets the representation differently.

b_rows_sample.anchor: "A change carrying NO information about D..." ... The ascending and descending rank conventions are information-equivalent recodings of the same rank representation, yet they produce substantially different performance for the fixed decoder O.
b_rows_sample.statement: Requests softening the phrase 'a change carrying no information about D' to the more formal 'the ascending and descending rank conventions are information-equivalent recodings of the same rank representation, yet they produce substantially different performance for the fixed decoder O', on the ground that what matters theoretically is not an informal claim of 'no information' but that the transformation between conventions is information-preserving/invertible; connects this directly to the project's Q-equivalence concept.

b_rows_sample.anchor: bytes: 37 -> 37 -> 37 -> 25 / fields: 2 -> 2 -> 2 -> 2 / cardinality: 26826 -> 5696 -> 3288 -> 162 / entropy: 15.04 -> 12.31 -> 11.10 -> 7.17 ... there is no single obvious scalar called "amount of reduction"
b_rows_sample.statement: Reports the four measured reduction-dimension trajectories (bytes, fields, cardinality, entropy) across R5..R2 and argues the evidence only establishes that no single scalar 'amount of reduction' captures all four dimensions -- i.e. reduction is multidimensional and the measured dimensions do not collapse into one common trajectory -- but four observations along a single chain cannot establish statistical independence, so hypothesis H-D's claim that 'the four dimensions move independently' should be softened to that weaker, corpus-supported statement.

a_rows_sample.statement: States the actual theorem to be proved: not that KnowledgeOS has exactly 13 kernel operators, but that among implementations satisfying a fixed semantic contract, no implementation can remove an irreducible required epistemic capability without losing semantic completeness, formalized as K_min=min_preceq{K: K|=C_KOS} ordered by semantic capability inclusion, not operator count.

a_rows_sample.anchor: A capability is defined as: c in C iff there exists an admissible epistemic scenario in which the presence or absence of c produces a difference in contract-observable behaviour. ... operator decomposition != semantic capability decomposition.
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines a capability c as belonging to the required set C iff there exists an admissible scenario where its presence or absence produces a difference in contract-observable behaviour, establishing that operator decomposition (how many named functions implement something) is not the same as semantic capability decomposition (which distinct behaviors are required).

a_rows_sample.statement: Separates epistemic attribution (A_t=Gamma(E_t,Q_t,C_t,EC_t), an internal kernel transformation) from the externally-constrained factive predicate Knows(a,p,c,t)=>True(p,c,t), preventing the kernel from manufacturing truth merely by attribution and thereby preventing the minimality proof from hiding truth verification inside the kernel.

a_rows_sample.anchor: K1 ==_sem K2 iff for every admissible (q,c,e,x), the two implementations produce observationally indistinguishable semantic behaviour: Obs(K1,q,c,e,x)=Obs(K2,q,c,e,x). Obs = (State,Gap,Determination,Revision,History,InvariantStatus,Attribution,Transition). ... internal representations may differ ...
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines the first-pass semantic equivalence K1 ==_sem K2 as pointwise equality of an eight-component observation function (State, Gap, Determination, Revision, History, InvariantStatus, Attribution, Transition) across every admissible situation, establishing that two kernels can have different internal representations while being semantically equivalent -- 'this is the missing mathematical piece that previously prevented a genuine minimality theorem.'

a_rows_sample.anchor: Lemma 1 -- Capability Irreducibility. Let c in C_K. Suppose there exists an admissible scenario s_c such that Obs(s_c|c)=1 but Obs(s_c|C_K\{c})=0. Then c is irreducible with respect to the declared capability basis. Proof: Assume the contrary ... Obs(s_c|C_K\{c})=Obs(s_c|c) ... Contradiction. Theref
a_rows_sample.statement: Proves Lemma 1 (Capability Irreducibility): if there exists an admissible scenario where capability c produces an observable effect that the remaining capability set cannot reproduce, then c cannot be removed from the declared capability basis, via a proof by contradiction against the assumption that c is derivable from the rest.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Theorem 1 -- Minimal Capability Set. If for every proper subset S' subsetneq S there exists an admissible witness w_S' such that Obs(K_S,w_S') != Obs(K_S',w_S'), then S is a minimal semantically complete capability set. Proof: ... contradiction ... Hence S is minimal.
a_rows_sample.statement: Proves a first-pass Theorem 1 (Minimal Capability Set): given a semantically complete capability set S such that every proper subset S' has an admissible witness distinguishing K_S from K_S', S is minimal, via a proof by contradiction assuming some proper subset were also complete.

a_rows_sample.anchor: the earlier exhaustive search found: the original 13-operator C0 was inadequate; adding Qualify repaired the missing capability; DetectGap was derivable; ... exactly two minimal implementations appeared; both had 13 operators; the difference was packaging. That gives strong experimental evidence ...
a_rows_sample.statement: Explains why the earlier exhaustive 13-operator search (finding the original C0 inadequate, Qualify repairing a missing capability, DetectGap derivable, and exactly two minimal 13-operator packagings differing only in packaging) constitutes strong experimental evidence for a candidate lower bound but does not by itself prove universal minimality -- experimentally irreducible implies candidate lower bound, never a universal theorem.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Suppose the irreducible capability set is C_irr={c_1,...,c_m}. By Lemma 1: for all c_i in C_irr, c_i not-preceq C_irr\{c_i}. Therefore every semantically complete kernel must realize each c_i: C_irr subseteq Capabilities(K) for every admissible kernel K. Hence |C_irr| <= |Capabilities(K)| for every
a_rows_sample.statement: Derives the lower-bound argument: since Lemma 1 shows every member of an irreducible capability set C_irr cannot be derived from the rest, every semantically complete kernel must realize all of C_irr, giving C_irr subseteq Capabilities(K) and hence |C_irr|<=|Capabilities(K)| for every admissible implementation K.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Now construct a reference kernel K* = Implementation(C_irr). If we demonstrate K* |= {semantic adequacy, transition completeness, invariant preservation, capability completeness, observable behaviour contract} then |Capabilities(K*)|=|C_irr|. Combined with the lower bound ... K* is capability-minima
a_rows_sample.statement: Constructs the matching upper bound: a reference kernel K*=Implementation(C_irr) that, if shown to satisfy semantic adequacy, transition completeness, invariant preservation, capability completeness, and the observable behaviour contract, has |Capabilities(K*)|=|C_irr|, which combined with the lower bound establishes K* as capability-minimal via the standard lower-bound-plus-construction structure of a minimality proof.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Packaging theorem. Suppose Capabilities(K_A)=Capabilities(K_B)=C_irr and K_A ==_sem K_B. Then K_A and K_B are two minimal realizations of the same Kernel capability system. They need not have equal operator counts. For example K_A={Interpret,Represent} could be replaced by K_B={SemanticTransform}. I
a_rows_sample.statement: Proves a packaging theorem: two semantically equivalent implementations K_A, K_B realizing the same irreducible capability set C_irr are both minimal realizations of the same kernel capability system regardless of differing operator counts (e.g. K_A={Interpret,Represent} vs K_B={SemanticTransform}), so a smaller operator count establishes only more compressed implementation packaging, never a smaller epistemic kernel -- explaining why the earlier research concluded operator count is not representation invariant.

a_rows_sample.anchor: KernelCapability(c) iff c is semantically required and irreducible. DerivedCapability(c) iff c not-in KernelCapability and c=F(C_1,...,C_n) ... This resolves the DetectGap problem. We do not need DetectGap as a primitive if DetectGap = F(Determine,Discriminate,I,Q,EC) ... Capability exists !=> primi
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines KernelCapability(c) (semantically required and irreducible) versus DerivedCapability(c) (expressible as a composition F of kernel capabilities), formally resolving the DetectGap problem by showing DetectGap=F(Determine,Discriminate,I,Q,EC) under declared semantics, so a capability existing does not imply a primitive kernel operator exists for it.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Zero is defined over a transformation and preservation observation: Zero_{T,Pi}(S;D) iff Pi(T(D))=Pi(T(E_S(D))). Therefore Zero depends upon D,T,Pi,S. It is not itself an epistemic capability required to construct every kernel state. ... Zero not-in KernelCapability under the current contract. It re
a_rows_sample.statement: Formally excludes Zero from the primitive kernel: since Zero_{T,Pi}(S;D) is a predicate parameterized by D,T,Pi,S rather than an intrinsic epistemic capability, and the bridge experiments showed Zero neither implies nor is implied by adequacy, Zero not-in KernelCapability under the current contract, remaining instead a transformation-relative eliminability lens.

a_rows_sample.anchor: For D --T--> R the representation R is a carrier. KnowledgeOS asks whether Q=g.T, or H(Q|R)=0. That establishes representation adequacy. It does not establish that Represent must be an epistemic primitive. ... Representation mechanism != Representation capability != Kernel primitive.
a_rows_sample.statement: Formally excludes 'Represent' from the primitive kernel merely because every kernel needs some representation: representation adequacy (H(Q|R)=0) does not establish that Represent must itself be an epistemic primitive, since epistemic states may be represented implicitly through state transitions, typed relations, structured records, distributions, graphs, tensors, databases, or symbolic structures -- Representation mechanism != Representation capability != Kernel primitive.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Select cannot automatically be promoted to the epistemic kernel. Epistemic selection: Select_epi: H_Q -> A_Q. Practical/decision selection: Select_act: A^act -> Action, which belongs downstream: K_t -> Proposal -> Decision -> Authorization -> Action. Therefore Select in Kernel is not established mer
a_rows_sample.statement: Splits 'Select' into epistemic selection (Select_epi: hypothesis space to admissible hypotheses) and practical/decision selection (Select_act: belonging downstream in the K_t -> Proposal -> Decision -> Authorization -> Action pipeline), concluding Select in Kernel is not established merely because KnowledgeOS ultimately selects actions or hypotheses -- the capability must first be typed, exactly the semantic-granularity instability observed in the earlier reduction experiment.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Epistemic kernel is responsible only for irreducible epistemic transformations. Representation layer D--T-->R handles representation and reduction. Reasoning regimes provide domain-specific reasoning machinery. Zero Lens examines transformation-relative boundaries. Governance (Authorization) remains
a_rows_sample.statement: Produces the resulting six-way architecture separating Epistemic Kernel (irreducible epistemic transformations only), Representation Layer (D->R representation/reduction), Reasoning Regimes (domain-specific inference machinery), Zero Lens (transformation-relative boundary analysis), Governance (external authorization), and Execution (external actions) -- Kernel != Representation != Reasoning Engine != Zero != Governance != Execution -- described as a major DDD result: the kernel owns epistemic responsibility, not every mechanism involved in producing or consuming knowledge.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Theorem -- Relative Semantic Minimality of the KnowledgeOS Kernel. Let E be a fixed KnowledgeOS semantic environment with [10 fixed components including semantic equivalence and a capability set C_irr irreducible under Lemma 1, and a reference implementation K* realizing every capability in C_irr].
a_rows_sample.statement: Proves the first-pass main theorem (Relative Semantic Minimality of the KnowledgeOS Kernel): given a fixed semantic environment with ten specified fixed components (carrier, inquiry space, contract space, standards, transition semantics, invariant set, observable behaviour, semantic equivalence, an irreducible capability set C_irr, and a reference implementation K* realizing it), K* is minimal under ==_sem, i.e. no kernel satisfying the same contract exists with a strictly smaller capability set.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Proven conditionally: irreducibility + completeness => minimality. And: different operator packaging !=> different kernel. Experimentally supported: Qualify cannot simply be omitted; DetectGap is derivable; multiple minimal packagings exist; operator counting alone is inadequate ... Not yet universa
a_rows_sample.statement: Delivers a three-tier honest status ledger for the first-pass proof: proven conditionally (irreducibility plus completeness implies minimality; different operator packaging does not imply a different kernel); experimentally supported (Qualify's non-omissibility, DetectGap's derivability, multiple minimal packagings, inadequacy of raw operator counting); and not yet universally proven (the currently named capability set is not proved to be the unique universal kernel, pending formal closure of semantic equivalence, composition, lifecycle, and invariant preservation).

a_rows_sample.anchor: We may prove minimal without proving unique implementation. There may exist K_1,...,K_n such that K_i==_sem K_j and each is minimal. Then Kernel capability system is unique while Kernel implementation is not unique. That is exactly the mathematically correct resolution of the two 13-operator minima
a_rows_sample.statement: Establishes the crucial distinction between minimality and uniqueness: multiple semantically-equivalent implementations K_1,...,K_n can each be minimal, so the Kernel capability system can be unique even while the Kernel implementation is not, which is exactly the mathematically correct resolution of the two 13-operator minima found experimentally.

a_rows_sample.anchor: I would therefore not freeze 'The KnowledgeOS Kernel consists of 13 operators.'
