a_rows_sample.statement: Declines to freeze 'the KnowledgeOS Kernel consists of 13 operators', freezing instead the stronger semantic statement that the Kernel is the minimal semantically complete set of epistemic capabilities required to preserve the declared epistemic contract across admissible representations, transitions, and implementations (K_KOS=min_preceq_sem{K:K|=C_KOS}), establishing that kernel minimality is semantic, not syntactic.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Previously: 'We need to discover the Kernel.' Now: 'We have a formal criterion under which Kernel minimality can be proved.' a_rows_sample.statement: Restates the Absence-of-Evidence vs Evidence-of-Absence distinction (Tier P1): AbsenceOfEvidence holds iff neither phi nor not-phi is in K; EvidenceOfAbsence holds iff some evidence e derives not-phi; cited as required by the Zero Lens Specification's Non-collapse Invariant #3, and as a distinction every other compared formalism (FOL, K3/L3, plain FDE) collapses while R_req preserves it.

a_rows_sample.statement: Executive verdict on an R_req/ratification-style document: classified as research analysis / candidate specification, not yet ratifiable; explicitly rejects the document's own recommendation to add all ten proposed distinctions and to ratify, warning against R_req becoming an over-constraining 'master ontology'; distills the strongest contribution as R_req = the distinctions that must remain available for KnowledgeOS's required questions, combined with Representation Adequacy iff required distinctions are preserved.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Theorem (Closure and Structural Completeness): ... R_req is structurally complete if and only if every minimal information requirement I(tau) for all tau in T is mapped to a non-collapsing partition in R_req. Proof Construction (By Information-Theoretic Partitioning): 1. Sufficiency ... 2. Minimality ... 3. Closure: R_req is closed under Boolean operations on equivalence relations.
b_rows_sample.statement: States and sketches a proof for a Structural Completeness Theorem for R_req: R_req is structurally complete iff every minimal information requirement of every minimal operational task (contradiction isolation, Zero-state checking, epistemic query resolution, temporal garbage collection) maps to a non-collapsing partition. The proof construction has three parts: Sufficiency (append any distinction found missing by a task-output divergence), Minimality (keep only distinctions with a witnessing test vector), and Closure (R_req closed under Boolean operations on equivalence relations, sim_{d_i AND d_j} = sim_{d_i} intersect sim_{d_j}).

type_signature.domain: task set T and distinction set R_req

b_rows_sample.anchor: D-1.3 Explicit vs. Implicit Knowledge ... Explicit(phi) iff phi in K; Implicit(phi) iff phi not-in K and K entails phi. Tractability: O(1) for explicit; NP-hard in general for implicit deduction.
b_rows_sample.statement: Adds D-1.3 Explicit-vs-Implicit Knowledge to the R_req inventory (Tier P1): Explicit(phi) iff phi in K; Implicit(phi) iff phi not-in K and K entails phi; explicit lookup is O(1), implicit deduction is NP-hard in general -- connecting this batch's FR-1/K^exp-K^der distinction into the R_req formal distinction inventory with a stated complexity class.

b_rows_sample.anchor: D-5.1 Analytic vs. Synthetic Truth ... D-5.2 Necessary vs. Contingent Modality ... Necessary (Box phi), Contingent (Diamond phi and Diamond not-phi) ... Kripke frame accessibility valuation ... PSPACE-complete in general modal logics; approximated via static metadata.
b_rows_sample.statement: Adds two new Tier P2 distinctions to R_req: D-5.1 Analytic (true by definition/tautology) vs Synthetic (true by empirical observation); D-5.2 Necessary (Box phi) vs Contingent (Diamond phi and Diamond not-phi) modality via Kripke-frame accessibility valuation, noting general modal-logic decision is PSPACE-complete but approximated here via static metadata annotation rather than full modal inference.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 4.1 Integration with Contr ... When two incoming streams present e1 |- P and e2 |- not-P: 1. Contr sets KnowledgeStatus(P) = Contradictory (B={T,F} in FDE). 2. It prevents total logical explosion by trapping the assertion within an isolated contradiction frame. 3. It initializes ResolutionStatus(P) = Unresolved. 4. If d in R_req were collapsed, Contr would either trigger classical explosion or falsely collapse the state into Unknown.
b_rows_sample.statement: Specifies the required integration between R_req and the Contr contradiction-isolation subsystem: on conflicting evidence e1|-P and e2|-not-P, Contr must set KnowledgeStatus(P)=Contradictory, trap the assertion in an isolated frame to prevent explosion, and initialize ResolutionStatus(P)=Unresolved; explicitly states that collapsing any of D-1.1/D-3.1/D-4.1 would force either classical explosion or a false collapse into Unknown.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 4.2 Integration with Zero Lens Specification ... 0_KnowledgeOS iff for all P in K: (Status(P) not-in {Contradictory, Underdetermined} and Currency(P) == Current)
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines a formal Zero-state predicate for KnowledgeOS: 0_KnowledgeOS holds iff every proposition P in K has KnowledgeStatus(P) not in {Contradictory, Underdetermined} and Currency(P)==Current, i.e. no unsatisfied requirements or unhandled contradictions and no stale dependencies; requires all R_req distinctions to remain expressible without loss.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 4.3 Integration with Evaluation Engine ... Loss_{R_req}(pi) = sum_{d_i in R_req} w_i * I(Collapse(d_i,pi)) ... An adequate kernel projection requires Loss_{R_req}(pi) == 0 for all P1 distinctions.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines a quantitative Loss function for the Evaluation Engine using R_req as its metric: Loss_{R_req}(pi) = sum over d_i in R_req of w_i times an indicator of whether pi collapses d_i, with priority weights w_i (P1=1.0, P2=0.5); an adequate kernel projection must achieve Loss_{R_req}(pi)==0 for every Tier-P1 distinction -- a concrete quantification of the Representation Adequacy principle.

b_rows_sample.statement: Specifies a four-phase governance workflow for R_req (Draft Review & Completeness Proof marked COMPLETED, Formal Verification & Test Vectors marked COMPLETED, HPA Supervisory Ratification marked CURRENT STAGE, Kernel Candidate Adoption Baseline v1.0 Frozen as the final phase) plus protocol policies: Tier P1 distinctions are immutable across v1.x, and any new P2/P3 distinction requires a test-vector necessity demonstration, a tractability proof of no P1 regression, and two-thirds HPA Supervisory approval.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Measurement is not knowledge ... It becomes knowledge only after engineering history provides contextual meaning.
a_rows_sample.statement: States the strongest cross-cutting EKS principle: a raw metric (e.g. LCOM4=29) is measurement, not knowledge; it becomes knowledge only through the recommendation→decision→outcome→assessment→pattern chain.

a_rows_sample.anchor: EKS turns engineering activity into evidence, evidence into bounded recommendations and decisions, and decisions into durable engineering knowledge — while keeping architectural authority with humans and keeping future architectural evolution evidence-gated.
a_rows_sample.statement: States the single strongest coherent description of the current EKS architecture that this document's evidence supports, offered as the closing summary of a 60-section baseline.

b_rows_sample.anchor: RD-1 | A recommendation is immutable once issued; responses live in SEPARATE records
b_rows_sample.statement: A Recommendation is immutable once issued, with dedicated response records (decisions.jsonl) kept structurally separate from the issuance record.

b_rows_sample.anchor: RD-2 | Identity = (rule, subject) — duplicates cannot exist while open
b_rows_sample.statement: A Recommendation's identity is the pair (rule, subject); while a recommendation on that pair is open, no duplicate can be issued, confirmed by a re-run producing zero new records.

b_rows_sample.anchor: RD-3 | Rules produce structurally honest silence (absence of grounds → absence of advice)
b_rows_sample.statement: Recommendation rules are designed to stay silent when they lack grounds to fire, observed four times in Run 1 (e.g. insufficient history, flat CBO), rather than issuing speculative advice.

b_rows_sample.anchor: RD-4 | identity may need THREE layers: RecommendationDefinition / Instance / Revision
b_rows_sample.statement: A staged hypothesis proposes that Recommendation identity may eventually need three layers (Definition/Instance/Revision) because (rule,subject) dedup cannot answer whether a rule changed, whether re-issuance after changed conditions is warranted, or whether v1-ignored/v2-accepted should be distinguished; held at 'think, never implement, until a real question requires it'.

b_rows_sample.anchor: RD-5 | recommendations accumulate AGE — and age is already computable from existing timestamps
b_rows_sample.statement: Recommendation age (time-to-decision) is computable purely from existing issued/decided timestamps with no new schema fields; validated when Run 2 computed a real 6.5-hour time-to-decision from existing data.

b_rows_sample.anchor: RD-6 | ACTOR PROVENANCE GAP: the decision record's actor stamps the git user, but the decider was the AI at the user's direction
b_rows_sample.statement: When an AI participates in a decision at a user's direction, the decision record's actor field stamps the git user identity, obscuring who-executed versus who-authorized; only the free-text rationale comment carries the honest attribution today, flagged as a real modeling question once a second AI-mediated decision occurs.

b_rows_sample.anchor: RD-7 | A recommendation CAN currently be decided twice: two identical ACCEPTED records exist for REC-eaf245474a
b_rows_sample.statement: A genuine anomaly: a session interruption produced two identical ACCEPTED decision records for the same recommendation, empirically answering (by accident) that recommendations can currently be re-decided unguarded, and skewing a naive dashboard record count; the fix for this is deliberately deferred until the domain semantics (exactly-once vs last-wins) are decided, so as not to prematurely encode a guard.

b_rows_sample.anchor: NONE YET — insufficient evidence, said explicitly.
b_rows_sample.statement: The DDD classification of Recommendation (Application Service / Domain Service / Aggregate / Domain Capability / Process Manager) is explicitly refused for insufficient evidence after only one day of issuance with zero responses; the shape currently resembles 'an event with a process around it' more than an aggregate, pending accumulation of decisions, rationales, and outcomes.

b_rows_sample.anchor: DECIDING observed for the first time — ACCEPTED with reason code + comment
b_rows_sample.statement: Run 2 recorded the first-ever Decide action on a recommendation (ACCEPTED, reason code IMMEDIATE_VALUE), upgrading several ubiquitous-language terms from vocabulary-only to observed-exercised.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Impact: STILL insufficient — the first learning event is 3/5 complete (recommendation ✓ decision ✓ rationale ✓ · commit ✗ outcome ✗)
b_rows_sample.statement: Even after the first real decision, the KnowledgeOS-impact learning event remains only 3 of 5 complete (missing a real code change and a post-commit metric delta), so impact measurement stays insufficient evidence.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Re-run this discovery when: the first decision lands · every ~10 decisions thereafter · any anomaly appears in practice.
b_rows_sample.statement: The observation protocol commits to re-running this discovery instrument only on evidence triggers (first decision, every ~10 decisions, or an anomaly), never on a schedule, and forbids ML/ranking/confidence-scoring/adaptive behavior unless deterministic v1 demonstrably fails.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Recommendation lifecycle — class A, exercised once ... 8 recommendations remain open since 2026-08-04. The single closed loop returned INCONCLUSIVE ... the same recommendation was decided twice ... with near-identical rationales
b_rows_sample.statement: The full recommendation->decision->outcome->assessment chain is implemented and has been exercised exactly once end-to-end: 10 issued -> 2 decision rows (1 unique recommendation) -> 1 outcome -> 1 assessment (verdict INCONCLUSIVE, 'only 1 commits since decision, min 3'); 8 recommendations remain open since 2026-08-04; the same recommendation was decided twice with near-identical rationales, which the mechanism permits (classifying by latest) but the duplicate is still visible in the record. DASHBOARD.md itself frames the drop-off as 'a finding, not a failure -- an organizational mirror.'

a_rows_sample.anchor: They may support the same proposition p=HasVersion(S,v1) while remaining distinct evidence objects. Therefore we need at least three relations: Identity, Equality, Support. These must not be conflated.
a_rows_sample.statement: Establishes via a two-observation example (o1 by System A at t1, o2 by System B at t2, both supporting the same proposition p) that Identity, Equality, and Support must be three distinct, non-conflatable relations: distinct observations can support the same proposition without being identical or equal to each other.

a_rows_sample.anchor: KnowledgeOS may require domain identity in addition to mathematical equality ... a possible distinction is: StructuralEqual(x,y) versus SameIdentity(x,y). This is not yet an accepted KnowledgeOS definition. It is a required question.
a_rows_sample.statement: Poses object-level StructuralEqual(x,y) versus SameIdentity(x,y) as a required, not-yet-answered distinction: two records may be structurally identical while referring to different historical occurrences, so domain identity may be needed beyond ordinary mathematical equality.

a_rows_sample.anchor: There are at least four possibilities. A. Syntactic equality ... B. Semantic equality ... C. Observational equality ... D. Provenance-sensitive equality ... These are not interchangeable.
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines four non-interchangeable candidate Knowledge-State equality relations: syntactic (byte/structural identity), semantic (same knowledge semantics), observational (same result under every permitted observation), and provenance-sensitive (content and relevant provenance equivalent).

a_rows_sample.anchor: K1={p,e1} and K2={p,e2} where e1!=e2 but Supports(e1,p) and Supports(e2,p). Should K1=K2? There is no obvious answer. ... This proves that equality cannot be defined until we know what constitutes semantically essential information. Equality depends on the ontology and semantics.
a_rows_sample.statement: Gives a worked counterexample (two states differing only in which distinct evidence item supports the same proposition) showing equality is undecidable until it is settled whether provenance is semantically constitutive of knowledge identity or merely metadata -- concluding equality is ontology/semantics-dependent, not free-standing.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The mandate explicitly tells us not to assume this dependency ordering [G1->G2->G3]. ... the dependency graph is more accurately: Ontology -> State Representation -> Semantic Identity -> Equality ... So G1->G3 is plausible, but G1->G2->G3 is not established.
a_rows_sample.statement: Corrects a previously assumed linear dependency ordering (G1: what is a KnowledgeState -> G2: what is epistemic status -> G3: what is equality) into a revised chain Ontology -> State Representation -> Semantic Identity -> Equality, with epistemic status interacting with both representation and equality rather than sitting strictly between state-definition and equality; the direct G1->G2->G3 chain is explicitly downgraded to not established.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The propositions may refer to different times ... Then there is no contradiction. This demonstrates that contradiction cannot be determined from proposition content alone. ... A better candidate is: Contradicts(p1,p2,c) ... contradiction is likely a derived semantic relation, not a primitive field o
a_rows_sample.statement: Shows via a temporal-interval example (HasVersion(S,v1) valid on [t1,t2), HasVersion(S,v2) valid on [t2,t3)) that two propositions with conflicting content are not automatically contradictory, since contradiction depends on context c as well as content; concludes contradiction is a derived semantic relation Contradicts(p1,p2,c), not a primitive Knowledge-State field.

a_rows_sample.anchor: with both assert validity over exactly the same interval ... If the domain invariant is: forall t: #Version(S,t)<=1, then Contradicts(p1,p2)=true. ... Contradiction required: proposition semantics; temporal validity; domain constraints. Contradiction is not merely a property of two strings.
a_rows_sample.statement: Gives a strong-contradiction example: two version propositions over the identical time interval, evaluated against an explicit domain invariant (a service has at most one version at any time) actually do produce Contradicts=true, demonstrating contradiction requires jointly proposition semantics, temporal validity, and domain constraints -- it is a relation evaluated under a semantic regime, not a syntactic property.

a_rows_sample.anchor: A logical regime could define Contradiction_L. A temporal regime could define Contradiction_T. A probabilistic regime might instead calculate P(p1|E) and P(p2|E). These need not produce the same classification. Contradiction may be regime-relative.
a_rows_sample.statement: Proposes that contradiction may be regime-relative: a logical regime, a temporal regime, and a probabilistic regime applied to the same pair of propositions need not agree on whether a contradiction exists -- a stronger claim than merely 'KnowledgeOS supports contradictions', and supportive of a multi-regime architecture operating over a common substrate.

a_rows_sample.anchor: P(p)=0.7 ... It could represent: probability of truth; confidence in an observation; reliability of a source; posterior probability; frequency in a population; degree of belief; probability of an answer. These are mathematically different quantities. 0.7 alone has no epistemic semantics.
a_rows_sample.statement: Argues a bare numeric uncertainty value (e.g. P(p)=0.7) has no epistemic semantics on its own, since it could denote any of at least 7 mathematically distinct quantities (probability of truth, observation confidence, source reliability, posterior probability, population frequency, degree of belief, or probability of an answer) -- reinforcing an earlier corpus warning against identifying measurement/probability with knowledge itself.

a_rows_sample.anchor: P_M(p|E) has a meaningful interpretation relative to M. This is fundamentally different from asserting p=0.7. ... K --probabilistic regime--> D ... A probability distribution may be a regime-specific representation over a knowledge-state space [not] KnowledgeOS = Probability Distribution. The latter
a_rows_sample.statement: Relocates probability from being a property directly assigned to a proposition (p=0.7) to a projection K --regime--> D produced by an explicit probabilistic model M (P_M(p|E)); explicitly rejects the earlier corpus formulation 'KnowledgeOS = Application + Distribution + Measure' as a category error, preserving instead the weaker claim that a probability distribution may be one regime-specific representation over the knowledge-state space.

a_rows_sample.anchor: not every numerical assignment licenses arithmetic operations ... c(p)+c(q) is not automatically meaningful. Nor is 2c(p). Numeric representation != quantitative measurement.
a_rows_sample.statement: Invokes a Roberts-style measurement-theory constraint: a numerical assignment is meaningful only when its empirical relational structure and representation theorem justify it, so arithmetic operations on a stored confidence/uncertainty number (e.g. c(p)+c(q), 2*c(p)) are not automatically meaningful -- numeric representation is not the same as quantitative measurement, a constraint relevant to any future statistical regime.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Knowledge Substrate plus Semantic Relations plus Epistemic Qualifications plus Regime Specific Projections rather than one homogeneous mathematical object containing every possible quantity. ... Projection_R: K x R -> Y_R where K = knowledge substrate; R = regime; Y_R = regime-specific representatio
a_rows_sample.statement: Converges on a 4-part architectural decomposition (Knowledge Substrate, Semantic Relations, Epistemic Qualifications, Regime-Specific Projections) rather than one homogeneous state object, formalized as a candidate interface Projection_R: K x R -> Y_R (K=substrate, R=regime, Y_R=regime output), instantiated for logical (LogicalModel), probabilistic (Distribution), measurement (MeasurementSpace) and governance (Decision/ComplianceAssessment) regimes -- explicitly not yet the final architecture but a testable interface.

a_rows_sample.anchor: A regime may transform or interpret a knowledge substrate, but it must not silently change the historical identity of the underlying knowledge objects. ... the projection should preserve the identity mapping id_K: K -> K. A regime-specific representation must not silently turn e1 into e2.
a_rows_sample.statement: States a candidate cross-regime invariant: any regime projection Pi_R(K)=Y_R must preserve the identity mapping id_K:K->K on the underlying knowledge objects -- a regime interpretation must never silently substitute one evidence/knowledge object's identity for another's, which is particularly important for provenance.

a_rows_sample.anchor: KnowledgeOS must distinguish the epistemic substrate from the mathematical regimes used to interpret it. ... Probability != Knowledge. Measurement != Knowledge. Logical inference != Knowledge. but all may operate on knowledge under properly defined regimes.
a_rows_sample.statement: States the step's central principle: KnowledgeOS must distinguish the epistemic substrate from the mathematical regimes (logical, probabilistic, measurement) used to interpret it -- Probability != Knowledge, Measurement != Knowledge, Logical inference != Knowledge, though all may legitimately operate on knowledge as regimes; noted as independently arrived at, matching an existing corpus warning against equating the epistemic core with measure theory.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Is the candidate Knowledge State actually a state, or is it fundamentally a history/process? ... We therefore need to test K_t versus H_t=(K_0,T_1,T_2,...,T_t) and determine whether K_t is sufficient to reconstruct everything that KnowledgeOS claims to preserve. ... the true formal object may be clo
a_rows_sample.statement: Sets up the next test (named Step 247, State vs. History Sufficiency Test): whether the candidate Knowledge State K_t is sufficient by itself, or whether the true formal object must be a state-history pair (K_t, H_t) with H_t=(K0,T1,...,Tt), given the corpus's repeated emphasis on provenance/transformation/history as central rather than a single lineage component.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Can two knowledge states be identical while having different histories? If yes, then History(K) != K may be fundamental. Construct an example K1 and K2 with identical current semantic content but different histories. Then test K1=K2 under: structural, semantic, provenance-sensitive, historical ident

a_rows_sample.anchor: CONTRADICTION #1 — Knowledge as a generic object: forbidden in 208, used as an Owner in 210
a_rows_sample.statement: Step 208 Section 208.28 boxes a prohibition: the Data->Information->Evidence->Assessment->KnowledgeClaim transformations of semantic status 'should not [be collapsed] into one generic object called Knowledge.' Step 210 Section 210.25's matrix row I11 nonetheless assigns Owner='Knowledge' (and row I3 compounds it with 'Knowledge infrastructure'), the exact generic object Step 208 boxed a prohibition against two files earlier in the same band. Severity HIGH; neither Step-206 bounded context, and neither file notices.

a_rows_sample.anchor: CONTRADICTION #2 — Provenance composition (208) excludes the authority Step 209 requires
a_rows_sample.statement: Step 208 Section 208.25 asserts as an equality P(G)=P(A)∪P(E), boxed as 'provenance must be closed under semantic transformation.' Step 209 Section 209.4 requires Final(D)⇒DecisionBasis(D)∧Authority(D). Since Authority(D), the governance grant that made a decision final, is in neither P(A) nor P(E), a governed decision's provenance under Section 208.25 cannot contain its own authority, yet Step 209's own traceability requirement (Basis(D) including authority) demands that it does -- the two cannot both hold. Independently checked, the equality is additionally vacuous if closure holds (P(A)⊇P(E) implies the union is just P(A)) and self-refuting if it does not. Severity HIGH.

a_rows_sample.anchor: CONTRADICTION #3 — The evidence-strength scale is recalibrated between Step 210 and Step 212
a_rows_sample.statement: Step 210 Section 210.30 defines E_1=documentation, E_2=manual inspection, E_3=automated test, E_4=property-based test, E_5=formal verification. Step 212 Section 212.6 defines E_0=No evidence, E_1=Claim/documentation, E_2=Static implementation evidence, E_3=Executable test evidence, E_4=Runtime/production evidence, E_5=Formal verification. E_2, E_3 and E_4 disagree between the two files (only E_5 agrees), so a claim 'has E_4 evidence' means a property-based test under Step 210 and production observation under Step 212 -- entirely different assurance. Aggravating factor: Step 212's calibration silently matches the uncited Step 109's (E2=implementation, E4=runtime), so Step 212 restores an earlier convention without knowing it. Severity HIGH.

a_rows_sample.anchor: CONTRADICTION #4 — E_1 bound twice inside Step 210 itself
a_rows_sample.statement: Step 210 Section 210.20 writes E_1⇒P and E_2⇒¬P (evidence items entailing propositions); Step 210 Section 210.30, ten sections later, writes E_1=documentation (an ordinal assurance rung). Same symbol, same document, incompatible types, undisambiguated. Severity MEDIUM-HIGH.

a_rows_sample.anchor: CONTRADICTION #5 — Evidence/Test ordering reversed between Step 210's own boxed conclusion and Step 211's boxed conclusion
a_rows_sample.statement: Step 210 Section 210.40 boxes Invariant->Owner->Enforcement->Evidence->Test->Assurance; Step 211 Section 211.2 boxes I->Owner->Mechanism->Test->Evidence -- directly conflicting orderings, both boxed as conclusions in consecutive files. Step 210's own Section 210.1 tuple and Step 209's tail agenda both side with Step 211's ordering, so Step 210's boxed conclusion contradicts Step 210's own boxed tuple. Severity MEDIUM; the direction matters since Evidence->Test means evidence licenses the test while Test->Evidence means the test produces the evidence, which is what Steps 212-214 assume throughout.

a_rows_sample.anchor: CONTRADICTION #6 — min over assurance vs. the prohibition on scalarization, both boxed in Step 211
a_rows_sample.statement: Step 211 Section 211.6 states Assurance(I_global)<=min{Assurance(I_1),Assurance(I_2),...}; Step 211 Section 211.17 boxes 'Vector assurance is preferable to premature scalarization.' min over a set requires a total order on the codomain, but Section 211.9 makes assurance a 6-vector (only partially ordered), so evaluating min requires exactly the scalarization Section 211.17 forbids -- the two boxed positions of one file are mutually exclusive. Aggravated by Section 211.4's ordinal-only assurance-adjacent quantities and by Section 211.17's own use of cardinal values A_s=1, A_p=0, 0.83. Severity HIGH.

a_rows_sample.anchor: CONTRADICTION #7 — Step 212 builds ownership diagnostics and deletes the ownership data needed to run them
a_rows_sample.statement: Step 212 Section 212.15 boxes 'Ownerless Invariants' as a finding to explicitly search for (I exists but Owner(I)=empty set), yet Step 212 Section 212.4's register reprints all fifteen invariants with the Owner column removed (columns reduced to ID|Property|Target), and no search for ownerless invariants is performed anywhere in the file. Step 210's deleted Owner column contained exactly the data Sections 212.15/212.16 are designed to interrogate: 7 of 15 rows owned by a layer or pattern (effectively ownerless), 5 of 15 slash-shared. Severity HIGH.

a_rows_sample.anchor: CONTRADICTION #8 — F/D/P/U mandated in Step 213, applied zero times across Steps 213-215
a_rows_sample.statement: Step 213 Section 213.26 mandates that every important statement during reconstruction carry an [F]/[D]/[P]/[U] label ('our editorial control system'). Zero of the hundreds of statements in the three files that mandate the labels carry one, even though Section 213.26 explicitly scopes the requirement to these reconstruction documents themselves. b_rows_sample.anchor: MATCH VERDICT: 6 of 8 agenda items delivered; 2 named and NOT delivered
b_rows_sample.statement: Probe (a): Step 207's tail agenda for Step 208 lists eight items (contract composition, information preservation, semantic loss, version compatibility, monotonicity, contradiction, uncertainty propagation, provenance preservation) under the question 'can a chain of individually valid transformations produce an invalid or misleading conclusion?'. Step 208 delivers 6 of 8: version compatibility is NOT delivered (Version appears only as a tuple field; no compatibility relation between contract versions is defined) and uncertainty propagation is NOT delivered (Section 208.14 shows uncertainty being lost, but no composition rule for uncertainty through C_2 o C_1 is given, and the word 'propagation' never occurs in Step 208). b_rows_sample.anchor: Answered from scratch: zero citations to Steps 048/050/058
b_rows_sample.statement: Probe (b): machine grep of Step 208 (and all 8 in-scope files) for the prior corpus's answers to the same headline question -- Step 048's boxed 'LocalCorrectness ⇏ GlobalCorrectness', Step 058's boxed 'CorrectContexts ⇏ CorrectComposition', and Step 050's Attack 5 ('semantic collision', PASS) -- finds zero matches anywhere in the band. Step 208 Section 208.13 re-derives the same proposition in new notation ('locally valid but globally invalid'), so the same proposition is now boxed four times in the corpus in four notations with zero cross-reference; under LATER != SUPERSEDING, Step 208 does not supersede 048 or 058, it duplicates them without knowing they exist. Step 208's Section 208.22 (contradiction propagation) and Section 208.15 (RichEvidence -> SimpleBoolean) likewise re-derive the ground of Step 050's Attack 2 and Attack 5 respectively, also uncited.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Further arithmetic checks: 0.87>=0.80 correct; 0.91+/-0.08 within range at 1 sigma but 2-sigma bound exceeds 1; ratio checks disclaimed
b_rows_sample.statement: Additional independently-verified arithmetic in the band: Step 209 Section 209.15's 0.87 >= 0.80 evaluates to True (correct). Step 208 Section 208.14 / Step 210 Section 210.12's 0.91 +/- 0.08 gives [0.83, 0.99], within [0,1] at 1-sigma, but at 2-sigma the upper bound is 1.07 > 1 -- out of range for a quantity called 'confidence', though the corpus never commits this specific error since the interval's coverage level is left unlabelled. b_rows_sample.statement: Step 208 ('Semantic Contract Algebra') treats a DDD context contract as an information-preserving projection and defines: semantic sufficiency S_B ⊆ I(C(A)) relative to a receiving context's task; minimal sufficient contract; semantic projection pi; semantic loss L(C) = I_required - I_preserved; semantic integrity SI(C,B); the anti-pattern 'Booleanization' (collapsing rich epistemic state into a Boolean); contract temporal validity C(t); provenance composition P(G)=P(A)∪P(E); the KnowledgeArtifact 6-tuple (Content, Meaning, Provenance, Validity, Version, EpistemicStatus); the Data->Information->Evidence->Assessment->KnowledgeClaim ladder; Proposition as a first-class object; and a four-layer architecture split (Epistemic/Normative/Decisional/Operational).

b_rows_sample.anchor: PREVIOUS DEPENDENCY (cited BY NUMBER). 1 — We continue from Step 207.
b_rows_sample.statement: Step 208 cites exactly one prior step by number (Step 207, 'we continue from...') and nothing else -- not Steps 048, 058, 050, or 082. Later response in scope: Step 208's SI non-compositionality (Section 208.12) is restated in Step 211 Section 211.5 as 'Component correctness ⇏ System correctness'; Step 208's L(C) (Section 208.10) reappears in Step 212 Section 212.19 as L(C)=InformationBefore(C)-InformationAfter(C) without Step 208's own caveat; Step 208's Section 208.14 example reappears in substance, uncredited, in Step 212 Section 212.20.

b_rows_sample.anchor: EVOLUTION VERDICT: PARTIALLY_RESOLVES / REVIVES; DEFINITION VERDICT: PARTIALLY_CLEAR
b_rows_sample.statement: Step 208 resolves 6 of 8 of Step 207's agenda items and, unknowingly, revives already-boxed results from Steps 048 and 058. Definitionally: Booleanization, Suff(C,B,Task), semantic projection, and the four-layer split are CLEAR. The information measure I(.) is NOT DEFINED -- Section 208.3 writes an ordinal comparison I(A)<I(E) and Section 208.10 writes a difference L(C)=I_required-I_preserved while itself stating 'we should not treat this as a literal numeric quantity until we define an information measure' -- the measure is never defined and the operations are performed anyway. S_B ('the information necessary to perform its legitimate responsibility') is AMBIGUOUS because 'legitimate' is never defined, so S_B cannot be constructed for any concrete B.

b_rows_sample.anchor: FIRST INVALID INFERENCE: Section 208.3 (compounded at 208.10); SECOND DEFECT: Section 208.25's provenance equation
b_rows_sample.statement: DERIVATION VERDICT PARTIALLY_VALID. I(A)<I(E) presupposes a total order on information content; I_required-I_preserved presupposes an interval scale; neither is established (Section 208.10 explicitly declines to establish one, then uses the operations anyway) -- every downstream claim quantifying loss is conditional on repairing this. Second defect: P(G)=P(A)∪P(E), boxed as 'provenance must be closed under semantic transformation,' is either vacuous (if closure holds, P(A)∪P(E)=P(A)) or self-refuting (if it does not, provenance is not closed); it also excludes any provenance contributed by the governance act itself, directly conflicting with Step 209 Section 209.4's Final(D) ⇒ DecisionBasis(D) ∧ Authority(D) (see Contradiction #2).

b_rows_sample.anchor: COMPUTABILITY: nothing in Step 208 reaches CONSTRUCTIBLE; TEST VERDICT: NOT_EXECUTED
b_rows_sample.statement: Computability ladder for Step 208's objects: Booleanization is DEFINED; Semantic Sufficiency S_B⊆I(C(A)) is DEFINED but not INPUTS_KNOWN (both S_B and I uninstantiated); L(C) is DEFINED but explicitly barred from COMPUTABLE by its own Section 208.10; the Contract Safety theorem (Section 208.37) is DEFINED but not DERIVED. Nothing in the file reaches CONSTRUCTIBLE. Test verdict NOT_EXECUTED (0 tests specified, 0 run); the nine review questions in Section 208.38 are a checklist, not tests.

b_rows_sample.anchor: STATISTICAL VERDICT: STRONG on framing, WEAK on inference; MEASUREMENT VERDICT: FAILS on the information measure
b_rows_sample.statement: Statistically, Section 208.6's sufficient-statistic analogy is immediately and correctly fenced ('this is an analogy, not a claim that DDD contracts are literally sufficient statistics') but left un-cashed (no Fisher-Neyman factorization or formal criterion transposed), and Section 208.23's handling of conflicting estimates is sound but uncited against prior statistical steps (025N, 082). Measurement-wise: I(.) has no declared scale type yet is compared (<) and subtracted (-) -- arithmetic NOT justified; result=0.91 in one block silently becomes confidence=0.91 in the very next (unjustified type conversion between a point estimate and a degree of belief); uncertainty=0.08 is silently converted into a symmetric +/-0.08 interval half-width in Step 210 Section 210.12, presupposing an unstated symmetric error distribution and coverage level; epistemic strength S(x) is compared with > (Section 208.9 forward) while Step 209 Section 209.21 later explicitly retracts any universal total ordering on the same kind of quantity.

b_rows_sample.anchor: DDD VERDICT: STRONG — the best DDD content in the band; UBIQUITOUS-LANGUAGE: Evidence != Claim boxed, then violated two files later
b_rows_sample.statement: Step 208's sufficiency-relative-to-responsibility (Section 208.4) is a correct, non-obvious Published-Language/conformist-boundary formulation; S_B ⊆ I(C(A)) ≪ I(A) (Section 208.5) is precisely the anti-Shared-Kernel constraint; Booleanization (Section 208.16) is a genuinely useful named anti-pattern; the four-layer split (Section 208.36) is a defensible strategic decomposition -- but none of it is mapped to Step 206's bounded contexts or Step 207's actual context contracts. Section 208.28 rules 'we should not collapse [Data/Information/Evidence/Assessment/KnowledgeClaim] into one generic object called Knowledge' -- a ruling violated two files later (Contradiction #1). Section 208.30 promotes Proposition to a first-class term; Section 208.29 boxes Evidence != Claim but gives it no owning context ('term without an owner').

b_rows_sample.anchor: ASSUMPTIONS / HIDDEN ASSUMPTIONS; UNDEFINED SYMBOLS in Step 208
b_rows_sample.statement: Stated assumptions: a contract is total and deterministic; information is set-like so subset applies; S_B is knowable a priori. Hidden assumptions: that an information measure exists at all (Section 208.10 defers it and nothing in the band supplies one); that provenance sets are finite and mergeable (required by P(A)∪P(E), never stated); that Valid(C) (Section 208.2) and SI(C,B) (Section 208.12) are different predicates, though the text slides between them; that 'legitimate responsibility' (Section 208.4) is externally given, smuggling the governance model into the definition of sufficiency. Undefined symbols: I(.) (deferred), S_B (depends on undefined 'legitimate'), T_1, A_I/G_I/D_I, Preserve(.), RequiredProvenance(R_C), Knowledge(E).

b_rows_sample.statement: Survives: Booleanization as a named anti-pattern; Suff(C,B,Task) (purpose-relative sufficiency); the four-layer split; Evidence != Claim; probability-of-proposition != truth-value-of-proposition; the explicit refusal to claim contracts are sufficient statistics; non-monotonicity as a requirement; the boxed claim 'the objective is not zero information loss, the objective is zero loss of relevant meaning' (the band's clearest and most durable architectural statement).
